articles.title: Eight-year-old undergoes endoscopic treatment for rare swallowing disorder
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The child, diagnosed with Type II achalasia, underwent a minimally invasive procedure at Rela Hospital in Chennai

An eight-year-old boy diagnosed with Type II achalasia – a rare disorder that affects the ability to swallow food and liquids – has undergone a Perora-l Endoscopic Myotomy (POEM) procedure at Rela Hospital.

Achalasia affects the nerves controlling the muscles of the oesophagus, causing the lower oesophageal sphincter – a muscular valve connecting the food pipe to the stomach – to remain abnormally tight. This prevents food and liquids from passing normally into the stomach. The condition is estimated to affect 0.1 to 0.18 children per 100,000 annually.

The child had progressively worsening difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. Following the procedure, he was able to resume consuming clear liquids and subsequently, a soft diet, within 24 hours.

POEM involves passing an endoscope through the mouth and creating a small tunnel within the oesophageal wall to reach and divide the muscle fibres causing the obstruction. Unlike conventional surgery, the procedure does not require external incisions or stitches.

S.N.K. Chenduran, senior consultant and endoscopic surgeon, Department of Medical Gastroenterology, performed the procedure, which took about 50 minutes. He said performing POEM in children required particular precision because of the smaller dimensions of the oesophagus and the delicate tissues.

Dinesh Jothimani, director, Hepatology and Medical Gastroenterology, said persistent swallowing difficulties, regurgitation, vomiting, and unexplained weight loss in children warranted medical evaluation.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.
• The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Karnataka to write to Prime Minister asking for inclusion of enhanced quota in Ninth Schedule
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: After the High Court of Karnataka quashed the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, the State government will write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to include the enhanced reservation for SCs and STs in the 9th Schedule of the Constitution

After the High Court of Karnataka quashed the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, the State government will write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to include the enhanced reservation for SCs and STs in the 9th Schedule of the Constitution.

“A letter will be sent to the Prime Minister in this regard. If a meeting with the Prime Minister is possible, this matter will be discussed,” Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar told presspersons after chairing the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development Council meeting on Thursday.
“The matter came up for discussion during a meeting of legislators and Ministers from the SC and ST communities,” said the Chief Minister.

On the Special Leave Petition filed in the Supreme Court against the Karnataka High Court order, he said the responsibility of deciding who should argue on behalf of the State in this legal battle and monitoring the case has been given to Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara, Ministers Satish Jarkiholi, and K.H. Muniyappa. “We are confident of getting justice in the Supreme Court,” he said.

He also said that a vision group would be constituted to decide on the contours of new programmes to be implemented for the welfare of the communities. The Chief Minister said that a Cabinet sub-committee has been formed under the leadership of Mr. Parameshwara and preparations are under way to implement the programmes announced in the party manifesto.

“Our leaders have pointed out that certain schemes are overlapping. It has been decided to get a social audit conducted by reputed institutions to study the impact of grants provided through SCSP/ TSP programmes,” he said.

Following suggestions by legislators and Ministers from these communities on new schemes and ideas at a meeting with the Chief Minister on Thursday, deliberations will be held under the chairmanship of Mr. Parameshwara for two days. Discussions will be held with the Finance Department on whether any changes can be made before submitting a report to the government.

“It is our government’s intention that ₹44,631 crore allocated for SCSP/ TSP scheme should reach the beneficiaries. The government has also decided to hold a convention of SCs and STs to inform people about the promises we made before the elections and what has been fulfilled. The leaders will decide on the venue,” Mr. Shivakumar said.

The State government will also write to the Centre, requesting release of ₹1,937 crore that is pending for 2025-2026 under Centrally-sponsored schemes. Of the total Central share of ₹3,497 crore, the State has received ₹1,560 crore. While the Centre did not release grants, the State had also not released grants, resulting in a setback in implementation of several schemes. The Finance Department has now been asked to release the grants irrespective of grants received from the Centre.

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Thursday said that the government has instructed the Education Department to provide new look to hostels and school uniforms. “We implement these from next year. Let the government school children wear good uniforms just like those in private schools. If that requires a little extra money, we will provide it,” he said.

articles.title: Private passenger ship service between Beypore and Lakshadweep soon
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As part of the trial, the ship, capable of accommodating 250 passengers, anchored safely at the port wharf. Maiden commercial run anticipated in November
A private passenger ship service between Beypore and Lakshadweep is set to commence operations following the arrival of the vessel Theja at the Beypore port on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The initiative aims to restore maritime connectivity that has faced prolonged interruptions. As part of the trial, the ship, capable of accommodating 250 passengers, anchored safely at the port wharf in the morning. Official clearance procedures and regulatory approvals are in progress, with the maiden commercial run anticipated this month.

According to port officials, the initiative aligns with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan’s ‘Mission Samudra’ development framework, which seeks to leverage Keralam’s extensive coastline and port infrastructure to catalyse new economic and commercial prospects. Representatives of the operating company had recently met the Chief Minister to brief him about the project’s progress and strategic importance, they said.

Stakeholders noted that beyond streamlining passenger transit, the service would give a fresh momentum for maritime tourism at the historically significant Beypore port, while strengthening socio-economic and commercial ties between Keralam and the archipelago.

articles.title: Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Microsoft said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”; it determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks

A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday (November 12, 2026), with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps.

Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.
Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.
Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications.

In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”

Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.
Microsoft did not immediately provide more information around what might be causing that failure, but added that it was testing a fix.
“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X.
Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

articles.title: India and U.K. are turning climate ambition into action
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The U.K.-India climate partnership shows what delivery can look like in practice. Both our countries recognise that the shift to cleaner growth is not separate from the pursuit of prosperity

Next week, Mumbai will become the stage for one of the world’s boldest climate ideas. The largest ever Earthshot Prize edition will bring together innovators, investors, businesses, policymakers and young people to turn environmental solutions into impact at scale. Five winners will each receive £1 million to accelerate their work.

It all began with a simple but powerful idea: that human ingenuity, innovation and optimism can help repair our planet. Founded by His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales, The Earthshot Prize seeks solutions capable of delivering transformative environmental impact. Since the Prize was launched in 2020, India has produced more Earthshot finalists and winners than any other country (nine finalists including four winners). This year two of the 15 finalists are based in India. As the Prize arrives in Mumbai, India’s growing influence in clean growth and climate innovation will be on full display.

Science, Space & Environment Report: India and U.K. are turning climate ambition into action. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Sukhbir Badal likely to meet Amit Shah on November 13, SAD-BJP alliance may be announced this month
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: SAD sources said that Mr. Badal is likely to leave for New Delhi after his rally at Raikot to meet Mr. Shah, with talks on seat sharing and finalising the alliance on the agenda

After months of speculation over a possible re-alliance between the old partners Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly election, a likely meeting between SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and Union Home Minister Amit Shah on November 13 is being viewed as a move toward sealing the alliance.

SAD sources said that Mr. Badal is expected to leave for New Delhi in the second half of the day, after his rally at Raikot, to meet Mr. Shah. It is expected that the talks surrounding the seat sharing and finalisation of the alliance for the Punjab election would be on the agenda. Even as leaders from both parties remained tight-lipped about the deliberations, the sources indicated that the announcement about the alliance could be made within November.

In August this year, Mr. Badal had met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, where the possibility of renewing the alliance was discussed. A SAD source had confirmed that, with discussions underway, an alliance could materialise.

The SAD and the BJP were alliance partners since the late 1990s, however, amid the controversy over the Centre’s agriculture sector laws, which were later repealed, the SAD — one of the BJP’s oldest alliance partners — decided to break away from the NDA coalition in 2020.

articles.title: Bomb threat emails target BMC, Pune civic body, PNB branches; searches find nothing suspicious
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “A hoax bomb threat email was received at the BMC office and PNB Bank this morning. Nothing suspicious was found. Further legal process is ongoing,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 2) Raghasudha R. said

Bomb threat emails targeting civic offices in Mumbai and Pune, along with Punjab National Bank (PNB) branches in Mumbai, triggered security checks on Thursday (November 12, 2026). Police and bomb squad personnel searched the premises but found nothing suspicious.

According to police, threat emails were received at a Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) office and PNB branches in Zaveri Bazar and Marine Lines, claiming that explosives had been planted on the premises.
Local police and bomb detection and disposal squad personnel rushed to the locations and conducted searches following the alerts.

“A hoax bomb threat email was received at the BMC office and PNB Bank this morning. Nothing suspicious was found. Further legal process is ongoing,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 2) Raghasudha R. said.
The Mumbai Mayor’s office also received a bomb threat via email, prompting police and bomb squad personnel to reach the premises and initiate an investigation.

The threatening email also warned of explosions at multiple locations across Mumbai, including the airport and actor Amitabh Bachchan’s residence. According to sources, the email contained references to Khalistan and inflammatory remarks about the 1984 anti-Sikh violence.
Police are examining the technical trail of the emails, including the sender’s address and IP details, to trace their origin.

Meanwhile, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) received a bomb threat on its official email address on Thursday. The sender claimed that an explosive device had been planted inside the civic body’s building and threatened to detonate it.
Fire brigade and bomb squad personnel rushed to the PMC premises and conducted a search. However, no suspicious objects were found.

articles.title: TNPDCL seeks nod to procure 3,000 MW
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum
The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) has increased the quantum of its proposed power procurement from 1,500 megawatt (MW) to 3,000 MW through a medium-term tender agreement.
The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum.

A senior TNPDCL official said amid a power demand of about 19,000 MW and an extended summer, it has been proposed to buy 3,000 MW of round-the-clock (RTC) power for five years, under the Finance, Operate and Own guidelines.

TNERC will take up the application for medium-term power purchase, along with requests for deviation from the guidelines and permission to float a short-term tender to procure RTC and peak-hour power for the period from February to July next year.

TNPDCL submitted in its application that the annual power demand had increased to 22,000 MW from an average of 18,000 MW due to various factors, including changes in weather pattern, increasing migrant population, and a surge in electric vehicle sales, with the State set to face an energy shortage of 7,000 MW by 2029-30.
The senior official said the long-term power purchase agreements signed for a quantum of 2,830 MW would expire by 2028-29, prompting new procurement plans.
The estimated cost of the medium-term procurement is around ₹5.50 per kilo watt per hour, with the annual expenditure pegged at ₹6,150 crore.
When the State faced a power shortage this October, TNPDCL had to purchase power at a cost of ₹30 per unit to bridge the peak-hour gap.

articles.title: Twin cyclone leave livelihoods in tatters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cyclones, Arnab and Murasu, which hit the Andhra Pradesh coastline within a span of a week, delivered a severe blow to the fisherfolk communities, coconut and casuarina growers in West Godavari and Konaseema districts, many of whom may have to look for alternative livelihoods for two to three years, writes Nellore Sravani

For generations, coconut trees have been more than just crops for the people in the coastal districts of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, and West Godavari. They have been their livelihood. However, two cyclones that hit the coastal district of Andhra Pradesh within the span of a week have left the coconut growers, farmers and fishing communities in the region staring down the barrel as thousands of coconut trees were flattened, lakhs of acres of paddy fields were wiped out, and dozens of boats became dysfunctional. Konaseema district has witnessed the swath of destruction, with over 73,500 coconut trees uprooted and paddy destroyed across 1,18,109 acres, leaving around 88,000 farmers in tatters. Meanwhile, in West Godavari district, 27,397 coconut trees were destroyed, affecting more than 5,000 small and marginal growers.

Andhra Pradesh was ravaged by two cyclones between October 28 and November 3. One was a ‘Very Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) Arnab and the other, a ‘Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (SCS) Murasu, leaving the districts of West Godavari, Konaseema, and Bapatla in ruins, while Guntur, East Godavari and Palnadu were also affected, according to the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority. Coastal areas in two districts of West Godavari and Konaseema were ravaged by violent gales of around 150 kmph at the time of Arnab’s landfall on October 28 and 29, and suffered once again when extremely heavy rainfall pounded the districts on November 3 and 4 after Murasu made landfall near Ongole.

• For generations, coconut trees have been more than just crops for the people in the coastal districts of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, and West Godavari. They have been their livelihood. However, two cyclones that hit the coastal district of Andhra Pradesh within the span of a week have left the coconut growers, farmers and fishing communities in the region staring down the barrel as thousands of coconut trees were flattened, lakhs of acres of paddy fields were wiped out, and dozens of boats became dysfunctional. Konaseema district has witnessed the swath of destruction, with over 73,500 coconut trees uprooted and paddy destroyed across 1,18,109 acres, leaving around 88,000 farmers in tatters. Meanwhile, in West Godavari district, 27,397 coconut trees were destroyed, affecting more than 5,000 small and marginal growers.
• Andhra Pradesh was ravaged by two cyclones between October 28 and November 3. One was a ‘Very Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) Arnab and the other, a ‘Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (SCS) Murasu, leaving the districts of West Godavari, Konaseema, and Bapatla in ruins, while Guntur, East Godavari and Palnadu were also affected, according to the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority. Coastal areas in two districts of West Godavari and Konaseema were ravaged by violent gales of around 150 kmph at the time of Arnab’s landfall on October 28 and 29, and suffered once again when extremely heavy rainfall pounded the districts on November 3 and 4 after Murasu made landfall near Ongole.

articles.title: Amidst simmering tensions, India-Bangladesh consular dialogue postponed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This would have been the fifth such consular dialogue and the first after the August 2024 uprising; postponement due to tensions over former PM Hasina’s plan to return to Bangladesh next month

Days after Bangladesh’s deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested Dhaka for a new passport and national identity card, the fifth India-Bangladesh consular dialogue that was scheduled to take place on November 17 and 18 has been postponed, a diplomatic source has confirmed.

The source indicated that the postponement of the dialogue was mainly on account of growing tensions in the bilateral relationship caused by Ms. Hasina’s announcement that she will return to Bangladesh next month.

The planned consular dialogue would have been the first such meeting between the two sides in more than two years. The last such dialogue was held in New Delhi on May 29, 2024, just over two months before the Hasina government fell in a youth-led uprising in Dhaka.

The consular dialogue was scheduled to be held in Dhaka at the level of Director Generals of the Foreign Ministries of both countries. The planned agenda included issues of border management, visa procedures, and the repatriation of citizens detained on both sides. The number of Indian visas issued was drastically reduced when tensions broke out in August 2024. According to sources, India has gradually increased the number of visas issued to travellers from Bangladesh in recent months, especially after the election of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in February this year.

The two countries started a consular dialogue in 2017 to “strengthen people-to-people contacts by having a regular channel of communication on consular, visa, and mutual legal assistance cooperation matters between India and Bangladesh.” Four rounds of consular dialogues were held during the rule of the Awami League in Dhaka. As per the Ministry of External Affairs, the fourth round held in May 2024 discussed issues like “visa matters, repatriation, Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty cases etc.”

Attempts at normalising the India-Bangladesh relationship in recent months have been hindered by Ms. Hasina’s presence in India, where she took refuge on August 5, 2024. On November 9 this year, a London-based legal firm representing Ms. Hasina wrote to the High Commission of Bangladesh in New Delhi requesting a new passport and the national ID card. “In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client,” said the letter sent by the law firm Matrix Chambers.

However, the Acting Foreign Minister of Bangladesh Humayun Kabir responded to this development by telling journalists that Bangladesh would not issue a passport to Ms. Hasina. Instead, he said, Dhaka would seek Ms. Hasina’s extradition under an “acceptable prisoner exchange process”, adding that such a handover would have to be conducted carefully and under proper surveillance.

articles.title: Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police sanctions the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; CCS clears 26 new roads as part of ICBR-III

Amid continuing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh since late July, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) has sanctioned the construction of new border infrastructure in the northeastern State, a senior government official told The Hindu .

Earlier, in February, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) had cleared the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) project. Under the scheme, as many as 26 roads are to be constructed along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, another government official said. The Union Government has not yet officially announced the ICBR-III project or publicly disclosed these details.
This is only the second time after the 2020 Galwan clashes in eastern Ladakh that a critical road infrastructure project has been sanctioned along the border with China.

The first phase of the ICBR was initiated in 2005 when it was decided that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) would construct 27 priority roads with a total length of 608 km along the border with China.

The second phase of the ICBR, comprising 32 roads with a total length of 683 km, was approved on September 21, 2020, just months after 20 Indian soldiers were killed in violent clashes with the Chinese People’s Liberation Army in eastern Ladakh.

Since September, the ITBP has authorised the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Upper Subansiri and Kurung Kumey districts, covering the areas bordering China in Arunachal Pradesh.

The project clearance came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit from September 11 to 13 in New Delhi, which was attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping. A government statement after the meeting said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.

In December 2020, the MHA had approved construction of 18 pedestrian tracks, including foot suspension bridges, log bridges, and staging camps, measuring a total length of 598.27 km in the border areas of Arunachal Pradesh.
On October 22 this year, former ITBP Director-General Shatrujeet Kapur mentioned that the “face-off” with Chinese troops “continues at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh.”

Addressing the Himveer Samman Samaroah at the Central Training College at Alwar in Rajasthan, Mr. Kapur said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-offs happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues. Our Shaurya commandos played an exemplary role in this.”

articles.title: U.S., Ukraine say Europe to join Russia talks as Putin sticks to hardline stance
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday (November 12, 2026) Europe would join the next round of talks with Russia, as Vladimir Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on its hardline demands to end almost five years of war.

In a packed day of shuttle diplomacy following negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Mr. Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Mr. Zelenskyy in Dublin.

As they spoke to journalists on the tarmac of a military airbase in Ireland, the main piece of progress touted by the Ukrainian leader and U.S. President Donald Trump's representative was that European negotiators would be at the table for future talks.
Mr. Zelenskyy said Europeans will take part rather than remain "separately" on the sidelines as they were in Abu Dhabi, insisting: "They will have a voice".
Mr. Kushner later reiterated the sentiment in a post on X, writing: "Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners."
"Significant differences remain, but we are encouraged by the progress made," he posted, adding that the schedule and details on the negotiating track would be released "shortly".
An EU official told AFP representatives of five European capitals as well as the European Commission that the U.S. envoys, and that a new multilateral meeting "will be fixed soon".
The Kremlin did not confirm Mr. Putin had agreed to include Europe in future talks, which Kyiv and its allies have long been seeking.

Instead, the Russian leader had earlier told the U.S. duo he would not water down demands to control parts of Ukraine that Russia claims to have annexed and ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine -- a deployment he said would be a "continuation of war".
As the United States has pushed for Europe to be allowed at the table, Moscow has sought to reframe talks as part of a wider discussion about European security.

articles.title: TVK faces criticism from Congress over law and order in Tamil Nadu, allegations against Kallakurichi MLA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A senior Congress leader said the TVK-led government should form a co-ordination committee to steer the State Government and make decision-making accountable

Despite being one of its strongest allies, senior leaders of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, including Sivaganga MP Karti P. Chidambaram, Karur MP S. Jothimani, and Mayiladuthurai MP R. Sudha have been scathing in criticising the TVK-led government over the recent spate of “revenge” murders, deterioration of law and order in the State and demanded action against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh for his allegedly objectionable message to the District Collector .

While TNCC president B. Manickam Tagore restated State School Education Minister Rajmohan’s response (that murder cases during TVK government should be compared with the same last year), urging the State government to provide crime data periodically to counter DMK’s “propaganda,” Mr. Karti was much more direct in his criticism of the School Education Minister.

Responding to Mr. Rajmohan’s defence on X, Mr. Karti said, “This is classic whataboutery by Minister, the fact is that murders, particularly planned revenge killings are taking place, this is alarming & worrisome. Degenerate criminal behaviour is rising in society. It’s incumbent upon the government to have a visible show of force, increase patrolling & random ID checks and mandate all those in K.D. lists report to the designated police station daily. Statistics that these murders happened previously is no solace to the citizenry.”
Lok Sabha MPs Ms. Jothimani and Ms. Sudha called for action against TVK Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh for allegedly sending an objectionable message to Kallakurichi’s Collector.
After criticising the decision to disband the high-level committee on Union-State relations , Ms. Jothimani also underlined the need to ensure safe working spaces for women.

“Reports are circulating on social media that a TVK MLA allegedly sent obscene text messages to the Kallakurichi District Collector and behaved inappropriately when he went to meet her in person. The Kallakurichi District Collector is said to have filed a formal complaint about this. If these social media reports are true, a proper investigation must be conducted and strict action taken. No matter how high a woman rises through her knowledge, skills and hard work, we simply cannot move beyond this kind of deplorable mindset that ultimately sees her as nothing more than a woman and a body,” she said.

Ms. Sudha urged the Chief Minister to investigate the allegation against the MLA. “It is unacceptable that the District Collector, a woman serving in this role, has been placed in such a morally distressing situation while ensuring the safety of people from all walks of life in the district,” she said.

articles.title: Centre gives another extension to panel probing 2023 Manipur violence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the seventh extension for the Commission; the Commission asked to submit the report “as soon as possible but not later than the 20 May, 2027.”

The Centre has given another six-month extension, till May 20 next year , to a Commission of Inquiry to submit its report on the probe into the 2023 Manipur violence that claimed more than 260 lives, a government notification said.

The three-member panel, now headed by former Supreme Court judge Balbir Singh Chauhan, was formed on June 4, 2023, in the aftermath of the ethnic violence that broke out in the northeastern State in May that year.
It was initially headed by former Gauhati High Court chief justice Ajai Lamba, who resigned with effect from February 28. Justice Chauhan took charge on March 1.
According to the notification published in the gazette, the Commission shall submit its report to the Centre “as soon as possible but not later than the 20 May, 2027.”

The panel is probing the sequence of events and facts relating to the ethnic violence that broke out in the State on May 3, 2023, after a “Tribal Solidarity March” was organised in the hill districts.
The protest was held against the Meitei community’s demand for Scheduled Tribe (ST) status. The ensuing violence claimed more than 260 lives.
The violence was preceded by earlier tensions over the eviction of Kuki villagers from reserve forest land, leading to a series of smaller agitations.
The Centre constituted the commission on the recommendation of the Manipur government, citing the necessity of an inquiry into a matter of public importance.
The scope of the inquiry includes ascertaining whether there were any lapses or dereliction of duty on the part of any of the authorities or individuals responsible.

The Commission is also assessing the adequacy of the administrative measures taken to prevent and deal with the violence and riots. It is looking into the complaints or allegations submitted by any individual or association.

articles.title: The PM’s political career will be over if we were to debate: Rahul Gandhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister taps my phone, the Opposition leader says; he is no longer attacking me, Congress leader adds, as there is ‘a little fear’ in his mind

Accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi of tapping his phone, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday (November 13, 2026) dared Mr. Modi to debate him on who was an anti-national.
The Prime Minister’s “political career will be over” if he accepted the invitation to debate as he (Mr. Gandhi) had “evidence” against Mr. Modi on his phone, the Congress leader claimed.

“The Prime Minister’s political career will be over if he comes and debates with me. He knows that and I know that. He keeps calling me anti-national. I want to show the nation exactly who is anti-national, exactly who is controlled by whom and since when, and he knows the truth of that,” the Congress leader said in a video on his Instagram and X handles.

Replying to a question during an ‘Ask Me’ session on Instagram on why he was insisting on a public debate when the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has said the exchange could take place in Parliament, Mr. Gandhi said he was not allowed to speak in the House and even his microphone was switched off.

“You did not let me talk on the Farm Bills, vote chori (theft), SIR (Special Intensive Revision), China, on [General] Naravane’s book, [Jeffrey] Epstein. I want a one-on-one debate. I don’t want a debate entailing long speeches,” Mr. Gandhi said, adding, “I want that Narendra Modi makes allegations against me and I do the same to him. He can come. There will be a table. On one side, there will be Narendra Modi ji , and on the other side, it will be me.”
The Opposition leader suggested that business tycoon Gautam Adani or Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat could become the judge for the debate.
“But I guarantee that the Prime Minister will not remain the PM after a one-on-one debate with me,” he claimed.

“The proof is here,” Mr. Gandhi said in response to another question on what proof he had to back his allegations. “The Prime Minister knows it because he taps my phone. The moment he comes for the debate, one-on-one debate, everybody will know who is controlled by foreign powers, who is an anti-national, and since when he has been an anti-national, and lots of other details are on my phone,” he added.

“Notice something: there is a little fear in his (Modi’s) mind because he is no longer commenting about me; he is no longer attacking me; he is being very, very careful. There is a reason for it, guys,” Mr. Gandhi said.
The Opposition leader also took a swipe at the Prime Minister over his Deepavali milan (gathering) programme at the BJP headquarters with representatives of the media.

articles.title: DMK urges Tamil Nadu DGP to act against TVK MLA for sending ‘obscene messages’ to Kallakurichi Collector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The MLA had denied sending any such message to the collector; DMK chief Stalin said CM Vijay should take ‘real action’ against erring MLAs instead of delivering ‘punch dialogues’

DMK president M.K. Stalin on Thursday (November 12, 2026) said that “delivering punch dialogues” would not solve any problem and that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should take “real action” against Deputy Speaker M. Ravishankar for allegedly undermining the dignity of the Assembly and ruling party MLA Arul Vignesh for allegedly sending an inappropriate message to the Kallakurichi District Collector.

articles.title: Madras High Court refuses to reject election plea against Udhayanidhi’s win from Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice G. Arul Murugan dismisses two applications filed by the Leader of the Opposition and decides to proceed with the trial

The Madras High Court on Friday (November 13, 2026) refused to reject an election petition filed by P. Milany of Theni district, challenging the victory of Leader of the Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin from the Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni Assembly constituency in the 2026 general elections.

Justice G. Arul Murugan dismissed two applications filed by the LoP with a plea to reject the election petition and strike off substantial pleadings made by the election petitioner. The judge decided to proceed with the trial and directed the applicant to file his reply statement by December 11, 2026.

The LoP had urged the court to reject the election petition on multiple grounds, including the supposed delay in filing the election petition within the statutory limitation period of 45 days from the date of declaration of results. However, the judge refused to accept the arguments advanced by the applicant.

The applicant was declared elected after securing 62,992 votes, as against his nearest rival candidate D. Selvam of the TVK, who had garnered 55,852 votes. However, the election petition was filed by another candidate, Mr. Milany, who had contested from the constituency as an Independent and secured 30 votes.

Highlighting that the result of the election was declared on May 4, 2026, the LoP claimed that the election petition challenging his victory ought to have been filed on or before June 17, 2026. Since the present petition had been filed on June 18, 2026, he argued that it was barred by limitation.

The applicant’s contention was that the day of declaration of results must not be excluded while calculating the limitation period of 45 days prescribed under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, since the legal provision uses the term “from the date of election of the returned candidate.”
His counsel had contended that the principle of excluding the first day, under the General Clauses Act of 1897, for the purpose of calculating limitation period would not apply to election petitions.

“Normally, Your Lordship knows that if a judgment is pronounced today, the limitation would begin only from the next day. But the 1951 Act is a special legislation and it specifically states that an election petition must be presented within 45 days from the date of the election of the returned candidate,” the counsel had argued.

He also claimed the Election Commission of India had also sent a communication to the Registrar General of the High Court confirming that the election petitions with respect to the 2026 general elections must be filed in the High Court on or before June 17, 2026.

articles.title: 12 people die in bus-truck collision in Assam's Kaziranga
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accident occurred at Rangajan near Hathikuli Tea Estate in Kohora range on National Highway 715 when the passenger vehicle collided with the truck, a senior officer said
Twelve people died in a head-on collision between a minibus and a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam on Friday (November 13, 2026), police said.
The accident occurred at Rangajan near Hathikuli Tea Estate in Kohora range on National Highway 715 when the passenger vehicle collided with the truck, a senior officer said.

"We have got a preliminary report that at least seven people were killed in the accident. We are all at the spot, and bodies are being retrieved from the bus, so the number of deaths is likely to rise," Golaghat Senior Superintendent of Police Swapnaneel Deka told PTI .
Later, five more succumbed to their injuries, another officer said.
The exact number of people travelling in the bus is not immediately known, the police said.
Assam Panchayat and Rural Development Minister Atul Bora, who is also the local MLA, reached the site immediately and was supervising the relief and rescue operations.
The injured people were taken to the Kohora Model Hospital, and most of the critically injured were referred to the Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.

"The bus was running at very high speed, violating restrictions imposed near the park. We think that the accident took place when the driver of the minibus lost control, and the vehicle collided with the container truck," he added.

Twelve people died in a head-on collision between a minibus and a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam on Friday (November 13, 2026), police said.

The accident occurred at Rangajan near Hathikuli Tea Estate in Kohora range on National Highway 715 when the passenger vehicle collided with the truck, a senior officer said.

"We have got a preliminary report that at least seven people were killed in the accident. We are all at the spot, and bodies are being retrieved from the bus, so the number of deaths is likely to rise," Golaghat Senior Superintendent of Police Swapnaneel Deka told PTI .

Later, five more succumbed to their injuries, another officer said.

The exact number of people travelling in the bus is not immediately known, the police said.

Assam Panchayat and Rural Development Minister Atul Bora, who is also the local MLA, reached the site immediately and was supervising the relief and rescue operations.

The injured people were taken to the Kohora Model Hospital, and most of the critically injured were referred to the Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.

"The bus was running at very high speed, violating restrictions imposed near the park. We think that the accident took place when the driver of the minibus lost control, and the vehicle collided with the container truck," he added.

articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained

fullParagraphs: The RBI has reportedly proposed a ₹50 lakh sub-limit within the $250,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap to curb dollar outflows and protect the rupee

The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%

India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

Jensen Huang resigned as Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), bringing an end to his 33-year stint at the helm of the artificial intelligence giant he co-founded, following revelations of his extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.

Nvidia and Mr. Huang, are also facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.
The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​

“The Court is aware of the global outage affecting Microsoft systems. The Court is currently not receiving emails, but the Portal and contact forms are still functioning as normal. Parties and members of the public may not receive email notifications,” the Supreme Court of the U.K. tweeted.
Citing Germany’s approach, FOSS United CEO Poruri said the country had allowed individual regions to choose their email service providers, many of which use established free and open-source software.

India should adopt a similar approach instead of relying on a single provider, he said. Referring to the migration of government email services from the National Informatics Centre (NIC) to Zoho, he cautioned against replacing dependence on one provider with dependence on another.
Such diversification could also support domestic micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and strengthen the government’s Make in India initiative, he added.
The latest Microsoft outage should serve as a wake-up call for India to reduce its dependence on external technology service providers, Sai Rahul Poruri, CEO of FOSS United, told The Hindu.
Disruptions to email services, a cornerstone of professional communication, could result in significant financial losses for businesses, he said.

European stock market operator Euronext advised listed companies on Friday (November 13, 2026) morning to ‌use the telephone to communicate corporate information after ⁠an outage in Microsoft’s Outlook email service.

“Euronext Corporate Actions and Listing ‌teams are currently experiencing an email communication ‌disruption and are unable to ‌receive ⁠emails,” the company, which ⁠runs exchanges in Paris, Brussels, Lisbon, Amsterdam, Oslo, Athens and Milan, said in a ‌corporate filing.

articles.title: UN nuclear watchdog urges Iran to take 'steps' towards inspections
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The International Atomic Energy Agency has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel and the U.S. launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites

The UN's nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take "incremental steps" to allow inspectors to return to key nuclear facilities in the Islamic republic, adding such access was "critical" in a report seen by AFP on Friday (Novemeber 13, 2026).

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel, joined by the United States, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites.
Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, which erupted on February 28, and the IAEA has repeatedly called for access.
In its report, the agency said that it was "critical" for it to conduct "verification activities in Iran without further delay".
"The director general encourages Iran to consider technical and gradual measures by which conditions are achieved that allow for the return of agency inspectors to Iran," the report said.
The IAEA "acknowledged that the military attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities and sites created an unprecedented situation".

But because of a lack of cooperation "the agency is not able to conclude that there has been no diversion of declared nuclear material from peaceful nuclear activities in Iran", the report said, raising "serious proliferation concern" that "needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency".

The IAEA board in September referred Iran to the UN Security Council, marking the first time Iran has been referred to the UN top body in 20 years for failing to comply with its nuclear reporting obligations.

Before the June 2025 strikes, the IAEA calculated that Iran possessed approximately 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, nearing the 90% needed to make a bomb and well above the 3.67% limit set by a now-defunct 2015 agreement with Iran.
Since June 2025, the fate Iran's nuclear stockpile has remained uncertain.

articles.title: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada’s blue wall in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it.

Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage drags on as company observes ‘limited recovery’
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa

Microsoft Outlook suffered a major outage across the world Thursday (November 12, 2026), with tens of thousands of users struggling to access their email as the company said it was working "aggressively" to reduce the impact.

The disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, dragged on for much of the U.S. workday and also affected other company products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
The disruption went global within a span of an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.
A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas," but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.
"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.
"We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."
In the United States, around 130,000 users reported issues with Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time (1800 GMT), according to Downdetector.

fullParagraphs: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was also called to testify before Senate Banking Committee

U.S. lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.
The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters.
“Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote on Thursday (November 12, 2026) on X.
Mr. Scott said he was requesting mR. Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs.

Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related.
U.S. intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy scandal
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says she has been stopped from coming to Hyderabad for Bharat Summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ms. Lyng says she has been denied entry into India despite having a visa
Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng, who works for the Oslo-based daily newspaper Dagsavisen , has said that she has been stopped from coming to India despite having a valid visa.

“I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. I had been invited as a panellist and speaker on the future of media and press freedom. But «orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” she said in a post on X, on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

“I was supposed to speak on media, press freedom and democracy and how they are intertwined,” she spoke in the video message where she puts the onus on India’s Home Minister Amit Shah to let her come as 48 hours are still there for her session.

I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. I had been invited as a panelist and speaker on the future of media and press freedom. But «orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa. Here is my message for @AmitShah
She linked the refusal to let her into India to the freedom of press question she posed in Norway to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in May 2026.

Ms. Lyng has been listed as a speaker on Day 2 of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on November 14 in a session that will have Leonard Novy, director, Institute for Media and Communications, Sangeeta Baruah Pisharoty, president of the Press Club of India and Francesco Lapenta director of Institute of Future and Innovation Studies. The session will be moderated by Pawan Khera, MP and chairperson of INC Communications.

The Indian Embassy in Norway has not released any statement about the denial of permission. “The embassy in Norway is not at fault. They were truly nice and helpful during the process. It is the Ministry of Home Affairs that has ruined the trip by denying me entry even though I have gotten a visa and had political clearance for the conference,” she wrote in another social media past.
