articles.title: India will remain a trusted partner for global investors, assures Union Minister Piyush Goyal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid the global uncertainties, India is doing all it can to ensure safety of the investors’ money, says the Union Minister for Commerce & Industry

Seeking to assuage fears over the safety of Foreign Direct Investments (FDI) due to the likely impact of global uncertainties, Union Minister for Commerce & Industry Piyush Goyal said India had been and would remain a trusted partner and a reliable destination for investors even as wars raged in other parts of the world.
The ongoing conflicts cast their shadow on international trade, but India was an exception, with its stable policies and governance that would never let the investors down, he asserted.

Participating as the chief guest in the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam on Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Goyal said the world was witnessing multiple crises, challenges and intense competition, but India was committed to standing by investors during these tough times.
He recalled that centuries ago, Kakatiya ruler Ganapati Deva, who governed the Andhra region, issued inscriptions assuring foreign investors of confidence and security.

The investor community could be assured of the business environment even during the present times, as the Government of India was doing all it could to ensure the safety of the money they were pumping into various projects, he asserted.

Mr. Goyal said India would fully respect and protect Intellectual Property Rights and extend cooperation to innovators and investors. India would never steal technology, he stated, promising industries full support in manufacturing high-quality products at competitive costs and at a greater speed.
While foreign investments poured in, India’s skilled youth were making a significant contribution to the country’s GDP growth by leveraging on their skills and capabilities to a phenomenal effect.
He went on to invite entrepreneurs to invest in India and Andhra Pradesh, saying they were offering tremendous opportunities in manufacturing, tourism and several other sectors.
Visakhapatnam was transforming from a ‘Steel City’ into a ‘Silicon City’ and regions like Orvakal and Pudimadaka were emerging as green energy hubs, Mr. Goyal observed.

Further, Mr. Goyal said Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was a visionary leader who thinks ahead of his time and recognises the potential of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Quantum Technologies.

articles.title: When the village becomes an art gallery: 26 homes open their doors to creativity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘10.26’, an unconventional exhibition by Niracharthu in Enkakkad, takes art beyond gallery walls, bringing paintings into the intimate spaces of everyday life

What if an art gallery had no white walls, no ticket counter and no imposing entrance? What if, instead, visitors had to walk through a village, step into its homes and discover paintings displayed on verandas and in domestic spaces? In Enkakkad, art is finding an unconventional home. Twenty-six houses in the village have opened their doors to host ‘10.26’ (Paththu irupathaaru), an exhibition that brings together selected works from the 10-year artistic journey of Niracharthu. Here, the village itself becomes a gallery, and its homes offer an alternative setting for experiencing visual art.

Moving away from the familiar gallery format, the exhibition seeks to dissolve the boundaries between art, architecture and everyday life. Instead of asking villagers to travel to urban galleries, it brings art to their doorsteps, placing the domestic veranda in the spotlight as a space for artistic engagement.

More than 50 works by 45 artists who have participated in Niracharthu’s art camps are on display. The exhibition traces a decade of artistic exploration while offering visitors an opportunity to encounter art in spaces that are part of the village’s lived experience.

The exhibition was formally opened through a walk-through of all 26 venues. Manoj Vailoor, principal of the Mavelikkara College of Fine Arts, and curator Megha V. Sreyus led the walk-through, accompanied by children attending the art workshop, local residents and members of the Niracharthu team.

For curator Megha V. Sreyus, the idea goes beyond changing the location of an exhibition. It is about changing the way people encounter and experience art. “This exhibition invites the viewer to abandon the passive, sterile walking patterns of the gallery hall. To navigate this curated spatiality is to inhabit an itinerary of collective memory, domestic architecture and situated visuality — proving that the most urgent critical engagements of our time can emerge directly from the communal porch. Thus, this exhibition transforms the veranda as an alternate threshold of a visuality reimagined,” she says.

By turning familiar homes into exhibition spaces, ‘10.26’ also creates an opportunity for residents to engage with artworks in an informal setting. The experience is as much about discovering the village as it is about discovering art. The exhibition will continue until December 6. Visitors can explore the 26 venues between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Officials stated that DISCOMs would be evaluated for their performance over a five-year period, following by transmission, generation, renewable energy and RDSS.

The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

articles.title: No compromise with Ukraine, Putin indicates to U.S. envoys during talks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Russian President proposes a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city in Donetsk; he also rules out agreeing to foreign troops being stationed in Ukraine

Vladimir Putin indicated on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that Russia will not compromise on its hardline demands to end the Ukraine offensive but offered a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city in Donetsk during a Kremlin meeting with U.S. envoys.

The Russian President said he would not water down his territorial demands to control parts of Ukraine that Russia claims to have annexed and ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops being stationed in Ukraine — a deployment that he said would be a “continuation of war”.
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were in Moscow after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi searching for a way to end Europe’s worst conflict since the Second World War.
The Americans, meanwhile, urged Mr. Putin to allow European representatives to sit at the table for the next round of talks.
Moscow has successfully managed to reframe the discussions on the war as part of a wider discussion about European security.

But Kyiv and European leaders have urged against a new “Yalta” — a reference to the post-Second World War deal to carve the continent into spheres of influence — and said talks must be focused on ending the Ukraine war first.
Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff will travel to Dublin, where a European summit is taking place, to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy later on Thursday.
Usually held behind closed doors, the Kremlin chose to televise a lengthy opening exchange between Mr. Putin and the U.S. envoys.
The Russian leader also rejected talk of a possible territorial settlement involving “grey” — or demilitarised — zones between Ukrainian and Russian positions.

The Russian President proposes a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city in Donetsk; he also rules out agreeing to foreign troops being stationed in Ukraine

Vladimir Putin indicated on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that Russia will not compromise on its hardline demands to end the Ukraine offensive but offered a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city in Donetsk during a Kremlin meeting with U.S. envoys.

The Russian President said he would not water down his territorial demands to control parts of Ukraine that Russia claims to have annexed and ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops being stationed in Ukraine — a deployment that he said would be a “continuation of war”.

Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were in Moscow after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi searching for a way to end Europe’s worst conflict since the Second World War.

The Americans, meanwhile, urged Mr. Putin to allow European representatives to sit at the table for the next round of talks.

Moscow has successfully managed to reframe the discussions on the war as part of a wider discussion about European security.

But Kyiv and European leaders have urged against a new “Yalta” — a reference to the post-Second World War deal to carve the continent into spheres of influence — and said talks must be focused on ending the Ukraine war first.

Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff will travel to Dublin, where a European summit is taking place, to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy later on Thursday.

Usually held behind closed doors, the Kremlin chose to televise a lengthy opening exchange between Mr. Putin and the U.S. envoys.

The Russian leader also rejected talk of a possible territorial settlement involving “grey” — or demilitarised — zones between Ukrainian and Russian positions.

articles.title: No need for Opposition approval to launch strikes, says Israel’s Katz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot urged caretaker PM Netanyahu to show restraint, warning that force without a “direct and immediate threat” could have “disastrous consequences for Israeli democracy and citizens’ trust”

Israeli caretaker Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that the outgoing coalition does not need permission from the opposition to decide on fresh military operations, following calls to show restraint.
“We do not need approval from the opposition or any legal authority” for the army to carry out strikes in any of the arenas where it operates, Mr. Katz wrote on X.

The leader of the opposition bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, has called on caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to show restraint, warning that the use of force without a “direct and immediate threat” could have “disastrous consequences for Israeli democracy and for citizens’ trust”.
Mr. Netanyahu repeatedly threatened to resume the Iran war on the campaign trail for elections last month, warning of threats and even posting an image of a nuclear bomb destroying Tel Aviv.

Mr. Katz said Thursday (November 12, 2026) that the outgoing coalition had “demonstrated resolve and sound judgment in dealing with Iran, in full coordination with the IDF — and that will remain the case now, as circumstances require”.
Mr. Netanyahu agreed to meet Thursday (November 12, 2026) with Mr. Eisenkot to discuss national security following the row over whether the outgoing government can resume the conflict.
In a short joint statement, Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Netanyahu said they would meet at the Prime Minister’s office for a briefing attended by Mr. Netanyahu’s military aide.
The announcement came a day after Mr. Eisenkot, who has a mandate to try to form a new government , accused Mr. Netanyahu of refusing to brief him, in what he called a deviation from protocol.

Avigdor Liberman, a key member of Mr. Eisenkot’s political bloc who has been named head of a parliamentary committee on foreign and defence affairs, also criticised Mr. Netanyahu on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

“I warn you: a caretaker government is not allowed to make decisions that could drag Israel into war without parliamentary oversight and without the full consent of all security agencies,” said Liberman, a hawkish former aide to Mr. Netanyahu who has become a strident critic.

articles.title: Trump says U.S. does not ‘need a deal with Iran’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: His comments came shortly after the Wall Street Journal reported that Vice-President J.D. Vance was mulling face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that he was directing Vice-President J.D. Vance to focus completely on domestic anti-fraud efforts and not negotiations towards a deal to end the war with Tehran.
“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Mr. Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
The Journal ’s report added Mr. Trump had told aides and counterparts that he was open to Mr. Vance reopening talks with Tehran and that the president had empowered Mr. Vance to negotiate.
Oil prices rose after Mr. Trump’s remarks on social media, while Wall Street futures slipped further.
Anger over war with Iran, which has caused fuel prices to surge in the United States, has been seen as a key factor pushing voters away from Republicans.
Mr. Vance was among Republicans to blame the Iran war for the party’s losses at the ballot box.

The conflict has been ongoing since U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran in late February, prompting Tehran to choke off the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for energy transit. The blockage has wreaked havoc on the world economy, causing energy costs to rocket.

articles.title: Amidst simmering tensions, India-Bangladesh consular dialogue postponed
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: This would have been the fifth such consular dialogue and the first after the August 2024 uprising; postponement due to tensions over former PM Hasina’s plan to return to Bangladesh next month

Days after Bangladesh’s deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested Dhaka for a new passport and national identity card, the fifth India-Bangladesh consular dialogue that was scheduled to take place on November 17 and 18 has been postponed, a diplomatic source has confirmed.

The source indicated that the postponement of the dialogue was mainly on account of growing tensions in the bilateral relationship caused by Ms. Hasina’s announcement that she will return to Bangladesh next month.

The planned consular dialogue would have been the first such meeting between the two sides in more than two years. The last such dialogue was held in New Delhi on May 29, 2024, just over two months before the Hasina government fell in a youth-led uprising in Dhaka.

The consular dialogue was scheduled to be held in Dhaka at the level of Director Generals of the Foreign Ministries of both countries. The planned agenda included issues of border management, visa procedures, and the repatriation of citizens detained on both sides. The number of Indian visas issued was drastically reduced when tensions broke out in August 2024. According to sources, India has gradually increased the number of visas issued to travellers from Bangladesh in recent months, especially after the election of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in February this year.

The two countries started a consular dialogue in 2017 to “strengthen people-to-people contacts by having a regular channel of communication on consular, visa, and mutual legal assistance cooperation matters between India and Bangladesh.” Four rounds of consular dialogues were held during the rule of the Awami League in Dhaka. As per the Ministry of External Affairs, the fourth round held in May 2024 discussed issues like “visa matters, repatriation, Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty cases etc.”

Attempts at normalising the India-Bangladesh relationship in recent months have been hindered by Ms. Hasina’s presence in India, where she took refuge on August 5, 2024. On November 9 this year, a London-based legal firm representing Ms. Hasina wrote to the High Commission of Bangladesh in New Delhi requesting a new passport and the national ID card. “In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client,” said the letter sent by the law firm Matrix Chambers.

However, the Acting Foreign Minister of Bangladesh Humayun Kabir responded to this development by telling journalists that Bangladesh would not issue a passport to Ms. Hasina. Instead, he said, Dhaka would seek Ms. Hasina’s extradition under an “acceptable prisoner exchange process”, adding that such a handover would have to be conducted carefully and under proper surveillance.

articles.title: ISRO successfully carries out ground static test of PSLV third stage
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The configuration of the third stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) which is looking to get its workhorse launcher, the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), back on track has successfully carried out the ground static test of the PSLV third stage (PS3) at the Static Test Facility in Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

“Subsequent to the anomalies observed in the third stage of PSLV during the PSLV-C61/EOS-09 & PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 missions, the configuration of the PS3 stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far,” ISRO said.

“The configuration has been strengthened and essential improvements have been carried out in the nozzle configuration to improve design margins along with updated procedures in the acceptance of raw materials, assembly procedures and quality checks,” ISRO added.
It also said that the mechanical interfaces have been strengthened with redundancy in the sealing systems and adequacy of the design margins have been verified.

“The updates in assembly procedures and non-destructive tests (NDT) during the various phases of integration and transportation have been implemented and the new version of the PS3 solid motor stage is realised and tested successfully,” ISRO said.
Based on the detailed analysis and reviews of the test data, the space agency said further tests are planned.

The configuration of the third stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) which is looking to get its workhorse launcher, the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), back on track has successfully carried out the ground static test of the PSLV third stage (PS3) at the Static Test Facility in Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

“Subsequent to the anomalies observed in the third stage of PSLV during the PSLV-C61/EOS-09 & PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 missions, the configuration of the PS3 stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far,” ISRO said.

“The configuration has been strengthened and essential improvements have been carried out in the nozzle configuration to improve design margins along with updated procedures in the acceptance of raw materials, assembly procedures and quality checks,” ISRO added.

It also said that the mechanical interfaces have been strengthened with redundancy in the sealing systems and adequacy of the design margins have been verified.

“The updates in assembly procedures and non-destructive tests (NDT) during the various phases of integration and transportation have been implemented and the new version of the PS3 solid motor stage is realised and tested successfully,” ISRO said.

Based on the detailed analysis and reviews of the test data, the space agency said further tests are planned.

articles.title: India undergoing massive transformation in renewable energy: Earthshot Prize CEO
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: “There is a race on right now. The first country that can have access to cheap, clean and abundant energy, is going to have a huge economic advantage. And India knows that,” says Jason Knauf

India is at the forefront of climate solutions, and its innovations have immediate global application, especially when it comes to issues such as heat stress, Earthshot Prize CEO Jason Knauf said. He was speaking with The Hindu on Thursday (November 12, 2026) on the background of the launch of the five-day Earthshot Prize summit, which will take place in Mumbai and Jaipur from November 13 to 17.

As COP31 gathers in Türkiye for climate negotiations, it is India and Mumbai which will send a message of climate solutions, he said. “There is a race going on right now. The first country that can have access to cheap, clean and abundant energy, is going to have a huge economic advantage. And I think, India knows that. Which is why so much is being done here to use the huge solar resource that India has,” he said.

Earthshot Prize is one of the world’s most prestigious environmental awards. It was founded by Prince William six years ago. This is the first time the awards are being held in India. Prince William will be in India for the events.

On Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Knauf spoke about how India was an inspiration behind starting the award, why the awards are being held in India and particularly in Mumbai this year, and the lessons he has learnt during his stay in the country. Observing that India is undergoing a “massive transformation” about renewable energy, he said it had an advantage over other countries to bring in sustainable climate solutions. He said there was no debate between economic progress and environmental protection anymore. “What is good for the environment is good for business, and Indian companies are showing that,” Mr. Knauf said, adding that the past Indian winners had been able to raise $800 million in commercial international investment after winning the Earthshot Prize.
The Earthshot Prize is slated to make large announcements about two Indian finalists — Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Mahila Housing Trust, in the coming week.

Mr. Knauf said climate action conversation needed to move beyond the ‘environment bubble’. Acknowledging India’s efforts in the conservation sector, he said it was important to showcase India’s optimism to the world. Adding that the inspiration behind the awards came from India too, he spoke of how the Prince of Wales saw environmental action during his visit to India in 2016, when he was inspired by the country’s approach towards working with nature.

“For a country that is on the frontline of the environmental issues despite having not caused them, people are more optimistic about their abilities to solve them, than many richer countries. That tells you something. We all have to learn from that example. We are happy that the Earthshot Prize is coming here to celebrate that Indian spirit for the whole world,” Mr. Knauf said. He added that Mumbai was chosen as it was the financial and entertainment capital of the country.

“Earthshot Prize is about getting out to people. We want to get out to investors, to corporate leaders. We also want to tap into the world of entertainment and sporting. Mumbai is the perfect place for that. It is the global capital for the financial sector and the entertainment world,” he said.

This year, Earthshot Prize ceremony will be held at an unprecedented scale, he said, adding that over 5,000 people would participate in the events which would draw people from different countries, and children from over 24 States of India. The event would be live telecast around 240 countries for the first time.

Asked about how he saw the climate challenge, Mr. Knauf said he was an eternal optimist. “At Earthshot, we have a simple equation — urgency + optimism = action. Anyone who wants to give up and be negative, that is a big threat to action. As big a threat as carbon emissions. Because the second we decide that the issues are too hard, then we look the other way. That is giving up, and particularly for the next generation that is coming, it is an unacceptable attitude,” he said.

articles.title: Military helicopter crashes in southern Turkey, killing 4
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The aircraft crashed for unknown reasons in Samankoy, a neighbourhood on the southern outskirts of the provincial capital Malatya in the evening
A military helicopter crashed in southern Turkiye on Thursday (November 12, 2026), killing four personnel, the Turkish Defence Ministry said.
The aircraft crashed for unknown reasons in Samankoy, a neighbourhood on the southern outskirts of the provincial capital Malatya in the evening.

“As a result of an accident involving our S-70 helicopter in Malatya, for a reason not yet determined, 4 of our heroic comrades-in-arms aboard the helicopter were martyred,” the Ministry said in a social media post. “We pray that God will have mercy on our martyrs and offer our condolences and prayers for strength to their grieving families, our Turkish Armed Forces, and our noble nation.”

TV images showed the wreckage of the helicopter burning near a cluster of buildings in an otherwise open area of land. The Demiroren News Agency reported that flames had spread to a nearby house but reported no casualties on the ground.
Police, firefighters and medical teams were dispatched to the crash.
The Sikorsky S-70 is widely used as a transport helicopter by militaries across the world. Its variants include the Black Hawk, which can carry up to 11 soldiers plus its air crew.
The Turkish Air Force operates a large base — the 7th Main Jet Base — to the north of Malatya.

articles.title: ‘No one in Dallas wants this’ | U.S. data centre boom fuels concerns over water shortage
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As AI infrastructure expands, residents question its impact on everyday life amid growing demands on local resources and public utilities

“Hey, what do you think of the data centre that’s coming up right across the street from here? I see a lot of construction happening around us all the time,” I ask my colleague Kevin, sounding innocent and naïve, for my Swedish friends had warned me — when I was moving to the U.S. earlier this year — not to touch politics or any sensitive topic at the workplace in America. Instead, talk about family, they had recommended. I didn’t know where data centres fell on that spectrum.

Kevin stiffens. We are having lunch. He carefully places his fork down and looks past me through the window, where a dusty haze from the construction is floating in the hot Texan air, and starts talking softly.

“You know, no one in Dallas wants this! This data centre will run us dry and take all the residents’ water. Water pressure at home has already dropped, and it’ll make our electricity bills higher,” says Kevin, and then looks straight into my eyes and asks, “Why are we paying for this? Anyone vote on this?”
I didn’t have any answers and decide to gently steer the conversation in a different direction. But the question remains alive inside me.
Aerial view of a portion of the Meta Prometheus Campus, an AI data centre and supercluster project, in New Albany, Ohio. | Photo Credit: Getty Images

Until recently, data centres primarily served the needs of cloud computing, search, streaming and e-commerce. However, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has changed the equation because training and operating large AI models require vast amounts of specialised computing power that these newly constructed data centres aim to provide.

AI models, especially generative ones such as Claude and ChatGPT, need huge amounts of processing power and data storage to be trained and used. They come from massive data centres that house special chips, such as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) and Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), to handle these demanding AI tasks quickly.

According to Cushman & Wakefield, a global real estate services firm, the U.S. is by far the most dominant data centre market in the world, and there are, at this point, more than 1,500 data centre projects underway across the country. Within the U.S., the state of Virginia alone has more than 11 GW (gigawatt) of operational data centre capability in 2026, and Dallas is catching up fast.

India is witnessing a similar expansion. According to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, the country’s installed data-centre capacity has grown from around 375 MW in 2020 to approximately 1,575 MW today. The Central Electricity Authority estimates that power demand from data centres could reach nearly 17 GW by 2031-32. Google, meanwhile, is investing $15 billion over five years in an AI hub in Visakhapatnam, including a data-centre campus with an initial capacity of 1 GW. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian has called it the company’s largest AI hub outside the U.S., saying that the company’s “long-term vision” is to accelerate India’s own AI mission.
A view Inside the NTT data centre campus in Garland, Texas, March 2026. | Photo Credit: Getty Images

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

fullParagraphs: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: IT hubs see 82% commute by personal vehicles, just 2% use public transport
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As Cyberabad grapples with growing traffic congestion, an overwhelming 82% of commuter movement across its key IT hubs is accounted for by personal vehicles, while public transport contributes just around 2%, highlighting the region’s dependence on private modes of transport.

According to data presented by Cyberabad Police and the Society for Cyberabad Security Council (SCSC), traffic across 15 key IT-sector locations exceeds 2.5 million vehicles and people every day. The figures underline the scale of the mobility challenge in one of Hyderabad’s fastest-growing employment hubs, which has a resident population of around 3.5 million spread across approximately 637 sq. km, apart from a substantial daily commuter population travelling from other parts of the city.

With around six lakh IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) employees represented by the corporates participating in a stakeholder interaction on Tuesday, Cyberabad Police are looking to bring companies on board to encourage a shift towards shared and sustainable commuting practices.

Director General of Police C.V. Anand stressed the need for public participation, corporate collaboration and sustained awareness campaigns to improve road discipline and traffic management. Highlighting the five pillars of traffic management, namely Education, Enforcement, Engineering, Emergency and Enablement, he said changing established commuting habits would require continuous outreach through schools, colleges, workplaces and local communities.

Cyberabad Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh and SCSC CEO Naved Alam Khan presented an overview of the traffic situation in Cyberabad and outlined the measures being undertaken to address congestion.

“In a first-of-its-kind initiative, we brought together real estate developers, including My Home Group, Google and other MNCs, urging them to take an active role in easing traffic congestion through measures such as staggered office timings, traffic management initiatives and greater participation in improving traffic flow,” said Mr Singh.

Officials also called upon companies to promote employee carpooling, increase the use of larger shared transport vehicles, introduce centralised shuttle services and synchronise hybrid work schedules. Improved parking management and incentives for employees using public transport were also highlighted as possible measures.

The authorities also unveiled the logo of ‘Cyberabad Moves’, a three-day exhibition and symposium scheduled to be held from November 26 to 28 at T-Hub. The event will bring together government departments, startups, civil society organisations, school students, corporate leaders and citizens to explore practical and technology-driven solutions to urban mobility challenges.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 11 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 IT hubs see 82% commute by personal vehicles, just 2% use public transport

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

As Cyberabad grapples with growing traffic congestion, an overwhelming 82% of commuter movement across its key IT hubs is accounted for by personal vehicles, while public transport contributes just around 2%, highlighting the region’s dependence on private modes of transport.

According to data presented by Cyberabad Police and the Society for Cyberabad Security Council (SCSC), traffic across 15 key IT-sector locations exceeds 2.5 million vehicles and people every day. The figures underline the scale of the mobility challenge in one of Hyderabad’s fastest-growing employment hubs, which has a resident population of around 3.5 million spread across approximately 637 sq. km, apart from a substantial daily commuter population travelling from other parts of the city.

With around six lakh IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) employees represented by the corporates participating in a stakeholder interaction on Tuesday, Cyberabad Police are looking to bring companies on board to encourage a shift towards shared and sustainable commuting practices.

Director General of Police C.V. Anand stressed the need for public participation, corporate collaboration and sustained awareness campaigns to improve road discipline and traffic management. Highlighting the five pillars of traffic management, namely Education, Enforcement, Engineering, Emergency and Enablement, he said changing established commuting habits would require continuous outreach through schools, colleges, workplaces and local communities.

Cyberabad Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh and SCSC CEO Naved Alam Khan presented an overview of the traffic situation in Cyberabad and outlined the measures being undertaken to address congestion.

“In a first-of-its-kind initiative, we brought together real estate developers, including My Home Group, Google and other MNCs, urging them to take an active role in easing traffic congestion through measures such as staggered office timings, traffic management initiatives and greater participation in improving traffic flow,” said Mr Singh.

Officials also called upon companies to promote employee carpooling, increase the use of larger shared transport vehicles, introduce centralised shuttle services and synchronise hybrid work schedules. Improved parking management and incentives for employees using public transport were also highlighted as possible measures.

The authorities also unveiled the logo of ‘Cyberabad Moves’, a three-day exhibition and symposium scheduled to be held from November 26 to 28 at T-Hub. The event will bring together government departments, startups, civil society organisations, school students, corporate leaders and citizens to explore practical and technology-driven solutions to urban mobility challenges.

articles.title: World Wars and India’s sacrifice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: We owe it to ourselves to be honest with our past, just as we owe it to our armed forces to honour the sacrifices of those who went before them

On the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month, most Commonwealth and other allied nations fall silent for two minutes to honour the fallen of the two World Wars. Not so much in India: wreaths are laid in cantonments, but for most, this is just another day. India has an uneasy relationship with Remembrance Day. However, the idea that the World Wars were something that happened to someone else, somewhere else, could not be further from the truth.

Indian ambivalence over the two World Wars belies its enormous contribution to fighting fascism. Undivided (British) India sent 1.5 million men to fight in World War I, 74,000 of whom never returned home. For WWII, India produced the largest volunteer army of 2.5 million soldiers, with 87,00–89,000 making the ultimate sacrifice. The princely states also sent significant troops. Whereas the Indians who fought in the Great War were mostly sent to distant lands, in WWII, about 7,00,000 of them were defending Indian territory. The war came home to India when Japan invaded the country in March 1944.
Political & National Report: World Wars and India’s sacrifice. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Civil police officer injured in attack by detained man in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The officer was injured after a man who had been detained on charge of creating public nuisance in the city allegedly bit on his hands while he was being taken in a police vehicle for medical examination

A civil police officer (CPO) attached to the Ernakulam North police station was injured after a man who had been detained on charge of creating public nuisance near the North overbridge bit on his hands when he was being taken in a police vehicle for medical examination, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

This comes two days after another CPO who was on traffic duty at the High Court bus stand was injured after a recklessly driven private bus rammed him. The incident occurred after the officer stopped a row of vehicles for an ambulance to pass through.

The Ernakulam Central police have registered a case against Muhammed Iqbal, 25, of Sashthamkotta in Kollam who, while being reportedly under the influence of intoxicants, bit on the hands of the police officer named Ajith Paul. He was seated on the last row of the police vehicle, from where he jumped into the middle row seat and reportedly tried to force open the door as the vehicle reached the Ernakulam General Hospital.

The officer was injured as he attempted to overpower him. The detainee also reportedly used abusive words. The police charged him under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Section 121 (1) — voluntarily causing hurt to a public servant to deter him from discharging his duty and 296(b) — use of obscene words in a public place.

He was taken for medical examination after he reportedly turned unruly at the police station soon after he was detained. He allegedly continued to create unruly scenes at the station even after being brought back after medical examination, a video of which went viral. Following these, he was remanded in judicial custody.

Veeramani, being investigated as the main accused in a series of child sexual abuse cases, approached the Madras High Court with a plea to order an investigation into the human rights violations allegedly perpetrated against her by the State police and also to quash the summons issued after forcibly making her deboard a Singapore-bound airplane on October 23, 2026.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan is expected to hear her plea on Wednesday (November 11, 2026). The High Court Registry had numbered her writ petition (criminal) subject to maintainability. articles.title: Focus on Tamil during Kandasashthi: Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He urged temples under the purview of the department to ensure that Odhuvars chant/sing the Thirupugazh, Thirumurai, and Kandasashthi kavacham

Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) S. Ramesh on Tuesday said that Tamil language and literature will be given priority during the Kandasashthi festival in all major Murugan temples.

He urged temples under the purview of the department to ensure that Odhuvars chant/sing the Thirupugazh, Thirumurai, and Kandasashthi kavacham. Priests should also give priority to Tamil in all pujas and proceedings during the festival. Discourses and concerts should be in Tamil as well, he added.

In a set of directions issued to executive officers of temples, the Minister said that special arrangements must be made for persons with disabilities, senior citizens, and mothers-to-be at temples for darshan. Volunteers should be made available to assist such devotees, said an official statement here.

Mr. Ramesh said that temple officials should coordinate with the police, fire and other departments to ensure proper arrangements such as drinking water, toilets and medical care for devotees for darshan, during Kandasashthi and Sura Samharam.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu police step-up surveillance on habitual offenders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 443 accused persons arrested in Statewide drive against rowdyism
The Tamil Nadu police have arrested 443 accused persons involved in various crimes, including drug offences and violent crimes, across the State and enhanced vigil on habitual offenders.

In a two-day operation against rowdyism and organised crime, which was launched on Monday, the police conducted intensive checks at places frequented by persons with criminal antecedents. Police personnel checked the activities of more than 15,000 anti-social elements and thousands of vehicles as part of the operation, which resulted in the arrest of 443 suspects who were produced in local courts and remanded in judicial custody.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Director-General of Police and Head of the Police Force, Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, said the two-day operation was planned decisively to curb criminal activities, disrupt drug distribution networks, and reinforce absolute public order.

Police teams across Tamil Nadu systematically tracked and checked 8,626 listed rowdies. As many as 796 habitual offenders were placed under strict preventive surveillance. articles.title: Strategic autonomy must guide India’s Starlink policy
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: India must balance Starlink’s benefits with national security and strategic autonomy

Recently, Elon Musk unleashed a volley of social media posts, accusing Indian “oligarchs” of impeding Starlink’s entry into India. The government rejected the accusation and clarified that all satellite operators must go through the same regulatory process. The ensuing public debate has centred on Mr. Musk, Mukesh Ambani, protectionism and telecom competition. All this obscures important questions of how much control India will have over Starlink once it operates here.

In its current form, Starlink is unlikely to replace fibre and mobile networks because they have almost opposite strengths. Fibre and mobile networks take time and money to set up, but can serve many people in one area. Starlink reaches remote places without towers or cables but is limited by how many users it can serve in one region. While fibre and mobile networks are optimised for density, Starlink is optimised for reach. Starlink has previously stopped taking new residential customers in areas where it ran out of capacity.

articles.summary: India must balance Starlink’s benefits with national security and strategic autonomy
articles.keyPoints:
• India must balance Starlink’s benefits with national security and strategic autonomy
• Recently, Elon Musk unleashed a volley of social media posts, accusing Indian “oligarchs” of impeding Starlink’s entry into India. The government rejected the accusation and clarified that all satellite operators must go through the same regulatory process. The ensuing public debate has centred on Mr. Musk, Mukesh Ambani, protectionism and telecom competition. All this obscures important questions of how much control India will have over Starlink once it operates here.
• In its current form, Starlink is unlikely to replace fibre and mobile networks because they have almost opposite strengths. Fibre and mobile networks take time and money to set up, but can serve many people in one area. Starlink reaches remote places without towers or cables but is limited by how many users it can serve in one region. While fibre and mobile networks are optimised for density, Starlink is optimised for reach. Starlink has previously stopped taking new residential customers in areas where it ran out of capacity.

articles.title: Vaiko releases 34-year crime report; rebukes allies for criticising T.N. government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid ongoing accusations by Opposition parties of increase in crime and deteriorating law and order in Tamil Nadu, MDMK general secretary Vaiko on Tuesday released a catalogue of crimes that occurred over the past 34 years. He also lamented that the TVK-led government was being criticised by two of its coalition partners.
Addressing journalists in Chennai on Tuesday, he said except the IUML and the MDMK, the other parties within the ruling alliance have been criticising the administration.

Mr. Vaiko released a list detailing crimes committed in the State between May 1991 and May 2026. Citing the list compiled by the Madurai-based human rights organisation People’s Watch, he highlighted several major criminal incidents.

Speaking on the subject for over an hour, Vaiko also recounted the backdrop of key moments from his own political journey during this period. In particular, he detailed the circumstances surrounding his arrest under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA) in July 2002. He noted that upon learning of the Tamil Nadu government’s decision to detain him under POTA, he advanced his return from the United States — originally scheduled for July 15 — and arrived in Chennai on July 11 to court arrest. He added while he was meant to be lodged in the Vellore Central Prison, authorities attempted to detain him at the Madurai Central Prison en route, an effort that was abandoned only after his fierce resistance.

He also recalled that it was former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi who first addressed him as “Vaiko” instead of his full name V. Gopalasamy. He recounted that during the inaugural meeting held in Delhi to form the National Front, M. Karunanidhi had sent him a note on a slip of paper addressed to ‘ Thambi Vaikovukku’ .

Mr. Vaiko alleged some time after he founded the MDMK, L. Ganesan and Gingee N. Ramachandran attempted to split the party and organise a rival general council meeting on the instructions of the DMK leadership, but those efforts ended in failure.

He further recalled that following his release from prison under POTA, he undertook a padayatra from Tirunelveli to Chennai alongside 1,200 people, demanding an end to caste and communal clashes and the complete eradication of narcotics. Although he was denied entry into Chennai as the march neared the city, he defied the restrictions, entered Chennai, and addressed a public meeting.

Mr. Vaiko also mentioned that when Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa as a special guest to his swearing-in ceremony, he vehemently opposed the move and was arrested after staging a demonstration at Jantar Mantar.

Stating he had opposed the Sterlite plant in Thoothukudi from the very beginning, Mr. Vaiko alleged fresh efforts were under way to reopen the facility under the pretext of producing “Green Copper.” He claimed Vedanta’s Anil Agarwal had sought an appointment with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for this purpose; however, following his own appeal urging the Chief Minister not to meet him, the meeting did not take place, and Mr. Agarwal has now approached the court.
Prior to Mr. Vaiko’s address, leaders from his party spoke in detail about his political contributions.

articles.title: Bihar Cabinet hikes 3% DA for employees, pensioners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Cabinet approved the “Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme”, under which, 2,100 female students may be provided benefits beginning from the current financial year

Bihar Cabinet on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) approved a 3% increase in the dearness allowance (DA) for its employees, pensioners and family pensioners getting revised salary or pension as per the 7th Pay Commission recommendations.
The decision would provide relief to the common people during the festive season of Chhath.

“The Cabinet has taken a decision to increase DA by 3% three per cent from the existing 60% to 63%. It will be payable with effect from July 01, 2026. The hiked DA will be payable to government employees, pensioners and family pensioners getting revised salary or pension as per the 7th Pay Commission recommendations,” Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters here in a post cabinet briefing.

Similarly, DA has also been hiked by 7% (from 262% to 269%) and 14% (from 483% to 497%) for drawing salary/pension under the 6th Central Pay Scale and the 5th Central Pay Scale, Mr. Chaudhary said, adding that the hiked DA payable with effect from July 01, 2026.

In reply to a query, ACS said that the decision would put additional burden of ₹1,080.33 crore to the State’s exchequer. He, however, said that the amount for 6th and 5th pay scale people is minuscule.
A total of 32 decisions were approved by the Cabinet chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.

The Cabinet also gave its nod to “Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme”. It will be launched to promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and startup culture among female students enrolled in higher educational institutions and to help transform their innovative ideas into viable business ventures.

Under the scheme, a maximum of 2,100 female students may be provided benefits beginning from the current financial year. The scheme shall be implemented over a period of four financial years, from 2026-27 to 2029-30. A sum of ₹88.20 crore has been approved for the purpose.

In order to encourage the participation of female students in the fields of higher education and research, the Cabinet approved “Chief Minister’s Girls’ Ph.D. Fellowship Scheme”. The scheme will be implemented over four financial years, from 2026–27 to 2029–30. A sum of ₹126 crore has been approved for the purpose.

The launch of the “Chief Minister’s Girls’ Ph.D. Fellowship Scheme” is expected to increase the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of women in higher education and enable female students to avail themselves of the benefits of higher education

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 11 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Bihar Cabinet hikes 3% DA for employees, pensioners

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

The Cabinet approved the “Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme”, under which, 2,100 female students may be provided benefits beginning from the current financial year

Bihar Cabinet on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) approved a 3% increase in the dearness allowance (DA) for its employees, pensioners and family pensioners getting revised salary or pension as per the 7th Pay Commission recommendations.

The decision would provide relief to the common people during the festive season of Chhath.

“The Cabinet has taken a decision to increase DA by 3% three per cent from the existing 60% to 63%. It will be payable with effect from July 01, 2026. The hiked DA will be payable to government employees, pensioners and family pensioners getting revised salary or pension as per the 7th Pay Commission recommendations,” Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters here in a post cabinet briefing.

Similarly, DA has also been hiked by 7% (from 262% to 269%) and 14% (from 483% to 497%) for drawing salary/pension under the 6th Central Pay Scale and the 5th Central Pay Scale, Mr. Chaudhary said, adding that the hiked DA payable with effect from July 01, 2026.

In reply to a query, ACS said that the decision would put additional burden of ₹1,080.33 crore to the State’s exchequer. He, however, said that the amount for 6th and 5th pay scale people is minuscule.

A total of 32 decisions were approved by the Cabinet chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.

The Cabinet also gave its nod to “Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme”. It will be launched to promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and startup culture among female students enrolled in higher educational institutions and to help transform their innovative ideas into viable business ventures.

Under the scheme, a maximum of 2,100 female students may be provided benefits beginning from the current financial year. The scheme shall be implemented over a period of four financial years, from 2026-27 to 2029-30. A sum of ₹88.20 crore has been approved for the purpose.

In order to encourage the participation of female students in the fields of higher education and research, the Cabinet approved “Chief Minister’s Girls’ Ph.D. Fellowship Scheme”. The scheme will be implemented over four financial years, from 2026–27 to 2029–30. A sum of ₹126 crore has been approved for the purpose.

The launch of the “Chief Minister’s Girls’ Ph.D. Fellowship Scheme” is expected to increase the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of women in higher education and enable female students to avail themselves of the benefits of higher education

articles.title: Hemant Soren recommends CBI probe into Nisha Bhagat’s death case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of the Opposition in Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on November 7 demanded a CBI investigation into the death of social activist Nisha Bhagat

Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), recommended to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the death case of Tribal leader and social activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat.
Nisha Bhagat on November 6, 2026, allegedly died by suicide in Jharkhand’s Ranchi shortly after going live on social media. The incident took place under the Pithoria Police station area.
In her live broadcast she questioned the role of Hemant Soren’s government and certain individuals associated with land mafia, and the police.

Targeting the State government, she had said that if bringing the government’s shortcomings to public domain and exposing them is wrong, then she is now paying the price for it. During the live, she had also allegedly called up Pithoria PS SHO.
Leader of the Opposition in Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on Saturday (November 7, 2026) demanded that the CBI look into the case.
“The CBI will now investigate the Nisha Bhagat case. Orders have been issued,” Mr. Soren said in a post on X on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
The BJP has demanded a CBI investigation into the death. On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the BJP’s Scheduled Tribe Morcha organised a torchlight procession in Ranchi.
During the event, party leaders and workers demanded that Mr. Soren should give an explanation over Bhagat’s death and also conduct an impartial investigation.

The government’s decision came just hours after Ranchi Rural Superintendent of Police (SP) Gaurav Goswami assured the press that a Special Investigation Team (SIT) was investigating the matter. The SHO of Pithoria Police Station has also been removed from active duty and sent to the police lines.
Reacting to the CM’s order, Jharkhand BJP State president Aditya Sahu said that the decision has been taken under the pressure of BJP.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet clears policy frameworks to attract investments in AI, electronics, renewable energy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety to be set up at Mangalagiri; ₹31,387-crore green integrated AI data centre proposed by AM Intelligence at Amanam in Visakhapatnam district cleared

The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu at the Secretariat on Tuesday, approved a series of proposals aimed at attracting investments in artificial intelligence, electronics, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing, besides taking decisions on infrastructure, education and administration.

The Cabinet approved the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) Policy 2026-31 and the Robotics and Physical AI Policy 2026-36. It also cleared amendments to the Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 2024-29. The Cabinet approved the establishment of a dedicated Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety under the supervision of the Director-General of Police (DGP), with its headquarters at Mangalagiri.

Among the major investment proposals, the Cabinet approved an investment of ₹31,387 crore by AM Intelligence for a 512 MW green integrated AI data centre at Amanam in Bheemunipatnam mandal of Visakhapatnam district. It also cleared a ₹4,000.20-crore Carbon Cosmo advanced materials manufacturing project at Naidupeta and land allotment to Dixon Technologies in Tirupati for an investment of ₹700 crore, sources said.

The Cabinet approved the allocation of about 25 acres to Reliance Industries for a gigascale AI data centre at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district. An Epack unit for manufacturing AI data centre equipment will be established at Rambilli in Anakapalli district with an investment of ₹570.20 crore, creating employment for 2,565 people.

The Hetero Group was granted 173.82 acres in Nakkapalli Bulk Drug Park for its pharmaceutical units. The Cabinet also approved a ₹236.92-crore expansion project of Ravali Spinners in West Godavari district, expected to provide employment to 1,569 people.

The Cabinet cleared a proposal to establish a 30-acre FICCI FLO industrial park exclusively for women entrepreneurs at Jaggayyapet in NTR district. An integrated footwear park spread over 56.82 acres in Annamayya district and an MSME park at Thamballapalle were also approved.

On the energy front, the Cabinet approved the establishment of compressed biogas plants in NTR, Prakasam and Vizianagaram districts and agreed to examine the feasibility of setting up nuclear power plants using Small Modular Reactor (SMR) technology as an alternative to thermal power.

It approved the transfer of 5.50 acres of APGENCO land to the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) for a 15 MW waste-to-energy plant. A 30-year lease of 192.68 acres of Wakf land in Vajrakarur mandal in Anantapur district for a solar power project was also cleared.

Other decisions included allotment of five acres on lease to a Kendriya Vidyalaya at Shakamuru in the capital region, exemption from stamp duty and registration charges, and allotment of two acres for a Government Industrial Training Institute at Penukonda.

The Cabinet approved the creation of two posts, Principal Sannidhi Yadava and Sannidhi Yadava, at the Tirumala temple and a Chief Sthapathi post in the Endowments Department. It approved the withdrawal of earlier land allotments made to Websol Renewables and Metro Decorative at the Naidupeta Special Economic Zone.
