📰 Andhra Pradesh Cabinet clears policy frameworks to attract investments in AI, electronics, renewable energy

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety to be set up at Mangalagiri; ₹31,387-crore green integrated AI data centre proposed by AM Intelligence at Amanam in Visakhapatnam district cleared

The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu at the Secretariat on Tuesday, approved a series of proposals aimed at attracting investments in artificial intelligence, electronics, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing, besides taking decisions on infrastructure, education and administration.

The Cabinet approved the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) Policy 2026-31 and the Robotics and Physical AI Policy 2026-36. It also cleared amendments to the Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 2024-29. The Cabinet approved the establishment of a dedicated Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety under the supervision of the Director-General of Police (DGP), with its headquarters at Mangalagiri.

Among the major investment proposals, the Cabinet approved an investment of ₹31,387 crore by AM Intelligence for a 512 MW green integrated AI data centre at Amanam in Bheemunipatnam mandal of Visakhapatnam district. It also cleared a ₹4,000.20-crore Carbon Cosmo advanced materials manufacturing project at Naidupeta and land allotment to Dixon Technologies in Tirupati for an investment of ₹700 crore, sources said.

The Cabinet approved the allocation of about 25 acres to Reliance Industries for a gigascale AI data centre at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district. An Epack unit for manufacturing AI data centre equipment will be established at Rambilli in Anakapalli district with an investment of ₹570.20 crore, creating employment for 2,565 people.

The Hetero Group was granted 173.82 acres in Nakkapalli Bulk Drug Park for its pharmaceutical units. The Cabinet also approved a ₹236.92-crore expansion project of Ravali Spinners in West Godavari district, expected to provide employment to 1,569 people.

The Cabinet cleared a proposal to establish a 30-acre FICCI FLO industrial park exclusively for women entrepreneurs at Jaggayyapet in NTR district. An integrated footwear park spread over 56.82 acres in Annamayya district and an MSME park at Thamballapalle were also approved.

On the energy front, the Cabinet approved the establishment of compressed biogas plants in NTR, Prakasam and Vizianagaram districts and agreed to examine the feasibility of setting up nuclear power plants using Small Modular Reactor (SMR) technology as an alternative to thermal power.

It approved the transfer of 5.50 acres of APGENCO land to the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) for a 15 MW waste-to-energy plant. A 30-year lease of 192.68 acres of Wakf land in Vajrakarur mandal in Anantapur district for a solar power project was also cleared.

Other decisions included allotment of five acres on lease to a Kendriya Vidyalaya at Shakamuru in the capital region, exemption from stamp duty and registration charges, and allotment of two acres for a Government Industrial Training Institute at Penukonda.

The Cabinet approved the creation of two posts, Principal Sannidhi Yadava and Sannidhi Yadava, at the Tirumala temple and a Chief Sthapathi post in the Endowments Department. It approved the withdrawal of earlier land allotments made to Websol Renewables and Metro Decorative at the Naidupeta Special Economic Zone.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Cabinet approved the creation of two posts, Principal Sannidhi Yadava and Sannidhi Yadava, at the Tirumala temple and a Chief Sthapathi post in the Endowments Department. articles.title: Bihar CM suspends 15 officers for negligence of duty
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD) four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) suspended 15 officers with immediate effect for negligence and failure to ensure the quality resolution of applications under the ‘Sahyog’ (Assistance) Programme.
The action has been taken and departmental proceedings have also been initiated against them for failing to process applications in a timely manner,

Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD), four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.
The officers include Block Development Officers (BDOs) and Circle Officers (COs), assistance engineers and junior engineers.

“All officers and personnel must extend their full cooperation in the processing of applications. It is our duty to address everyone’s problems with sensitivity and promptness, and to ensure they receive justice,” Mr. Choudhary said while holding the ‘State-Level Sahyog Programme at Chief Minister’s Secretariat where 76 applications were received.

He further said that the government’s objective is to ensure a transparent, fair, and time-bound resolution to every citizen’s grievance. The ‘Sahyog’ camps are intended to address public concerns and ensure citizen satisfaction.

Mr. Choudhary has directed all District Magistrates, departmental secretaries, and officials within the Chief Minister’s Secretariat to go beyond merely reviewing the timeliness of the resolution of applications received through the ‘Sahyog’ portal; they must also conduct a thorough review of the quality of these resolutions.

The initiative, which was launched for the first time by Mr. Choudhary, is part of the state government’s ‘Ease of Living’ under the ambitious ‘Saat Nischay-3’ programme aimed at delivering services at citizens’ doorsteps.

At the time of launching the initiative in May 19, 2026, it was already mentioned that if a case is not resolved within 30 days of receiving the application, suspension and disciplinary action will be taken against the responsible officers. These camps are organised on the first and third Tuesdays of every month to address complaints related to block offices, police stations, and revenue offices.
Mr. Choudhary instructed officials to ensure that the grievances of the general public are addressed with complete clarity and transparency.

articles.title: Producers welcome proposal for minimum sustainable price for tea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to the Ministry of Commerce to implement minimum sustainable price (MSP) for tea. Several stake holders said that MSP is essential for long-term sustainability of the industry

Observing that a committee of Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to implement minimum sustainable price for tea, several stakeholders of the tea industry on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) welcomed the proposal and said that such an initiative will help in increasing wages of tea garden workers and is essential for long term sustainability of the industry.

Representatives of different associations associated with the industry expressed apprehensions that with implementation of the Code on Wages, there will be a further increase in wage costs, and the financial viability of tea producers is likely to face additional challenges

“The tea industry is confronted with mounting cost pressures, while tea price realisations have remained relatively stagnant. A Minimum Sustainable Price framework is therefore essential to bridge the widening gap between production costs and market realisations and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the industry,” said C. K Dhanuka, Chairman, Dhunseri Tea and Industries. Mr. Dhanuka added that a minimum sustainable price will help bring realisations in line with costs, so that the industry can accommodate wage revisions, protect employment and the competitiveness of Indian tea.
The proposal of implementing minimum sustainable price for tea have been made to Ministry of Commerce, which is yet to take a decision on the proposal, the stakeholders of tea industry said.

Suneel Singh Sikand, chairman of Indian Tea Association (ITA) called the recommendation for a minimum sustainable price is an important policy intervention towards addressing the structural challenges confronting the Indian tea industry.

“Ensuring remunerative returns to producers is critical to sustaining operations, facilitating investment in re-plantation and productivity enhancement and securing the industry’s long-term sustainability,” Mr. Sikand said.

Hemanta Bangur, former president of ITA said that the industry has failed to uplift the workforce and something is fundamentally wrong with the industry as the balance sheet of most of the tea growers is in the red.
“The market is dysfunctional and there is no level playing field. If market forces are left to determine the fate of industry, it will bring about the demise of tea gardens,” he said.
The Tea Industry employs millions of workers in about 270 large tea gardens and hundreds of small tea gardens across the State. The daily wage for a tea garden worker in West Bengal is ₹250 per day.

Representatives of Indian Tea Association (ITA), Tea Association of India (TAI), United Planters’ Association of Southern India (UPASI), Confederation of Indian Small Tea Growers Associations (CISTA) and Federation of Indian Tea Manufacturers Association (FITMA) issued a press statement on the stagnation in the prices over the past several years

articles.title: U.S. Republicans derail bid to impeach Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee; this halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January

Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) blocked an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war , handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party's crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.
The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to U.S. media.
ALSO WATCH What are the impeachment charges against Pete Hegseth? | The Hindu Explains

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Mr. Trump's troubles after Democrats swept last week's midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.
Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, hailed the vote as a "TOTAL VICTORY!"
"We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest."
Mr. Hegseth earlier on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the impeachment effort as a "farce" and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Mr. Trump.
"It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it," he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations "slander" and "sabotage."

articles.title: Over 74 lakh voters missing from Tamil Nadu electoral rolls, says citizens’ collective
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The collective has announced a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
The Independent Young Citizens Collective (IYCC) has alleged that 74.07 lakh voters have been removed from Tamil Nadu’s electoral rolls and demanded an inquiry into the alleged deletions.

Announcing a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the collective said the reported deletion of such a large number of names has raised serious questions about the exercise and its implications for democracy.
The IYCC is part of ‘People Against SIR’, a national platform comprising mass organisations, social movements and individual activists, independent of political parties.

The collective released its statement at a press conference at the Chennai Press Club on Tuesday. Those who addressed the meeting included political economist Parakala Prabhakar; Carnatic vocalist, writer and Ramon Magsaysay Award recipient T.M. Krishna; former General Secretary of the All India Bank Officers’ Confederation Thomas Franco; and cultural-political activist and IYCC co-convenor Radhika Ganesh.

Ms. Radhika Ganesh alleged that the SIR was a BJP-RSS project without constitutional basis and claimed that it had resulted in the removal of 74.07 lakh voters, accounting for around 11.5% of the State’s electorate. She described the deletions as a democratic crisis and sought answers from the Election Commission of India, accountability from the Union government and a clear response from political parties in Tamil Nadu.

Mr. Prabhakar called for the scrapping of the SIR and the restoration of all eligible voters whose names had been deleted. He also demanded that elections conducted using electoral rolls prepared through the SIR be annulled.

He sought the repeal of the 2023 law granting immunity to Election Commissioners and called for changes to the process of appointing them, including an end to the executive’s 2:1 majority in the selection committee. He further demanded that the forthcoming elections be conducted using the 2024 electoral rolls rather than the SIR rolls.

Mr. Krishna alleged that the revision exercise had been designed to create confusion and exclude voters. He questioned the Election Commission’s approach and the absence of a stronger political response to the exercise.

Criticising the enumeration form and the requirement for voters to furnish details relating to the 2002 electoral rolls, he said the exercise placed an unreasonable burden on ordinary citizens, many of whom might not remember their polling stations or other details from more than two decades ago.

He also alleged that the exercise appeared to focus more on identifying voters for deletion than ensuring the inclusion of every eligible citizen. He questioned the reliance on the 2002 electoral rolls when many voters had participated in subsequent elections.

articles.title: Pranab Mukherjee hinted at desire to become PM, ‘shocked’ me, writes Sonia Gandhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In her memoir, former Congress president recalls 2010 conversation; Pranab Mukherjee’s daughter Sharmistha asks what there was to be shocked about, says it is not a crime to be ambitious

Former President Pranab Mukherjee had “shocked” Sonia Gandhi by hinting at his “long-held desire” to become Prime Minister during a conversation with her in 2010, suggesting that perhaps it was time for a “change at the top”, the former Congress president has written in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love .
The book, published by HarperCollins, was made available in bookstores on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), but the official launch is likely to take place on November 16.

Mukherjee, then a senior member of the Manmohan Singh Cabinet, had developed serious differences with the then Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. He would sometimes stay back for conversations with Ms. Gandhi after meetings of the Congress Strategy Group, which was set up to discuss parliamentary business.

“On one occasion, in 2010, I think after expressing his frustration, he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top, which I understood as a hint of his long-held desire to become Prime Minister,” she wrote.
“I gently changed the subject, and though he may have been disappointed, he never made me feel he held it against me,” she added.

The late Mukherjee, who had served in Indira Gandhi’s Cabinet in the 1970s, was part of a core group that met weekly with Dr. Singh to coordinate the functioning of the government and the party. Other members included Arjun Singh, A.K. Antony and Ahmed Patel.
Ms. Gandhi says she often called on Mukherjee after he became President in 2012, largely to converse with the “erudite and knowledgeable politician that he always remained”.
Hitting back at Ms. Gandhi, Sharmistha Mukherjee, the late President’s daughter, said it was not a crime to be ambitious.
“What’s there to be shocked about?” she asked in a post on X in response to Ms. Gandhi’s remarks.

“Is it a crime to be ambitious, especially when that ‘ambition’ was supported by decades of experience in politics and governance, hard work and a brilliant mind? Once, when asked by me whether he wanted to become PM, he very candidly answered that ‘any politician worth his salt has this ambition’,” she wrote.

Former President Pranab Mukherjee had “shocked” Sonia Gandhi by hinting at his “long-held desire” to become Prime Minister during a conversation with her in 2010, suggesting that perhaps it was time for a “change at the top”, the former Congress president has written in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love .

The book, published by HarperCollins, was made available in bookstores on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), but the official launch is likely to take place on November 16.

Mukherjee, then a senior member of the Manmohan Singh Cabinet, had developed serious differences with the then Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. He would sometimes stay back for conversations with Ms. Gandhi after meetings of the Congress Strategy Group, which was set up to discuss parliamentary business.

“On one occasion, in 2010, I think after expressing his frustration, he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top, which I understood as a hint of his long-held desire to become Prime Minister,” she wrote.

“I gently changed the subject, and though he may have been disappointed, he never made me feel he held it against me,” she added.

The late Mukherjee, who had served in Indira Gandhi’s Cabinet in the 1970s, was part of a core group that met weekly with Dr. Singh to coordinate the functioning of the government and the party. Other members included Arjun Singh, A.K. Antony and Ahmed Patel.

Ms. Gandhi says she often called on Mukherjee after he became President in 2012, largely to converse with the “erudite and knowledgeable politician that he always remained”.

Hitting back at Ms. Gandhi, Sharmistha Mukherjee, the late President’s daughter, said it was not a crime to be ambitious.

“What’s there to be shocked about?” she asked in a post on X in response to Ms. Gandhi’s remarks.

“Is it a crime to be ambitious, especially when that ‘ambition’ was supported by decades of experience in politics and governance, hard work and a brilliant mind? fullParagraphs: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document”

A day after the Acting Foreign Minister of Bangladesh, Humayun Kabir, stressed that Dhaka would not issue a passport to deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and insisted on getting her extradited from India under an “acceptable prisoner exchange”, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that a “travel document” was needed for international travel.

“Extradition of former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina is a legal matter and it will be dealt with accordingly,” said Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in response to a question about Ms. Hasina’s presence in India. He described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document.”
Officials said Ms. Hasina can be extradited either on a Bangladeshi passport or an Emergency Certificate that would prove that she has Bangladeshi citizenship.

On Monday (November 9, 2026), Mr. Kabir cited the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh, which was signed during the Hasina era in 2013, and said, “Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process.”

An official dealing with the matter told The Hindu on Monday (November 9, 2026) that a passport was required for extradition. The deposed Prime Minister has sought a new passport and a national identity document through a London-based law firm that has written to the Bangladesh government.

Bangladesh has a history of leaders going into exile or being imprisoned for long periods after returning. Current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was in exile for nearly 17 years before he returned from the United Kingdom on December 25, 2025.
On August 5, 2026, Ms. Hasina had announced at a virtual press conference that she would return to Bangladesh in December this year.

Over the past few days, the law and order situation has deteriorated across Bangladesh, with incidents of violence, looting, and arson being reported. On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Jamaat-e-Islami and the National Citizen Party, which are in the Opposition, accused the government of failing to maintain law and order.

Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman, said the country’s Home Ministry has failed to contain the situation. “Even the Army Golf Club has now witnessed cocktail explosions. Similar incidents have occurred in front of the Special Branch headquarters, at police station gates, and at Dhaka University, where explosions have taken place for three consecutive days. Two people were injured there,” he said.

articles.title: U.S. House Oversight Committee criticises Trump administration over release of Epstein records
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and President Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act

The Republican-led House Oversight Committee slammed the Trump administration on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) for botching the public release of millions of pages of records relating to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.

In a report scrutinising the government’s handling of criminal investigations of Epstein and his longtime confidant Ghislaine Maxwell, the committee faulted President Donald Trump and the Justice Department for reneging on a promise to open the files, which led Congress to pass a law forcing their release.

After Congress stepped in, the administration missed disclosure deadlines and concealed names of alleged co-conspirators while failing to adequately protect victims, “including through deficient redactions that exposed their sensitive information,” the report said.

The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and Mr. Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which requires the Justice Department to publicly disclose records relating to the late sex offender, many of which were previously confidential. The report also comes on the heels of last week’s midterm elections, when Republicans suffered heavy House losses in failing to hold their majority after a campaign where the release of government records related to Epstein became a recurring campaign issue.

“The Trump administration has repeatedly committed to releasing Epstein-related files,” the report said. “However, multiple shortcomings related to releasing documents and failures to adequately communicate about those releases plagued the DOJ’s efforts.”

Democrats used the Trump administration’s handling of the files to accuse Republicans of protecting the wealthy and well-connected, suggesting Trump’s past relationship with Epstein exposed him to potential unethical activity. The report stated, “Trump’s lack of involvement is confirmed by numerous lines of testimony in interviews or depositions with various individuals.”

The Justice Department released the bulk of the so-called Epstein files in December and January. In all, more than 3 million pages of documents were disclosed, along with more than 2,000 videos and 180,000 images. Then-Attorney General Pam Bondi’s handling of the Epstein files contributed to her firing in April.

The records included documents concerning Epstein’s famous associates, including Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly known as Britain’s Prince Andrew, and email correspondence between Epstein and Elon Musk and other prominent contacts from across the political spectrum.

More than 350 different ads mentioning Epstein aired since Labour Day for Republican and Democratic candidates running in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. Ads from Democratic-aligned groups claimed Republican candidates voted against releasing the Epstein files, while candidates from both parties accused each other of taking donations from associates of the convicted sex offender.

The report also examined how federal authorities investigated Epstein nearly two decades ago but failed to bring charges after multiple underage girls told police and the FBI that they had been paid to give Epstein sexualised massages.

U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli ⁠attacks on Lebanon during the war have ⁠killed thousands and displaced millions. American and Israeli attacks have also ‌killed top Iranian officials, including the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

articles.title: U.S. Senate Republicans vote to keep John Thune as leader after steep midterm election losses
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: South Dakota Sen. John Thune has spent much of the last two years navigating President Trump, who has often been at odds with the Senate

U.S. Senate Republicans reelected South Dakota Sen. John Thune as their leader on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) after a tense day of private discussions about steep losses in the midterm elections that cost them their majority.

Mr. Thune was always expected to prevail, as he is popular with his GOP colleagues and was running unopposed in the secret-ballot election. But Senate Republicans vented their frustrations in three separate meetings on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) after an election wipeout that cost them at least seven Senate seats.

Some Republicans had tried to delay the leadership decision, but the conference voted 31-15 to proceed. Wisconsin Sen. Ron Johnson led the effort to postpone and walked out when it failed. The closed-door meetings were held in the small Old Senate Chamber with few aides in attendance.
As the conference debated earlier in the day, West Virginia Sen. Jim Justice said “we want to be thoughtful and do the right thing.”
He said there was a “legitimate argument that, good gracious, if we lost as badly as we lost, why would we continue on with the same leadership?”
At the same time, the current GOP leadership “didn't cause this problem to happen,” Justice said. “They do a good job.”

Republicans' angst and indecision come as frustrated Republicans are just beginning to reckon with what the election results mean for their future — and for their relationship with President Donald Trump, as voters resoundingly rejected their two years of single-party rule in Congress and the White House. Two additional Senate races remain uncalled in Alaska and Mississippi that could further deplete their numbers.

“I just think that we've got a lot of things that we've got to think through, and I think that to just rush into this and just ratify all of the same leadership, what message does that send?” Missouri Sen. Josh Hawley told reporters after the first meeting.

“If you don't think after losing seven Senate seats minimum that we need to change course, I don't know what planet you're on,” said Mr. Hawley, who voted to delay the elections. He said he wasn't aware of anyone else running for leader, but “maybe there would be” if they waited.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 11 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 U.S. Senate Republicans vote to keep John Thune as leader after steep midterm election losses

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

South Dakota Sen. John Thune has spent much of the last two years navigating President Trump, who has often been at odds with the Senate

U.S. Senate Republicans reelected South Dakota Sen. John Thune as their leader on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) after a tense day of private discussions about steep losses in the midterm elections that cost them their majority.

Mr. Thune was always expected to prevail, as he is popular with his GOP colleagues and was running unopposed in the secret-ballot election. But Senate Republicans vented their frustrations in three separate meetings on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) after an election wipeout that cost them at least seven Senate seats.

Some Republicans had tried to delay the leadership decision, but the conference voted 31-15 to proceed. Wisconsin Sen. Ron Johnson led the effort to postpone and walked out when it failed. The closed-door meetings were held in the small Old Senate Chamber with few aides in attendance.

As the conference debated earlier in the day, West Virginia Sen. Jim Justice said “we want to be thoughtful and do the right thing.”

He said there was a “legitimate argument that, good gracious, if we lost as badly as we lost, why would we continue on with the same leadership?”

At the same time, the current GOP leadership “didn't cause this problem to happen,” Justice said. “They do a good job.”

Republicans' angst and indecision come as frustrated Republicans are just beginning to reckon with what the election results mean for their future — and for their relationship with President Donald Trump, as voters resoundingly rejected their two years of single-party rule in Congress and the White House. Two additional Senate races remain uncalled in Alaska and Mississippi that could further deplete their numbers.

“I just think that we've got a lot of things that we've got to think through, and I think that to just rush into this and just ratify all of the same leadership, what message does that send?” Missouri Sen. Josh Hawley told reporters after the first meeting.

“If you don't think after losing seven Senate seats minimum that we need to change course, I don't know what planet you're on,” said Mr. Hawley, who voted to delay the elections. He said he wasn't aware of anyone else running for leader, but “maybe there would be” if they waited.

Others said Mr. Thune wasn't the problem. “I don't think it was the fault of our leadership, quite frankly," said West Virginia Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, who was reelected to her leadership position as GOP policy chair.

articles.title: U.S. judge says Trump’s $10 billion BBC defamation case can proceed
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Kuntz in Florida declined to throw out Mr. Trump’s defamation ​claim against the BBC, ‌saying Mr. Trump had plausibly alleged that the broadcaster damaged his reputation and knew or should have known the clip was misleading

A federal judge on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said U.S. President Donald ​Trump’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC over a ‌misleadingly edited clip of a speech can go forward, ​but threw out Mr. Trump’s unfair trade ⁠practices claim against the broadcaster.

Mr. Trump is suing Britain’s publicly funded broadcaster for at least $10 billion over edited clips of a speech ‌that made it appear he directed supporters to storm the U.S. Capitol on January 6, ‌2021. The case is one of several ‌Mr. Trump ⁠has privately filed against the news media as ⁠part of a wider pressure campaign against coverage he dislikes.

U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Kuntz in Florida declined to throw out Mr. Trump’s defamation ​claim against the BBC , ‌saying Mr. Trump had plausibly alleged that the broadcaster damaged his reputation and knew or should have known the clip was misleading. Judge Kuntz’s ruling did not decide ‌whether Mr. Trump has proven those claims.
Mr. Trump called the ​ruling a “huge victory” in a social media post. “We will continue fighting against, and defeating, ⁠all of those who try to deceive the American People!” he wrote.
The BBC did not immediately respond to ‌a request for comment.
The BBC previously admitted the edits were misleading and apologised to Mr. Trump, though it denies being liable for defamation.

Mr. Trump’s lawsuit, filed in December in Florida federal court, accuses the BBC of defaming him by splicing together parts of the speech, including one ‌section where he told supporters to march on the Capitol ​and another where he said “fight like hell”. It omitted a section in which he called ⁠for peaceful protest.

The edited speech appeared in a BBC “Panorama” documentary show ⁠shortly before the 2024 presidential election, which Mr. Trump won. A leaked internal BBC memo cited ‌the edits as evidence of potential political bias, sparking a public relations crisis for the broadcaster and ​leading to high-level resignations.

fullParagraphs: Incident took place on Deepavali night in Baghpat; efforts on by three police teams to nab two accused who remain at large
A man posted as Army jawan in the Rashtrapati Bhavan security was allegedly shot by two neighbours following an old rivalry in Uttar Pradesh ’s Baghpat district on Deepavali night.

Saurabh Tomar (26), serving in the elite President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, underwent surgery at a private hospital in Meerut and is said to be stable. The bullet struck Mr. Tomar just behind the ear, the police said. His brother also suffered serious head injuries after being attacked with a stick.
The police have registered a case at Ramala police station against two accused and formed three police teams to arrest them, who remained at large.

A resident of the village, Mr. Tomar was recruited in 2021 and is currently posted at the Rashtrapati Bhavan. He was visiting the village on leave to celebrate Deepavali. On Sunday night (November 8, 2026), he was bursting firecrackers outside his home along with his brothers Vineet and Mintu when an argument allegedly broke out with two villagers, Dheeraj and his brother Monu alias Praveen.

“On 08.11.2026 at 9:45 p.m., Ramala police station received information that in village Gopalpur Khadana, Monu alias Praveen and Dheeraj, residents of the same village, fired a shot which ricocheted off the wall and hit the plaintiff’s son Saurabh (serving in Rashtrapati Bhavan security), injuring him. Vineet was also hit on the head with a stick and injured,” a statement by the Baghpat police read.

The complaint was filed by the Mr. Tomar’s father Janak Raj. “On receiving the information, Ramala police station immediately registered an FIR. Saurabh is undergoing treatment in a Meerut hospital. Both are in normal condition. Based on the complaint of the plaintiff/father Janak Raj, a case has been registered at Ramala police station. Three police teams have been formed to arrest the accused, and efforts are being made by them to arrest them,” the statement added.
The President's Bodyguard is the oldest and senior-most cavalry regiment in the Indian Army, stationed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

Incident took place on Deepavali night in Baghpat; efforts on by three police teams to nab two accused who remain at large

A man posted as Army jawan in the Rashtrapati Bhavan security was allegedly shot by two neighbours following an old rivalry in Uttar Pradesh ’s Baghpat district on Deepavali night.

Saurabh Tomar (26), serving in the elite President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, underwent surgery at a private hospital in Meerut and is said to be stable. The bullet struck Mr. Tomar just behind the ear, the police said. His brother also suffered serious head injuries after being attacked with a stick.

The police have registered a case at Ramala police station against two accused and formed three police teams to arrest them, who remained at large.

A resident of the village, Mr. Tomar was recruited in 2021 and is currently posted at the Rashtrapati Bhavan. He was visiting the village on leave to celebrate Deepavali. On Sunday night (November 8, 2026), he was bursting firecrackers outside his home along with his brothers Vineet and Mintu when an argument allegedly broke out with two villagers, Dheeraj and his brother Monu alias Praveen.

“On 08.11.2026 at 9:45 p.m., Ramala police station received information that in village Gopalpur Khadana, Monu alias Praveen and Dheeraj, residents of the same village, fired a shot which ricocheted off the wall and hit the plaintiff’s son Saurabh (serving in Rashtrapati Bhavan security), injuring him. Vineet was also hit on the head with a stick and injured,” a statement by the Baghpat police read.

The complaint was filed by the Mr. Tomar’s father Janak Raj. “On receiving the information, Ramala police station immediately registered an FIR. Saurabh is undergoing treatment in a Meerut hospital. Both are in normal condition. Based on the complaint of the plaintiff/father Janak Raj, a case has been registered at Ramala police station. Three police teams have been formed to arrest the accused, and efforts are being made by them to arrest them,” the statement added.

The President's Bodyguard is the oldest and senior-most cavalry regiment in the Indian Army, stationed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

articles.title: Several coaches of Sairang-Kolkata Express train derails at Digaru in Assam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: No injuries reported so far; loco pilot failed to control train’s speed while giving precedence to another train, authorities said

Several coaches of Kolkata-Sairang Express train derailed at Digaru railway station in Assam early Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after the loco pilot failed to control the train’s speed while giving precedence to another train.
All passengers are safe and no injuries were reported, Northeast Frontier Railway said.

#WATCH | Assam: A locomotive and five coaches of the Kolkata-Sairang Express (Train No. 13125) derailed at Digaru Railway Station in Kamrup (Metro) district at around 6:54 am today. According to Northeast Frontier Railway, all passengers are safe, and no injuries have been reported. Passengers are being transported to their destinations by an alternative train. Relief and rescue operations have been launched. (Visuals from the spot)

The train, enroute to Kolkata from Sairang near Mizoram’s Aizawl, derailed near Digaru railway station in Kamrup (Metropolitan) district around 6.54 a.m., resulting in the derailment of six coaches, including the locomotive.
Relief and rescue operations are under way, the Indian Railways zone said, adding that passengers are being taken to their destinations by an alternate train.
The exact cause of derailment is yet to be ascertained.

articles.title: ECI got grave, sensitive objection on registration of Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De), Delhi HC told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ECI said when the commission issued reminders to the CEO, Punjab to expedite the field verification reports, the CEO submitted a positive verification report in April which was under active consideration

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has told the Delhi High Court that it received a "grave and highly sensitive" inputs against the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) and that the outfit's registration as a political party may adversely affect the country's sovereignty and integrity.

The ECI said while the issue of registration of the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) was under consideration, the commission received a "sensitive" input in July that the outfit is rooted in "separatism", was founded by individuals detained under the National Security Act (NSA) and poses grave concerns regarding its allegiance to the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.

It said while the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Punjab gave a positive verification report about the organisation on April 27, 2026, the objection about the outfit's "separatist roots" was received on July 9 2026, and the CEO was then instructed to conduct a "comprehensive background inquiry" and furnish a detailed report.
The report of the inquiry is yet to be received, the ECI said.
The submissions were made by the ECI in two separate affidavits filed before Justice Saurabh Banerjee who has now listed the matter for consideration on January 11, 2027.

The affidavits were filed by the ECI in response to a petition by Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) seeking to direct the poll body to decide the January 22, 2025 application of the party in a time bound manner with an outer limit of one week.
The outfit has sought to approve the proposed name 'Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De)' and register it as a political party.

The Waris Punjab De was founded by late Deep Sandhu and later headed by jailed Khadoor Sahib MP Amritpal Singh. In January 2025, Singh's father and Faridkot MP Sarabjit Singh Khalsa announced the formation of a new political party, Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De).
Legislative Assembly elections are due in Punjab in February 2027.

The ECI, in its affidavits, said it received the petitioner's application for registration of the party on January 22, 2025 and after a detailed scrutiny, issued a deficiency letter in September last. It said while the petitioner was granted 30 days to cure the defects, it submitted the rectified documents in January this year, causing an inordinate delay of over four months.

articles.title: Domestic rooftop solar installations in T.N. remain low due to policy challenges, say consumers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A.D. Thirumurthi, advisor of the National Solar Energy Federation of India, says the consumers should be exempted from network charges for rooftop solar

With 425.61 MW of domestic rooftop solar installations in Tamil Nadu that have benefited from the PM Surya Ghar scheme, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation is taking efforts to bring more households under rooftop solar.
However, industry and consumer representatives say the State government should address a couple of basic policy issues so that more households go in for rooftop solar.

“While the government advertisements claim that consumers will get to pay nothing as bi-monthly energy charges if they instal rooftop solar, in reality, they have to pay network charges,” says K. Kathirmathiyon, secretary of Coimbatore Consumer Cause.

A.D. Thirumurthi, advisor of the National Solar Energy Federation of India, says the consumers should be exempted from network charges for rooftop solar. Further, in the case of additional solar energy generated in a financial year that goes unused, the consumers should be paid at least the average power purchase cost for the excess solar energy they feed to the grid.

Mr. Kathirmathiyon explained that if a consumer instals a five KW rooftop solar and his bi-monthly consumption is 500-550 units, he will supply the excess to the grid. He does not get any payment for the additional power. Instead, he will have to pay nearly ₹5,800 annually as network charges. Why should a consumer pay for solar energy that he has generated and not consumed, he asks.

“Tamil Nadu should adopt an approach similar to Kerala instead of allowing surplus electricity credits to lapse without compensation. Network charges applicable to domestic rooftop solar investors under the TNERC tariff framework with effect from October 22, 2021 constitute another major disincentive,” he says.

The Government and the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission should ensure domestic rooftop solar power producer/consumer is paid for the surplus electricity remaining unadjusted at the end of the settlement period (31st March). It should also withdraw network/wheeling charges levied on domestic rooftop solar power producers.
Mr. Thirumurthi says residents who consume more than 500 units of electricity in two months stand to benefit more if they go in for solar. The government should take steps to encourage them, he said.

articles.title: Thomas Markle sent back to jail after cutting off his ankle bracelet
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. Magistrate Judge ⁠Lindsay Griffin found that the father-in-law of Prince Harry had violated the terms of his pretrial release and ordered him returned to federal custody without bond at a hearing in Tampa, Florida, court records showed

Thomas Markle, an accused child sexual predator and the estranged father of Britain’s Duchess of ‌Sussex Meghan Markle, was sent back to jail on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) after cutting off an electronic ​ankle monitor he was ordered to wear as a condition of home confinement.

U.S. Magistrate Judge ⁠Lindsay Griffin found that the father-in-law of Prince Harry had violated the terms of his pretrial release and ordered him returned to federal custody without bond at a hearing in Tampa, Florida, court records showed.

Thomas Markle, 82, had been arrested and charged on Friday (November 6, 2026) with a ‌single federal count of possessing child sexual abuse material, including two explicit photographs of himself posed with a naked underage girl and other images of him with children in various stages of undress.

According ‌to an FBI affidavit filed in court as part of the criminal complaint lodged against him, one of ‌the ⁠photos showed a naked girl in a room that appears to be part of a ⁠motel chain in the Philippines, where Markle previously resided and where authorities initiated an investigation of him last month.
The affidavit says federal agents seized the material in question, including photographic slides, film negatives and books, from two storage units Markle had rented in Los Angeles since 2008.
Commenting on the case ​on Friday (November 6, 2026), FBI Director Kash Patel said Markle “targeted ‌innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions.”

Markle, who most recently resided at an assisted-living facility in Lakeland, Florida, near Tampa, denied possessing sexually explicit photos of children when such allegations first surfaced, telling the Daily Mail they were untrue and “sick lies.”

No plea was entered during Markle’s initial court hearing last ‌Friday, and the judge permitted him to be released from custody on condition that he submit ​to home detention and the wearing of an electronic monitoring device.
But federal prosecutors said they asked the judge to revoke home-release and keep him locked up pending trial after he was found ⁠to have cut the ankle bracelet off early Monday morning.

Agreeing that Markle’s housing situation had “become untenable,” Griffin granted prosecutors’ request. Markle was then re-arrested and returned to federal custody, according to the US Attorney’s Office in Los Angeles, where the ‌case against him was brought.

fullParagraphs: Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table

Top U.S. diplomat Marco Rubio said on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) that he saw no need to attack Iran again, as diplomatic efforts to end the war gathered steam and Tehran urged Washington to accept its demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Hours after President Donald Trump said he saw "positive momentum" towards resolving the eight-month war, Mr/ Rubio said the United States' squeezing of Iran's economy made further attacks unnecessary.

"The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations," the Secretary of State said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. "That's what I told our allies here today."

Iran's efforts to blockade Hormuz, the major exit route for Gulf energy shipments, have sent oil prices soaring — a major factor in the humbling of Mr. Trump's Republicans in last week's midterm elections.

Washington has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and in August announced what it called an "economic asphyxiation" campaign aimed at financially strangling Iran, already battered by years of sanctions.

Britain's Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called for greater efforts to end the conflict, while warning of the economic damage of an ongoing impasse. "We need to move beyond the 'no war, no peace' stalemate, which is causing deep economic pain for our countries," he said in Paris.
"We must see an all-out diplomatic effort to end this conflict, prevent a nuclear Iran and the threats it poses around the world, and get the Strait of Hormuz properly reopened."

Washington has appeared to taper down its threats of renewed strikes after the Republicans' defeat, and even Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — who launched the war alongside Trump and recently lobbied to "forever eliminate the existential threat of Iran" — appeared to recognise the shifting diplomatic reality.

"In the very near future, we're going to be confronted by international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the preservation of this terror regime that seeks to annihilate us," he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table.

articles.title: World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: COP31 host Turkiye is championing a voluntary initiative to accelerate the electrification of transport, buildings and industry, with a target of raising electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035

World leaders will take the stage at COP31 in Turkiye on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) but some prominent names are missing from this year’s annual UN climate summit even as global warming intensifies.

The two-week conference kicked off earlier this week in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, with governments under pressure to tackle the climate crisis after a year of heatwaves in Europe, deadly floods in Nepal and major wildfires in Indonesia.

Dozens of leaders will speak during the “high-level segment” taking place on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) and Thursday (November 12, 2026), including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian.
But observers have pointed to the absence of some big names, with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham the only leader from a G7 country scheduled to address the summit.

While European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen is coming to Antalya, French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni are skipping the event.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi are also absent from the most recent list.
“It is a shame that some of the bigger European leaders aren’t coming. We need Europe to be showing up strongly at this COP,” Cosima Cassel, a climate diplomacy expert at think-tank E3G, told AFP .
Wopke Hoekstra, the EU’s top climate official, said the absences were “not completely atypical” as leaders may have “practical” reasons for not being able to attend a summit.
But he also told reporters in Brussels that “expectations are not necessarily high” for this climate conference.
The French government said Mr. Macron would be absent because November 11 is World War I Armistice Day and the President will attend an EU summit in Ireland on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

fullParagraphs: The bus collided with 32 vehicles before slamming into a median strip, fire officials said

A commuter bus struck more than 30 vehicles stopped at a traffic light during the morning rush hour on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) in Seongnam, just south of Seoul, injuring dozens of people, fire officials in South Korea said.

At least 57 people were being treated for injuries, including nine who were seriously hurt, although none were in life-threatening condition, according to the fire department of Gyeonggi Province, which governs Seongnam.

The bus collided with 32 vehicles before slamming into a median strip, fire officials said. Photos from the scene showed the bus perched on a median strip with a shattered windshield and other damaged cars.

Police were questioning the bus driver, who tested negative in a breathalyzer test and told investigators that the brakes had failed, according to Park Chang-gon, an official from Seongnam's Bundang district police station.

The talks ‌in Abu Dhabi are the first three-sided discussions to be held since February. Mr. Zelenskyy described the first day as constructive and substantive.

“We are all very cautious with this topic because nobody really understands 100% what they want. I think ‌we understand, but nobody saw the documents, what the Americans discussed with the Russians,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.

He said the idea was first raised by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2021 and the administration of President Joe Biden at the time was cautious about it as the sequence of what had to be done first was ‌important.

“Everybody is ready for dialogue. First, stop the war in Ukraine. Second, ​security guarantees for Ukraine. Third, maybe some dialogue about the topic of security in Europe, in the world,” Mr. Zelenskyy ⁠said.
Earlier, Mr. Lavrov had said Moscow would not agree to an immediate ceasefire without knowing what would happen next.
He ‌said it would be wiser to discuss the outlines of the future security architecture in Europe first, and then a ceasefire ​in Ukraine.

fullParagraphs: US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation

Revelations that Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen ​Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker’s board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for ‌the company and concerns about the board’s ability to investigate its CEO independently.

Among corporate leaders, “There have definitely been affair scandals and ​sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No,” said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

Lipton was using a ⁠term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.

US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation “regarding the national security concerns raised ‌in news reports,” according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.

The stakes are high. While it is not clear if Huang violated the company’s code of conduct or what penalties Huang could face, its bylaws allow his removal “with ‌or without cause” by the vote of a majority of directors.
The company’s advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI ‌superiority. ⁠China’s Foreign Ministry called the spying claim “a groundless accusation, slander and a smear.”
Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as ⁠close ties to Trump. Huang owns 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.
Shares in Nvidia were down 6% on Tuesday, extending their losses from Monday over fallout from Huang’s affair.

Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three ​independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark ‌Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.
The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple’s Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.

articles.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4 trillion
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers

Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, in a listing that could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion.
The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers and is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.

The maker of the Claude AI models said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 each. The shares will trade under the ticker "ANT."
Seven tech companies including Google, Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft have also agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares at the IPO price in a separate private placement, the filing showed.
The companies are investors in Anthropic or major suppliers of its computing power.
Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would have made it the largest IPO on record.
Even at the top of its price range, the offering would fall short of the record set by Elon Musk's SpaceX, which raised $86 billion in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.
Anthropic has been aiming to go public the week of November 16, and reports said its shares would begin trading on November 19.

Anthropic's listing is "just another chapter" in investors' worries over the cost of the AI buildout and how it gets financed, Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management, told AFP.

"But at the end of the day, I think there are three massive companies that investors have wanted to be part of for the last three years and that's SpaceX for sure, Anthropic is next, and perhaps next year OpenAI," he said.

articles.title: RSS activist seeks FIR against Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge over arms seizure post
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The complainant alleged that the Minister’s statements and insinuations created an impression that the RSS was connected to criminal activities, potentially triggering hostility and disturbing communal harmony

A city-based RSS activist has lodged a police complaint against Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge at the Banashankari police station, seeking the registration of an FIR over an alleged social media post linking the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to a major seizure of arms and ammunition.

The complaint was submitted on November 10, 2026 by Tejas A. Gowda, a Bengaluru resident and RSS activist. He accused Mr. Kharge of allegedly circulating “misleading” information through his official X handle and attempting to disturb social harmony by associating the RSS with the seizure of around 44,250 live cartridges in Bihar and Haryana.

In his complaint, Mr. Gowda alleged that the Minister’s statements and insinuations created an impression that the RSS was connected to criminal activities, potentially triggering hostility and disturbing communal harmony.
He has sought action against theMminister under Sections 192, 196 and 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.
“Holding a constitutional office does not confer immunity from criminal law,” Mr. Gowda stated, urging the police to act independently and without political interference.

The complainant has also requested the police to preserve electronic records of the social media posts, obtain details of the ammunition seizure cases from police authorities in Bihar and Haryana, and investigate whether misleading information was knowingly disseminated.

The massive seizure of 44,250 live cartridges in Bihar and Haryana has exposed a serious interstate ammunition-smuggling network. This is not an ordinary criminal case. This is a grave national security concern. Even more disturbing are reports and photographs allegedly showing individuals implicated in the racket wearing RSS uniforms. The RSS and BJP owe the nation some answers. 1. WHAT IS THE RSS CONNECTION? Photographs reportedly show accused individuals in RSS uniforms. Were these individuals RSS Swayamsevaks? What positions did they hold in the organisation? If they were Swayamsevaks, what was their involvement in the ammunition racket? What was their intent? Who were they working for? 2. WHERE WERE 44,250 LIVE CARTRIDGES HEADED? This is enough ammunition to facilitate violence on a massive scale. Who were the intended recipients? Were these cartridges destined for organised criminal networks, extremist groups or other unlawful activities? 3. HOW DID GOVERNMENT-MANUFACTURED AMMUNITION ENTER THE ILLEGAL MARKET? Reports indicate that the seized cartridges bore markings associated with the Khadki ammunition factory in Pune. Who facilitated the diversion of this ammunition? Which licensed arms dealers and intermediaries were involved? How long has this network been operating, and how extensive is it? 4. WHY ARE THE BJP AND RSS SILENT? The BJP never misses an opportunity to lecture the country on nationalism, patriotism and national security. Yet, when individuals allegedly associated with RSS come under scrutiny in a massive ammunition-smuggling investigation, where is the outrage? Where is the accountability? 5. THIS IS PRECISELY WHY THE RSS MUST BE REGISTERED! An organisation cannot claim millions of Swayamsevaks when it suits its interests and conveniently disown individuals when serious criminal allegations emerge. Registration and proper membership records would strengthen accountability and make organisational associations easier to verify. The RSS demands accountability from everyone else. Why should it be exempt from the same scrutiny? @DrMohanBhagwat ji, I would be more than happy to personally facilitate the RSS's registration and even pay the registration fees myself.
Copies of posts from Mr. Kharge’s X account and another social media handle titled ‘Fact Myths’ were enclosed with the complaint.
Police acknowledged receiving the complaint, but no FIR had been registered at the time of reporting. Mr Kharge is yet to issue a statement on the matter.

articles.title: No, Periyar did not quit Congress in 1925
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Contrary to popular version, ‘Periyar’ E.V. Ramasamy did not leave the Congress at least for the next six or seven months, according to a perusal of reports published by this newspaper in the 1920s

It is generally believed and recorded by several scholars that one of the prominent non-Brahmin leaders, E.V. Ramasamy (EVR), known as Periyar among his admirers and followers, left the Congress in November 1925 at the famous Kancheepuram conference. [In those days, his surname - Naicker - was mentioned in every news item that The Hindu carried about him]. But, contrary to this popular version, EVR did not leave the Congress at least for the next six or seven months, according to a perusal of news items published by this newspaper in the 1920s. The Hindu too had reported EVR’s protest at the meet, an incident of which had been captured even in the shoulder - “MR. E.V. RAMASWAMI NAICKER WALKS OUT” - of the news item, titled “THE TAMIL NADU CONFERENCE,” published on November 23, 1925.

Even Eugene F. Irschick, a historian from the U.S., who specialised in the origins and the early phase of the non-Brahmin or Dravidian movement, in his 1969 work - Politics and Social Conflict in South India - stated (pages 272-273) that Periyar had left the Congress “by the end of 1925.” However, 17 years later, when his another work - Tamil Revivalism in the 1930s – was published, the veteran historian changed the year of Periyar’s exit to 1927 (page 90).
Tamil Nadu InFocus / Tamil Nadu / Indian National Congress / politics / parties and movements

articles.title: Russian paraglider trapped in power lines, rescued in Himachal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Russian paraglider in Himachal Pradesh's Mandi, who got entangled in high-tension electricity wires over 100 metres above the ground, was rescued after a 3-hour-long operation on Tuesday (November 11, 2026), police said.
The incident occurred near Tandu, when Alexey (48) took off from Bir Billing and got stuck in the wires mid-flight.

Following the incident, he immediately sent pictures of his location to the Bir Billing Paragliding Association to seek help. The association then alerted the district administration and dispatched rescue teams to the location.

The rescue operation was jointly carried out by the teams of the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Gawar Company.

Considering the potential danger of falling, the teams also laid nets and mattresses on the road. Machinery, including a crane, was used to rescue the pilot. He was safely rescued following a three-hour-long rescue operation.
He was taken to the Zonal hospital in Mandi, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Chander Prakash said.

fullParagraphs: LAB and KDA are demanding postponement of hill council elections to April-May next year, citing unfavourable winter timing and lack of consultation

The story so far: The Lieutenant Governor-led administration of Ladakh has announced back-to-back elections in the Union Territory. The three-tier polls — hill councils, panchayat and municipal elections — will be held in the next one month. While the panchayat and municipal elections are slated for November 21, the hill council elections will be held on December 4.

Ladakh is a U.T. without a legislature. So, these elections are key to provide platforms to public representatives in the region. However, the short window provided by the State Election Commission (SEC) is likely to make it hard for political parties to chart the course for their campaigning and enter into possible alliances.

articles.title: Keralam Minister’s claim on Muslim Youth League’s role in Netanyahu’s Israel defeat invites online ridicule
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Referring to alleged massacres in Israel, K.M. Shaji said Youth League workers from Malappuram, Kasaragod and Ernakulam had contributed to Netanyahu being forced to step down
Mr. Shaji, Minister for Local Self-Government, made the remarks while addressing a State-level meeting of the Youth League, the youth wing of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), in Kochi recently.
Referring to the alleged massacres in Israel, the Minister said Youth League workers from Malappuram, Kasaragod and Ernakulam had contributed to Mr. Netanyahu being forced to step down.

“You should understand that the Youth League workers in Malappuram, Kasaragod and Ernakulam had a role in Netanyahu being forced to step down,” he said, referring to their social media campaigns and protests against Israel.

He also highlighted the campaigns conducted by the organisation across different parts of the world, saying, “The campaigns you carried out through social media and the protests you organised against Israel wherever possible across the world” had made a difference.”
Mr. Shaji further said the development should be seen as a lesson, and that it was also part of the setbacks suffered by right-wing forces in several countries.
His remarks triggered a flood of trolls and memes on social media platforms.

One netizen sarcastically claimed that the new Israeli Prime Minister had invited the Muslim League to join his ministry, while another mocked the minister, saying the IUML and Youth League had voting rights in Israel.
However, some social media users defended Mr. Shaji, arguing that there was nothing wrong with his statement as he had only spoken about the influence of social media campaigns and interventions.

articles.title: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan back in jail after medical treatment, sources say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Imran Khan had an eye check-up at the Pakistan Institute of Medical ‌Sciences, one of the officials said
Pakistan’s former Prime Minister Imran Khan ​was taken to hospital in Islamabad late on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) ‌for medical treatment and returned to ​prison, sources said.
Khan, who is ⁠imprisoned in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, had an eye check-up at the Pakistan Institute of Medical ‌Sciences (PIMS), one of the officials said on Wednesday (November 11).
“He had some blood ‌pressure issues ... and was given required treatment ‌last ⁠night. He has been shifted ⁠back to his prison cell,” the person said.

The cricketer-turned-politician has faced multiple corruption charges since he lost power ​in a no-confidence vote ‌in 2022, and has been in prison for more than three years. All of Khan’s convictions bar one have been suspended ‌or overturned, with appeals pending. He ​denies wrongdoing and says the charges are politically motivated, a claim the government ⁠denies.
Khan’s lawyers say the 74-year-old’s health has deteriorated in prison and that he has ‌lost significant vision in his right eye.
It is the first known instance of Khan being taken to hospital for treatment and returned to jail since August, when his hospital visit was cut short.
A Pakistani ‌court has also ordered jail authorities to allow Khan’s ​legal team to see him and his wife, his party said.
His ⁠party’s deputy chairman, Shah Mehmood Qureshi, was also taken ⁠to hospital in the eastern city of Lahore from a jail ‌in the same city on Tuesday (November 10). He remains in hospital.

articles.title: Why Jamaica’s reparations petition has a solid legal basis
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The petition asks whether the enslavement of Africans in Jamaica violated international law

Led by Culture Minister Olivia Grange, the Jamaican government filed a petition on September 7, 2026, asking King Charles III of England — who is Jamaica’s Head of State — to refer three core legal questions to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (JCPC) under Section 4 of the Judicial Committee Act 1833. The questions ask whether the capture, transportation, and enslavement of Africans in Jamaica were ever lawful under English common law, whether those acts violated international legal principles, and whether the U.K. holds a legal obligation to provide reparatory remedies or compensation to the Jamaican people.

While the petition is pending, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently stated that while the British government is open to formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the transatlantic slave trade, he ruled out financial reparations, arguing that the contemporary British populace cannot be held liable for historical wrongs from a different era and legal context. However, a closer look reveals that Jamaica’s petition possesses far more legal weight than a cosmetic apology.

articles.title: Tech consultant sentenced to 16 years to life in stabbing death of Cash App founder Bob Lee
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A jury in December 2024 found Nima Momeni guilty of second-degree murder, rejecting the defendant's claim that he had acted in self-defense
The tech consultant convicted in the stabbing death of Cash App founder Bob Lee was sentenced in San Francisco on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) to 16 years to life to prison.

A jury in December 2024 found Nima Momeni guilty of second-degree murder, rejecting the defendant's claim that he had acted in self-defense. He has remained in custody since his arrest nine days after the April 4, 2023, killing.
Before imposing the sentence, San Francisco Superior Court Judge Alexandra Gordon rejected Momeni's request for a new trial. His attorneys have said they plan to appeal.
Members of Lee's family addressed the court on Tuesday (November 10), including his 18-year-old daughter, Scout Lee, who spoke directly to Momeni.
“You did not just end his life, you ended an entire future built around a man,” she told Momeni, according to media reports.
Momeni, wearing an orange jail jumpsuit, maintained that he acted in self-defense. He told Lee's family that he understood their loss.
“Unfortunately, we have completely different understandings of what transpired,” Momeni said.
Lee, a renowned tech mogul, was found staggering on a deserted downtown street, dripping a trail of blood and calling for help. Lee, 43, later died at a hospital.

Prosecutors said Momeni planned the attack on Lee, driving him to an isolated spot under the Bay Bridge and stabbing him three times, including once to the heart, with a knife he took from his sister's kitchen. They said Momeni was angry with Lee for introducing his younger sister to a drug dealer she says gave her GHB and other drugs and then sexually assaulted her.

But Momeni testified on the stand that Lee was the one who attacked him with a knife, angry after the tech consultant chided him about spending more time with his family instead of searching for a strip club that night. Momeni, who studies martial arts, said he didn't realize he had fatally wounded Lee or that Lee was even hurt.

articles.title: IBM to end U.S. visa, green card sponsorship for most roles in its Consulting arm
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Workers impacted by the move can work with IBM ‌outside the U.S. or leave by the ​end of the year, a report said
IBM said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that it was ending ​U.S. visa and green ‌card sponsorship for a majority ​of roles in IBM ⁠Consulting, which employs more than 1,50,000 people.

The move comes amid ‌tight scrutiny of foreign tech hiring by Donald ‌Trump’s administration. Last month, ‌it ⁠suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several ⁠major outsourcers, including Cognizant, Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services, from the Permanent Labor ​Certification process — ‌a key step toward green cards for foreign workers.
IBM Consulting has used U.S. high-skilled ‌visa programs to address skill ​shortages, but participation has been declining for years, a ⁠company spokesperson told Reuters .
It opted to end sponsorship for ‌most such roles as skill availability and client needs have evolved, the spokesperson added.
Workers impacted by the move can work with IBM ‌outside the U.S. or leave by the ​end of the year, Bloomberg News reported earlier, ⁠citing a company document it ⁠said it had seen.
Last year, the White House ‌announced a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions.

articles.title: Three polio workers abducted during vaccination campaign in northwestern Pakistan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The gunmen took the three workers from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district to an undisclosed location after abducting them. The abducted workers were identified as Mir Janan, Ikram and Khanzala, says police
Three polio vaccination workers were abducted by unidentified armed men during an ongoing immunisation campaign in northwestern Pakistan , police said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

The gunmen took the three workers from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district to an undisclosed location after abducting them. The abducted workers were identified as Mir Janan, Ikram and Khanzala, police added.
The Tank district administration confirmed the abduction, saying that three polio workers had been taken away by unidentified armed men from the Sorghar area.
The latest incident comes amid a series of abductions and attacks targeting polio vaccination teams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

On November 2, four polio workers were abducted by unidentified armed men from Tank district's Sheikh Attar area, while two other vaccinators kidnapped from Azam Warsak in Lower South Waziristan were subsequently released.
On November 4, a polio campaign supervisor, Jalil Khan, was abducted from the Chapri area of Jamrud in Khyber district.
In a separate attack, in Mohmand district on November 3, two policemen escorting a polio vaccination team were killed, and another was injured by unidentified gunmen.
The recurring incidents have raised serious concerns over the security of frontline health workers engaged in the nationwide campaign to eradicate polio.
