articles.title: Physical pain often peaks during your working years, not in old age
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A large new study has also found that people’s pain levels varied according to their income, geography, conditions like obesity, and habits like smoking

The world’s largest, most comprehensive source of information for scientists and doctors to assess diseases and health worldwide is the Global Burden of Diseases study. Yet its dozens of parameters do not include one on a leading cause of disability worldwide: pain.

But it is too easy to blame the study for this oversight: “For pain, there are no medical biomarkers and the best we can do is to ask a person about their subjective experience,” Matthew Fillingim, a researcher at McGill University, Canada, said.

Dr. Fillingim, along with 98 researchers from 63 institutions worldwide, gathered data and studied subjective experiences of pain from 6.1 million individuals from 118 countries, aged 5-100 years, between 1995 and 2005. They recently published their findings in Nature Medicine .

articles.title: Karnataka education officials asked to evaluate pros and cons of cluster kitchen system for midday meals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This would relieve teachers of midday meal responsibilities and enable them to focus on teaching, the association has argued

Considering the request of Government Primary School Teachers’ Association, the Joint Director of the PM Poshan Shakti Nirman scheme, under the Department of School Education and Literacy (DSEL), has instructed Deputy Directors of Public Instruction (DDPIs) and Block Education Officers (BEOs) of all districts in Karnataka to examine the pros and cons of adapting “cluster kitchen centre” system to provide midday meals to government schools .

Highlighting the workload on government school teachers, the association had requested the government to open cluster kitchens rather than prepare midday meals at every individual school. The association had submitted a formal request to the Principal Secretary of the School Education Department and the Director of the PM Poshan Abhiyan.

The association has argued that teachers are already burdened with several administrative tasks, including the school enrolment abhiyan, student scholarship enrolment and registration, and updating records in the Student Achievement Tracking System (SATS), apart from maintaining attendance records in the Nirantara app. This is in addition to responsibilities related to midday meals.
Teachers are also continuously deployed for census and other non-academic duties. Around 65,000 teachers had been deployed for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka.

Under the existing system, teachers oversee the procurement of groceries, milk, greens, vegetables, eggs and bananas, besides supervising food preparation and distribution. They are also required to maintain related records on the SATS and Nirantara apps.

However, various non-governmental organisations (NGOs) such as ISKCON’s Akshaya Patra and Adamya Chetana are already supplying midday meals through cloud kitchens or cluster kitchens in Bengaluru, Hubballi and other urban centres.

Therefore, the association has proposed establishing similar cluster-level kitchen centres across the State and allocating them to associations, organisations, self-help groups or Stree Shakti Sanghas for the preparation and supply of midday meals to government schools within each cluster. “This would relieve teachers of midday meal responsibilities and enable them to focus on teaching,” the association urged.

articles.title: Illegal oocyte collection racket: 27 ART centres inspected across Telangana, notices issued to seven hospitals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The investigation also includes examining the involvement of women identified in connection with the case, doctors, IVF centres and intermediaries allegedly facilitating the activities

The Telangana Health Department has intensified its investigation into the alleged illegal oocyte (egg) collection racket, with inspections conducted at 27 of the 44 identified Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) facilities across the State. Officials have detected 13 regulatory violations in seven hospitals and issued show-cause notices to their managements.

Health Minister C. Damodar Rajanarasimha has directed the department to conduct a comprehensive investigation into alleged illegal activities being carried out under the guise of oocyte collection and initiate stringent action against institutions and individuals found violating prescribed regulations.
Acting on the Minister’s directions, task force teams have been inspecting IVF centres across the State for the past four days. Inspections at the remaining facilities are continuing.

The department said further action would be initiated after a detailed examination of records seized by the police and information obtained from the National ART and Surrogacy Registry. The investigation also includes examining the involvement of women identified in connection with the case, doctors, IVF centres and intermediaries allegedly facilitating the activities.

As part of the investigation, the Health department officials visited the National ART and Surrogacy Registry in New Delhi on November 6 and sought details of the data submitted by registered ART clinics and ART banks operating in Telangana.

The department has reiterated that oocyte collection must strictly comply with the provisions of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act and Rules. All ART clinics and ART banks operating in the State are required to obtain mandatory statutory registration and adhere to the prescribed regulatory framework.

The Health Department also cautioned women against falling prey to misleading assurances and financial inducements offered by intermediaries, warning that such arrangements could expose them to unauthorised medical procedures.

articles.title: Vijayasai Reddy launches Parivartana Rajaneethi Party, vows to end ‘two-family’ politics in Andhra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The former YSRCP leader says he will mentor young leaders as Bal Thackeray and Kanshi Ram did, and that his Parivartana Rajaneethi Party will contest all 175 Andhra Assembly seats

Former YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) Rajya Sabha member V. Vijayasai Reddy on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) launched the Parivartana Rajaneethi Party (PRP) in Vijayawada, declaring that its principal objective would be to end the dominance of two political families in Andhra Pradesh and create opportunities for a new generation of leaders.
Unveiling the party, he said its flag featured a Dharma Chakra at the centre, with white and saffron as its colours.

Former YSR Congress Party leader Vijayasai Reddy on Wednesday announced the launch of a new political party in Andhra Pradesh, named the Parivarthana Rajaneethi Party (PRP), in Vijayawada. He also unveiled the party flag, featuring white and orange colours, marking the formal announcement of the new political outfit. The launch marks his entry into a new political platform in the State. Video: G N Rao

Addressing the gathering after the launch, Mr. Vijayasai Reddy said he had founded the party in the presence of deities and called on people to bring about political change. The future of Andhra Pradesh was in the hands of its people and not any individual leader, he said.

Alleging that both the ruling and Opposition parties had failed to address people’s basic needs, he said truth, accountability and public concerns had disappeared amid political self-praise and mutual criticism. People had the right to question anyone for wrongdoing, irrespective of whether it was Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy or himself.

He said the PRP was not intended to produce another political leader but to identify and nurture leadership qualities among the youth. The party wanted a capable young person to become Chief Minister, irrespective of caste or political lineage.
“Should the Chief Minister, Ministers and MLAs come only from these two families?” he asked, arguing that political leadership should be based on people’s mandate and merit rather than inheritance.

Referring to Bal Thackeray in Maharashtra and Kanshi Ram in Uttar Pradesh, Mr. Vijayasai Reddy said he would play the role of a ‘margadarshi’ (mentor), guiding the party while encouraging younger leaders to take up political and executive responsibilities. He said his focus would be on building the organisation, nurturing grassroots leadership and providing opportunities to the younger generation.

He said every caste and social group had capable leaders who could contribute to the State’s development. Leadership positions should not be inherited but earned through public support and ability. The party would work towards ending hereditary politics and prioritise the welfare of weaker sections, he said.

Referring to his role in building the YSRCP, Mr. Vijayasai Reddy said he had worked actively for the party before leaving it. The doors of the PRP would remain open to those willing to join its political journey, he added.

articles.title: NCW chief Vijaya Rahatkar to meet Jharkhand officials over Nisha Bhagat case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: "NCW chief Vijaya Rahatkar will interact with the media at the Guest House near Ranchi University, Ranchi, following her meeting with senior police officers and the district administration regarding the Nisha Bhagat case and other cases concerning women's safety and justice," the commission said in a statement

National Commission for Women (NCW) Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar will meet senior police officers and district administration officials in Ranchi on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) to discuss the Nisha Bhagat case and other matters concerning women's safety and justice.

Bhagat, a tribal activist, was found dead on November 6 after going live on Facebook and accusing the JMM-led government in the State and land brokers of harassing her. Her parents have alleged a conspiracy behind her death and demanded a CBI probe into the incident.

"NCW chief Vijaya Rahatkar will interact with the media at the Guest House near Ranchi University, Ranchi, following her meeting with senior police officers and the district administration regarding the Nisha Bhagat case and other cases concerning women's safety and justice," the commission said in a statement.

Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren ordered a CBI probe into Bhagat's death on Tuesday (November 10), hours after the officer-in-charge of Pithoria police station was removed from his post following conspiracy allegations.
"The CBI will now investigate the Nisha Bhagat case. Orders have been issued," Mr. Soren announced on X.
On November 7, the NCW took suo motu cognisance of the case and directed the authorities to ensure a time-bound investigation and submit a detailed action-taken report within seven days.
Bhagat's mother, Devika, on Saturday (November 7) alleged that her daughter was forced to take the extreme step due to pressure and threats from tribal leader Ajay Tirkey and his associates.

articles.title: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after GOP's midterm wipeout
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: After Democrats trounced GOP and won control of the next Congress, Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party
It's business as usual for President Donald Trump 's deportation offensive despite the Republican wipeout in the midterm elections.

In Los Angeles, masked immigration officers in body armour blocked a hospital emergency room driveway in a heavily Latino neighbourhood early Saturday (November 7, 2026). In central Alabama, twin 19-year-old brothers from Venezuela were arrested while driving back to college a day after the election.
Advocates reported arrests from California to Michigan to Massachusetts.
After Democrats trounced the GOP and won control of the next Congress, Mr. Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party.
“I'd love to do something on immigration,” he said in an interview with CBS “60 Minutes” recorded Friday (November 6, 2026).

Hours later, he named Stephen Miller , the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, as his new chief of staff. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said his orders had not changed.

“Deportations will continue,” Mr. Mullin wrote in an online post the day after the election, warning that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement takes no days off and that “this includes on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Election Day.”
María Bilbao, a campaign coordinator for the American Friends Service Committee in Miami, said she has received at least one call a day from someone detained in South Florida since the election.
“Everything remains exactly the same. The arrests have not ceased at all,” Ms. Bilbao said.

Florida Highway Patrol officers and ICE agents have detained people in their cars, as well as in places including supermarkets, pharmacies and gas stations. Immigrants under supervision have also been arrested when they showed up at ICE's Miami office for their appointments.

articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Since the outbreak was declared mid-May, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to a series of factors including conflicts and a health system crisis
Congo's Ebola cases have crossed 11,000 cases in another development that shows the severity of the outbreak.

The latest Health Ministry data on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.
Since the outbreak was declared mid-May, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to a series of factors including conflicts and a health system crisis.
The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to the eight of the country's 26 Provinces.

Dozens of Ebola outbreaks have been reported since the disease was first discovered in 1976. The largest and deadliest occurred in West Africa from 2014 to 2016, with 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths.

The current outbreak already ranks second, and has had at least three times the number of cases and deaths in the time since it was declared compared with the West Africa outbreak. Health officials declared the outbreak in May, but medical evidence suggests infections were occurring months earlier.

articles.title: U.S. and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, says Scott Bessent
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said that he wanted to “build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity”

The United States and ‌China should harbor no illusions about their differences on artificial intelligence as they navigate cooperation to ​mitigate the technology’s risks while competing for Artificial Intelligence (AI) supremacy, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said ⁠on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

Mr. Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said in prepared remarks to the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations in New York that he wanted to “build ‌a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity.”

The meeting in Shenzhen, to be held on the sidelines of the November 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders summit, will advance a new bilateral ‌dialogue on “superintelligence”, or SI, Bessent said, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology.
The dialogue is meant ‌to ⁠guard against shared risks and “prevent a misunderstanding between our two systems,” Bessent said.

“We also expect ⁠to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology,” he said, adding the two sides had agreed to establish a direct channel for alerting each other to serious incidents.

Mr. Trump and /Mr. ​Xi agreed on the new AI alert ‌system during their previous meeting at the White House in September, but Trump at the time also said he was reluctant to add new guardrails because he wanted to preserve US leadership.

“As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management — and to demonstrate how two nations ‌can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership,” Mr. Bessent said.

“As we do so, we ​should harbor no illusions about the differences between the United States and China. As I stated earlier, our interests will not always coincide. And our approach to every challenge, likewise, will ⁠not always converge,” he added.

Mr. Bessent’s remarks made no mention of the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , who is facing an investigation by the AI chipmaker’s board after a New York Times report that he had an affair ‌with a businesswoman suspected by U.S. security services of being a Chinese intelligence asset.
China’s Foreign Ministry has called the spying accusations “groundless” and “a smear.”

articles.title: India’s efforts to clean its air need not slow its economic growth
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The best interventions must address air pollution while supporting development priorities. Cleaner industrial processes may reduce emissions while improving efficiency. Clean cooking can reduce household smoke while improving convenience and health. Better waste management can reduce open burning while improving urban services

India ranked 176 out of 177 countries in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI), which is published by the Yale and Columbia Universities in the U.S. The index assesses 47 indicators across 12 issue categories. Of them, India performed the worst on air quality, where it ranked 175, yet it did considerably better on air pollution, ranking 88. This contrast is illustrative: doing better at controlling select emissions does not necessarily mean the air people breathe gets better. And only the latter matters for India’s health burden.

The State of Global Air 2025 report estimated that more than 20 lakh deaths in India in 2023 could be attributed to air pollution. A Central Pollution Control Board assessment in 2012 also found lower lung function in 43.5% of Delhi schoolchildren compared to 25.7% of children in a control group.

articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U.S.-China AI race
Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang 's has global implications.

The 63-year-old is the leading face of the artificial intelligence revolution with his black leather jacket and fluff of grey hair. He runs the company Nvidia, which produces highly coveted computer chips. That's landed him on a late-night phone call with President Donald Trump , a promoter of the industry.

But Mr. Huang was also liaising with a Chinese businesswoman who has allegedly fed intelligence — as well as advanced chips — to China. The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed.

It's a saga of personal betrayal, corporate espionage and high-tech development, and the fallout is spreading across Washington. There are bipartisan calls for investigations on Capitol Hill. The U.S. Department of Justice has opened its own probe. Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, is conducting an internal review.

Some expect the technology to reshape human civilisation by imbuing computers with the vast powers of creation and analysis, and Mr. Trump has repeated that “whoever wins AI, wins." Nvidia is the backbone of America's plans for dominating the field.
When asked about Mr. Huang's affair, Mr. Trump said this week that he had spoken to the tech executive as the scandal grew.
“I think he'll be in good shape," President Trump said, adding that "he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
As for when the President first learned about the concerns involving Ms. Alice Huang, Mr. Trump brushed off the question.
“They could have been mentioned," he said. "Certainly it didn't make much of an impact on me.”
With the AI race between the U.S. and China often framed as a fierce and consequential rivalry , the Justice Department has persistently warned of the espionage threat posed by Beijing.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U.S.-China AI race

Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang 's has global implications.

The 63-year-old is the leading face of the artificial intelligence revolution with his black leather jacket and fluff of grey hair. He runs the company Nvidia, which produces highly coveted computer chips. That's landed him on a late-night phone call with President Donald Trump , a promoter of the industry.

But Mr. Huang was also liaising with a Chinese businesswoman who has allegedly fed intelligence — as well as advanced chips — to China. The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed.

It's a saga of personal betrayal, corporate espionage and high-tech development, and the fallout is spreading across Washington. There are bipartisan calls for investigations on Capitol Hill. The U.S. Department of Justice has opened its own probe. Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, is conducting an internal review.

Some expect the technology to reshape human civilisation by imbuing computers with the vast powers of creation and analysis, and Mr. Trump has repeated that “whoever wins AI, wins." Nvidia is the backbone of America's plans for dominating the field.

When asked about Mr. Huang's affair, Mr. Trump said this week that he had spoken to the tech executive as the scandal grew.

“I think he'll be in good shape," President Trump said, adding that "he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”

As for when the President first learned about the concerns involving Ms. Alice Huang, Mr. Trump brushed off the question.

“They could have been mentioned," he said. "Certainly it didn't make much of an impact on me.”

With the AI race between the U.S. and China often framed as a fierce and consequential rivalry , the Justice Department has persistently warned of the espionage threat posed by Beijing.

fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. According to AFP , Megaspeed retorted in December of the same year, saying that Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

Jensen Huang, the top boss of the chip maker and one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship with Alice Huang. The Nvidia CEO said that he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife, my actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” the statement, uploaded on Nvidia’s website added.

articles.title: Telangana seeks World Bank assistance for urban mission programme in PURE and RARE regions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The project will help local bodies finance and manage with their own resources and access market finance by strengthening Telangana Urban Finance and Infrastructure Development Corporation (TUFIDC) as financial intermediary
The Telangana Government is actively working on securing loans from multilateral agencies for financing its urban development programmes.

The government is said to be seeking the World Bank’s assistance for the Telangana Urban Transformation and Jobs Program, part of the India Municipal Finance Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA), aimed at improving municipal finance systems, strengthen governance capacity and enhance access to commercial finance. The project envisages strengthening of the institutional and financial capacity of urban local bodies including access to market finance and improving climate resilient urban infrastructure in selected cities in the State.

The project, involving an estimated US $430 million (approximately ₹4,000 crore), will have the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development extending US $300 million Programme for Results loan and US $130 million to be funded by the State Government. It will support the State Government’s urban mission programme in selected cities in the Peri-Urban Regional Economy (PURE) and Rural Agricultural Regional Economy (RARE) as part of the Telangana Rising 2047 vision. The project is likely to be approved next year.

According to information, the project will help local bodies finance and manage with their own resources and access market finance by strengthening of the Telangana Urban Finance and Infrastructure Development Corporation (TUFIDC) as financial intermediary, rewarding improvements in urban local bodies’ finances and supporting municipal bonds. It will also finance climate-resilient water supply, sanitation, drainage and public spaces, and regeneration of municipal assets including areas around heritage sites for productive economic use.

The project envisages development of an ecosystem for institutional strengthening and municipal finance aimed at ensuring that the institutions and systems allow ULBs to finance and manage urban services with their own resources. The approach would be strengthening the TUFIDC at the State level. At the ULB level, it will reward better finances, support municipal bonds and build municipal finance skills.

The project is conceived in view of the rapid growth witnessed in the secondary and peri-urban cities necessitating investment in infrastructure and services at a scale that State grants and municipal revenues alone cannot finance. Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) depend largely on State and central transfers with low own source revenues and uneven financial reporting as a result of which only few ULBs are creditworthy.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu may approach Supreme Court seeking greater powers for Cauvery Water Management Authority
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB)

Frustrated that the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) does not have the power to enforce its orders, Tamil Nadu is contemplating approaching the Supreme Court with a prayer that the Authority be given teeth.
It wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), a case of which has been mentioned in the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s report (Volume V).

Established in October 1967, the BBMB is engaged in the regulation of the supply of water and electricity from Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects to Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, and Chandigarh. The CWMA chairperson Saumitra Kumar Haldar, too, in an interaction with The Hindu in August , referred to the Tribunal’s recommendation and explained that the Board, with the chief being appointed by the Union government, “owns, operates, manages, and regulates” the projects. “They [the BBMB] take joint decisions regarding how much water is to be given and what the scheduling will be. Everything is planned,” Mr. Haldar had said.

Tamil Nadu has been complaining that despite the quantities of water release stipulated by the CWMA in the last three-odd months being inadequate and lower than the proportionate share, the upper riparian State of Karnataka has not provided water, as per the mandated releases. Of the seven spells of the 15-day water release ordered by the Authority since July 29 , Karnataka has not complied with the release in five spells, even though, cumulatively, Tamil Nadu realised about 5,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) higher than the total figure of 5.71 lakh cusecs, according to a persual of the data measured at Biligundulu on the inter-State border of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

As per the data available with the Central Water Commission, four reservoirs of Karnataka (Krishnaraja Sagara, Kabini, Hemavathi, and Harangi) registered a net cumulative inflow of about 132 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) during the period of June 1 to November 4, marking a shortfall of around 54%. The 30-year-long average net inflow was around 288 tmc ft. If the same shortfall is to be applied in the case of Tamil Nadu, the realisation should have been around 67 tmc ft between June 1 and November 4 against the quantum of approximately 145 tmc ft in a normal year. But Biligundulu received 53.43 tmc ft only with a shortfall of around 13 tmc ft. The Authority, however, has not asked Karnataka to clear the backlog, which, according to the calculations of Tamil Nadu, comes to nearly 17 tmc ft.

A senior government official says that even when the State had approached the Supreme Court seeking its intervention, the latter’s response had been to tell the former to go to the Authority. But the CWMA’s orders had not been implemented properly. “Besides, the Authority has not been able to enforce the directions. This is why we are mulling over the option of approaching the Court with this prayer,” the official adds.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 11 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Tamil Nadu may approach Supreme Court seeking greater powers for Cauvery Water Management Authority

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The State wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB)

Frustrated that the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) does not have the power to enforce its orders, Tamil Nadu is contemplating approaching the Supreme Court with a prayer that the Authority be given teeth.

It wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), a case of which has been mentioned in the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s report (Volume V).

Established in October 1967, the BBMB is engaged in the regulation of the supply of water and electricity from Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects to Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, and Chandigarh. The CWMA chairperson Saumitra Kumar Haldar, too, in an interaction with The Hindu in August , referred to the Tribunal’s recommendation and explained that the Board, with the chief being appointed by the Union government, “owns, operates, manages, and regulates” the projects. “They [the BBMB] take joint decisions regarding how much water is to be given and what the scheduling will be. Everything is planned,” Mr. Haldar had said.

Tamil Nadu has been complaining that despite the quantities of water release stipulated by the CWMA in the last three-odd months being inadequate and lower than the proportionate share, the upper riparian State of Karnataka has not provided water, as per the mandated releases. Of the seven spells of the 15-day water release ordered by the Authority since July 29 , Karnataka has not complied with the release in five spells, even though, cumulatively, Tamil Nadu realised about 5,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) higher than the total figure of 5.71 lakh cusecs, according to a persual of the data measured at Biligundulu on the inter-State border of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

As per the data available with the Central Water Commission, four reservoirs of Karnataka (Krishnaraja Sagara, Kabini, Hemavathi, and Harangi) registered a net cumulative inflow of about 132 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) during the period of June 1 to November 4, marking a shortfall of around 54%. The 30-year-long average net inflow was around 288 tmc ft. If the same shortfall is to be applied in the case of Tamil Nadu, the realisation should have been around 67 tmc ft between June 1 and November 4 against the quantum of approximately 145 tmc ft in a normal year. But Biligundulu received 53.43 tmc ft only with a shortfall of around 13 tmc ft. The Authority, however, has not asked Karnataka to clear the backlog, which, according to the calculations of Tamil Nadu, comes to nearly 17 tmc ft.

A senior government official says that even when the State had approached the Supreme Court seeking its intervention, the latter’s response had been to tell the former to go to the Authority. But the CWMA’s orders had not been implemented properly. “Besides, the Authority has not been able to enforce the directions. This is why we are mulling over the option of approaching the Court with this prayer,” the official adds.

articles.title: Auto, taxi fares in Keralam to go up from January 1; operators call off strike
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Decision taken at meeting between representatives of auto-taxi trade unions and Transport Minister C. P. John; unions have demanded that existing minimum fare of ₹30 be raised to ₹50. Panel to study proposed revision

Keralam has decided to revise auto-rickshaw and taxi fares in the State from January 1, 2027. The decision was taken at a meeting between representatives of auto-taxi trade unions and Transport Minister C. P. John in Thiruvananthapuram on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
Following the State government’s acceptance of the unions’ demand for a fare revision, the 24-hour strike called by auto-rickshaw and taxi operators for Thursday has been called off.
The unions have demanded that the existing minimum fare of ₹30 be raised to ₹50.

Speaking to the media after the meeting, Mr. John said the State government would constitute a commission to study the proposed fare revision. The unions would be given an opportunity to present their views before the commission, which would recommend the revised rates. The final decision on the extent of the fare hike would be taken based on its report, with the new rates scheduled to come into effect on January 1, the Minister said.

“Since the last fare revision was effected on April 22, 2022, the government has accepted the unions’ demand for a revision in principle and decided to constitute a commission to examine the proposal. Steps are being taken to implement the revised rates from January 1,” he told the media.

The government has also agreed to consider several other demands raised by the unions, including Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) coverage for auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers, stricter regulation of two-wheeler taxis operating without the mandatory yellow number plates, and the provision of restrooms for drivers at hotels and other locations.

The Minister said discussions had been held with the Tourism Department and hotel owners on providing rest facilities for drivers and that the government would seriously consider the proposal. Though two-wheeler taxis are permitted to operate, some were found using white number plates instead of the mandatory yellow ones. The government has decided to take steps to strictly regulate such violations, he said.

articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam book purchase row: DVAC launches probe in Tamil Nadu libraries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The issue was flagged by award-winning Tamil writer Perumal Murugan who visited the library in Coimbatore recently and pointed to issues relating to price, quality and authenticity of content in some books.

The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has launched a detailed inquiry into allegations of serious financial irregularities at Anna Centenary Library in Chennai and Periyar Arivulagam library at Coimbatore .

DVAC officers perused records in both the libraries on Monday (November 9, 2026) and Tuesday (November 10) after registering the detailed inquiry which followed a statement made by Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Rajmohan alleging that irregularities took place during the erstwhile DMK regime in the purchase of books for the newly-launched Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore.

Amidst allegations that books with AI-generated content and factual mistakes were purchased at inflated rates, DVAC officers made enquiries with the library staff and took copies of certain records in both the libraries for investigation, sources in the investigating agency said.

The issue was flagged by noted Tamil writer Perumal Murugan who visited the library in Coimbatore recently and pointed to issues relating to price, quality and authenticity of content in some books. During the search at Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore on Tuesday, DVAC sleuths scrutinised documents pertaining to book purchase in the administrative section of the library, on the third floor.
The DVAC would register a case if prima facie evidence is established in the detailed inquiry.

articles.title: Moody’s ups India’s FY27 growth estimate to 7% on broad-based momentum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said

Moody's Ratings on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience.

In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to “intensifying and broadening price pressures”, with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6% target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand.
“India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7% from 6.5%,” it said.
Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said.
A sustained private investment boom that materially boosts manufacturing, employment and productivity could lift growth rates above Moody's baseline projections.
“With the RBI on track to raise rates further, tighter monetary policy could delay the recovery in private investment,” Moody's added.

India has adjusted to the energy price shock better than previously assumed, helped by its ability to diversify crude and gas supplies and buffer consumers from the immediate price impact through state-backed oil marketing companies and tax cuts.

India is also home to the world's largest single-site refining complex, and its large and sophisticated refining capacity has helped limit fuel supply disruptions while supporting its role as a major exporter of refined petroleum products, Moody's added.

“High frequency indicators, including robust capital goods production and imports, accelerating industrial credit growth and rising capacity utilisation, suggest that India may be at the cusp of a new private capex cycle after several years of corporate and banking- sector balance sheet repair,” the U.S.-based agency said.

Broader economic activity also remains solid amid expanding manufacturing and services purchasing manager indexes and double-digit year-on-year growth in goods and services tax revenue, vehicle sales and merchandise exports, it added.

articles.title: Alice Huang, who reportedly had affair with Nvidia CEO, is Chinese banker turned tech exec
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds

She was building a career in Chinese finance before turning to tech with a leadership role at a data centre company in Singapore. He is the high-profile CEO of Nvidia, the California-based company that makes computer chips relied upon by advanced artificial intelligence systems.
An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds.
The Chinese businesswoman also known as Huang Le had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, according to reports over the past month by the New York Times.

The newspaper also reported that top policymakers were informed in a memo that intelligence indicated she was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, recruited to influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available in China.

In one widely shared photograph of the pair, Jensen Huang and people surrounding him are holding drinks in Taipei, while Alice Huang sits behind him, apparently watching him in conversation. The picture was posted in 2024 by software company NetThunder to its LinkedIn page.
It remains unclear how long the affair lasted, and when exactly the relationship might have ended. The Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.
Publicly available information about Alice Huang is scant.

articles.title: Spain’s first general strike in 14 years brings clashing social and political desires to the fore
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors”

Millions of Spain’s workers are striking on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) to demand that the government remedy the nation’s housing crisis less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power.

Spain’s first general strike in 14 years is expected to cause delays to the widely used public transport system and lead to the slowdown or shuttering of businesses, factories and shops across the eurozone’s fourth largest economy.

Minor incidents were reported in the first hours, including roadblocks — some of them with burning tyres — in Barcelona, the second-largest city in the country, and scuffles between picketers and police near the country’s main wholesale market on the outskirts of the capital, Madrid. Striking workers set off fireworks on the stroke of midnight as they gathered in public squares in Barcelona.

The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors” — 90% in the automotive and port sectors, 85% in the meat industry, 82% in waste collection, and 75% in the energy sector — according to a statement posted on social media.
Between workers, activists, politicians and ordinary Spaniards, the groups have very different interests in Wednesday's (November 11) walkout.
The average rent in Spain has almost doubled in the last 10 years, eating into household budgets and angering voters.

Public anger over housing reached a boiling point following the nationally televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last month. The subsequent death of Maricarmen, as the woman became known, caused even more indignation and solidified her as a symbol of Spaniards who feel they pay too much on rent and can’t even dream of homeownership.
Housing activists leveraged the uproar over Maricarmen's eviction to call for the general strike. They soon won the backing of Spain's two main unions, UGT and CCOO.

The housing activists want several measures, including the elimination of tourist apartments, a crackdown on real estate speculation and protection for renters in the form of automatic renewals of leases.
The UGT and CCOO unions are demanding more government intervention in the housing market and a new minimum wage agreement through talks with the business owners' association.

articles.title: Iran says tanker struck mine, caught fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait

Iran's army said on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that an oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country has been targeting ships that transit without its authorisation.
Since the outbreak of the West Asia war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has, in response, imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.
The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.

"Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz," the naval forces of Iran's army said in a statement carried by state TV.
In recent weeks Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.

U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. military operations in the region, has been escorting ships through the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
On Tuesday (November 10), the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said three other oil tankers had caught fire in the strait.

articles.title: WhatsApp to simplify communication on app, add financial services
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Meta’s head of WhatsApp Kunal Shah shared a post outlining some largely expected outcomes for the messaging platform
Meta’s new head of WhatsApp, Kunal Shah, has promised simplified calls/messages and more financial services on the messaging platform, apart from increased AI integration.
In a post on the social media platform X on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Mr. Shah said he had spent around four months at WhatsApp.
He also shared some largely expected goals for the platform.
The WhatsApp executive said he would make voice notes, groups, stickers and video “simpler and more expressive.”

The company is also working with financial services and telecom partners to explore processes such as paying bills, borrowing money, and ensuring connectivity during travel. The aim of this step is to keep users within the messaging platform, even if they are completing other personal finance tasks.
Not surprisingly, Mr. Shah said he wanted to make these features more efficient with AI.
He did not announce any specific features or share a release date for the same.
WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls every day, he shared, while stressing that the company’s principles would not change any time soon.

“Your personal messages and calls stay end-to-end encrypted. This and our quality bar stays the same. What happens inside WhatsApp only matters for what it makes possible outside it: more time together, stronger communities, and fewer barriers between people and the lives they want to live,” shared Mr. Shah.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.

“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

articles.title: On Minorities Welfare Day, Telangana CM trains his guns on BJP and BRS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) sought to project Congress as the only political entity capable of taking on the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), even as he accused the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) of misleading Muslims and having truck with the Narendra Modi government.

Mr. Reddy was speaking on Minorities Welfare Day, coinciding with the birth anniversary of the first Education Minister Maulana Abul Kalam Azad , in Hyderabad on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) where he criticised the BJP’s stand on the 4% reservation for Muslims and challenged it to first abolish the quota in Gujarat.

Describing the BJP top brass as “musafir” (tourist), he said, “A musafir from Delhi, from far away, came to Chevella and said that they would form the government in Telangana. They said they would remove the 4% reservation for Muslims. I told those tourists that such people come and go. We have ignored such tourists.” He added, “Along with the majority, Congress will work for minorities, for education and for health.”

Putting the BRS into crosshairs, Mr. Reddy charged the party of failing to keep its promise of 12% reservation for Muslims. “A man promised you 12% reservations. Twelve years have passed and that man has run away. All promises during his time have not been kept,” he said.

The Chief Minister further alleged that the BRS’s car, its election symbol, turned into the BJP’s lotus when it reached Delhi. He questioned the BRS’s record in Parliament and accused its leadership of misleading Muslim voters

“In the past 10 years, how many times in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have they helped you? They have taken your help and given the impression that they are fighting Modi. You are believing him because he speaks Urdu, and say, ‘Let’s vote for him’. But he is deceiving you by speaking Urdu. He wears a sherwani for Ramzan, he sits with you, has biryani, qubani, and later embraces Modi,” he said.

Mr. Reddy said the the minorities had voted for regional parties across the country, who they thought would fight the BJP. He alleged that such parties could eventually join hands with the BJP, and that the Congress would never ally with the BJP.

Turning to education, Mr. Reddy recalled the contribution of Maulana Azad to the development of education. He said former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru had entrusted Maulana Azad with the responsibility of advancing education and that he had laid the foundation for the establishment of IITs. This, the Chief Minister said, enabled generations of engineers to emerge.

Mr. Reddy criticised the Union government for discontinuing scholarships for minority students. “I want to ask Modi what sin have they done? It is not in the hands of a person to decide where they should be born, it is Allah’s decision, Bhagwan ’s decision. But it is in our hands to help them to come out of poverty. Which God asked you to remove their scholarship? But Modi and Amit bhai (Amit Shah) can do this,” he said.

The Chief Minister added that if India has to be a world leader, the government should focus on education and welfare of minorities along with the SCs and STs. He said the government was committed to quality education and skill development especially against the backdrop of AI threatening jobs in the IT sector. However, blue-collar jobs could not be replaced by AI, and acquiring skills would ensure employment opportunities, he said.

articles.title: Kedarnath temple portals closed for winter; deity's palanquin begins journey to Ukhimath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The process began at 4 a.m. with special prayers and religious ceremonies, with all rituals performed in accordance with traditional customs before the temple doors were closed at the auspicious time
The portals of the Kedarnath shrine were closed for the winter season at 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) following prescribed rituals and the chanting of Vedic mantras.

The process began at 4 a.m. with special prayers and religious ceremonies, with all rituals performed in accordance with traditional customs before the temple doors were closed at the auspicious time.
Following the closure, the processional palanquin of Lord Kedarnath was carried around the temple complex before departing for the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath, the deity's winter abode.

According to the schedule, the palanquin will halt overnight at Rampur on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) before reaching Guptkashi on November 12. It will arrive at the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath on November 13.
For the next six months, devotees can offer prayers to the deity at the Omkareshwar Temple.
The ceremonial palanquin of Goddess Yamuna, led by Shani Dev Maharaj, departed from Yamunotri for Kharsali, the deity’s winter abode, amid traditional rituals and folk music.
Villagers and pilgrims accorded a grand welcome to the palanquin upon its arrival in the afternoon at the ancestral village of the goddess, showering it with flowers and garlands.
During the six-month pilgrimage season, the Yamunotri Temple Committee received more than ₹90 lakh in donations through donation boxes and receipt books.

On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), a day before the closure of the temple, the committee opened the donation boxes for the fourth time to count the offerings. The exercise yielded ₹10 lakh 42 thousand in cash, while approximately ₹6 lakh was collected through receipt books.

The portals of the Kedarnath shrine were closed for the winter season at 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) following prescribed rituals and the chanting of Vedic mantras.

The process began at 4 a.m. with special prayers and religious ceremonies, with all rituals performed in accordance with traditional customs before the temple doors were closed at the auspicious time.

Following the closure, the processional palanquin of Lord Kedarnath was carried around the temple complex before departing for the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath, the deity's winter abode.

According to the schedule, the palanquin will halt overnight at Rampur on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) before reaching Guptkashi on November 12. It will arrive at the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath on November 13.

For the next six months, devotees can offer prayers to the deity at the Omkareshwar Temple.

The ceremonial palanquin of Goddess Yamuna, led by Shani Dev Maharaj, departed from Yamunotri for Kharsali, the deity’s winter abode, amid traditional rituals and folk music.

Villagers and pilgrims accorded a grand welcome to the palanquin upon its arrival in the afternoon at the ancestral village of the goddess, showering it with flowers and garlands.

During the six-month pilgrimage season, the Yamunotri Temple Committee received more than ₹90 lakh in donations through donation boxes and receipt books.

On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), a day before the closure of the temple, the committee opened the donation boxes for the fourth time to count the offerings. The exercise yielded ₹10 lakh 42 thousand in cash, while approximately ₹6 lakh was collected through receipt books.

articles.title: Take steps to implement 10+2 education system from next academic year: Telangana CM directs officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Revanth Reddy directs officials to provide specialised education considering IX to XII standards as higher education

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy issued directions to take steps to implement a 10+2 education system from the next academic year (2027-28). They were asked to provide specialised education considering IX to XII standards as higher education. He said that changes in education system are needed to keep up with the needs of modern times.

The 10+2 education system was discussed at a meeting held by the Chief Minister — who is also Education Minister — with senior officials of the State Education Department, Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju along with government Adviser K. Keshava Rao and others at MCR HRD in Hyderabad on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy held a meeting on education, with senior officials of the State Education Department, Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju along with government Adviser K. Keshava Rao and others at MCR HRD in Hyderabad on Wednesday (November 11, 2026)
Stating that reforms must be brought in the State’s education, the Chief Minister said that measures have to be taken to provide necessary infrastructure.

articles.title: Jagan alleges large-scale malpractice in Andhra local body polls; says YSRCP vote share rose
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: YSRCP leaders allege bouncers at counting centres, rejected votes and recounts that changed results

YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has accused the Telugu Desam Party (TDP-led) government of resorting to large-scale electoral malpractice in the recent local body elections to conceal the growing public support for his party.

At a meeting with party leaders from several districts at Tadepalli on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), Mr. Jagan reviewed the conduct of the elections and alleged that irregularities, intimidation and manipulation had taken place at various stages of the electoral process, from the announcement of the schedule to the counting of votes.

మున్సిపల్, ఎంపీటీసీ, జెడ్పీటీసీ ఎన్నికలు జరిగిన తీరుపై పార్టీ కేంద్ర కార్యాలయంలో వివిధ జిల్లా నాయకులతో కలిసి సమీక్షించిన వైయస్ జగన్ గారు టీడీపీ దౌర్జన్యాలు, దాడులకి ఎదురు నిలిచి నాయకులతో పాటు కార్యకర్తలు గట్టిగా పోరాటం చేశారని వైయస్ జగన్ గారు కితాబు ఎన్నికలు సజావుగా జరిగి ఉంటే వైయస్‌‌ఆర్‌సీపీ ఓటింగ్ శాతం ఇంకా పెరిగేదన్న వైయస్ జగన్ గారు.. చంద్రబాబు ప్రభుత్వం తప్పుల్ని కప్పిపుచ్చుకోవడానికి అక్రమాలకి పాల్పడిందని మండిపాటు తమ రాజకీయ జీవితంలో ఈ తరహాలో ఎన్నికల్లో అక్రమాలను చూడలేదని వైయస్ జగన్ గారికి చెప్పిన పార్టీ సీనియర్ నేతలు

The YSRCP’s vote share had increased compared with the 2024 elections despite the alleged irregularities, he said. The party would have secured a much higher vote share had the elections been conducted in a free and fair manner, he added.

Accusing Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu of misusing official machinery, Mr. Jagan said the ruling party had resorted to undemocratic practices because of the growing support for the YSRCP and the declining popularity of the government. New methods of electoral manipulation had been adopted, including attempts to reverse results in places where YSRCP candidates had won, he alleged.
He also accused Mr. Naidu of trying to divert attention from the alleged irregularities by raising questions about the local body elections held during the previous YSRCP regime.

Party leaders who attended the meeting reportedly described the recent elections as unprecedented in terms of irregularities and alleged that the State Election Commission had failed to ensure a free and fair electoral process.
They alleged that bouncers were deployed at counting centres in place of authorised election agents and that relatives of candidates were kidnapped to force them to withdraw their nominations.

The leaders further alleged that large numbers of votes polled in favour of YSRCP candidates were declared invalid during counting and that power supply was deliberately disrupted at some counting centres to facilitate manipulation.

They also complained that repeated recounting was ordered in constituencies where YSRCP candidates had secured victories, allegedly resulting in changes to the final tallies. However, requests for recounting made by YSRCP candidates were rejected, they said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: About a month ago, when the NPCI had pushed back the rollout of MDR from its original date of October 15, it had said it would be implemented “immediately post Diwali”

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine hold second day of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘We are starting the second day of negotiations,’ Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, who leads Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, says on social media

Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a second straight day of U.S.-brokered talks on ways of ending the war started by Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

Hopes are low for any breakthrough in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations, although U.S. officials say they are determined to revive peace efforts that so far have failed to deliver significant results.
“We are starting the second day of negotiations,” Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service who leads Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, said on social media.

The envoys met for four hours on Tuesday (November 10) in the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which was chosen as a neutral venue. The talks, mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, were due to conclude later Wednesday (November 11).

The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.
Also, Russia's wartime economy is under heavy strain, and Ukraine is reeling from devastating aerial attacks on its power grid.
Mr. Umerov said that Wednesday (November 11) would begin with three-way talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, with Kyiv's delegation meeting afterwards with European officials.
Moscow doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations.
However, representatives of European governments, the European Union and NATO were in Abu Dhabi and were consulting with the Ukrainian delegation, officials said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday's (November 10) session was “constructive and quite substantive”.

articles.title: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: If anaemia reduction should align with India’s goals for NCD reduction, then the focus must be on better diets through diversification. That should be non-negotiable for public health policy: no amount of papering over cracks with pills and potions will work in the long term

India has had decades of unchanged high anaemia prevalence in women and children that has historically been thought to be due to iron deficiency. This has led firstly to an iron and folic acid (IFA) tablet supplementation targeted at women and children, and secondly to fitful implementation of mandatory fortification of staple foods. IFA is a ‘precision’ strategy, applying as it does to the vulnerable population it is intended for, while fortification is a broad strategy that applies to the entire population. The latter works in controlled settings such as clinical trials, but has not worked in real-world settings, and might have adverse effects when given to those it is unintended for.

The reason for pivoting: anaemia is mistakenly conflated with iron deficiency In India. The evidence is otherwise: in national Indian surveys, it has been shown that iron deficiency is not the major cause of anaemia. Indeed, fully one-third of anaemia cases demonstrate no micronutrient deficiency or obvious cause. Even so, giving iron should have sorted out those who did have iron deficiency anaemia, and reduced the general anaemia prevalence. While this could be a problem with inefficient programme implementation, two important questions arise: is there is really a deficiency in dietary iron intake in India? And is the administered iron being adequately absorbed and utilised for haemoglobin formation?

Science, Space & Environment Report: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Khaki whistle guards to replace metal chains for Karnataka police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police constables and head constables in Karnataka will soon replace the traditional metal whistle chains on their uniforms with new khaki-coloured whistle guards, following an order issued by Director-General and Inspector-General of Police (DG&IGP) M.A. Saleem.

Mr. Saleem, who is also the Head of the Police Force (HoPF), has directed all unit officers to take necessary steps to introduce the new whistle guards for lower-rank police personnel across the State.
