articles.title: TDB under fire as Sabarimala pilgrimage readiness faces delays
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The union said that although the Chief Minister directed tar and make roads to the parking areas motorable during his Nilakkal visit, many stretches remain muddy and essential repairs are delayed.

The delay in key preparatory works ahead of the annual Sabarimala pilgrimage season has drawn sharp criticism from Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) employees, who have held the leadership responsible for the lapses.

the Travancore Devaswom Employees Front, a Congress-backed employees’ union, has now come up flagging delays in completing essential infrastructure works and warned that inadequate preparations could disrupt the pilgrimage season.

“The Chief Minister had directed that the roads leading to the parking grounds be tarred and made motorable during his visit to Nilakkal. However, several stretches remain muddy even now. Essential repair works have also not been completed on time. The new construction work at the aravana plant, which was scheduled for completion during the previous monthly pooja, remains unfinished,” the union said in a statement.

More worrying is the dwindling stock of ghee required for aravana production, even as the tender process for procuring additional supplies from outside remains incomplete. Any delay in securing ghee could seriously affect production and distribution of the offering during the pilgrimage season, the union warned.

It held the Board president and administrative committee responsible for any disruption in aravana production, ghee supply, appam availability, transport facilities, sanitation or food arrangements for employees. The union also warned against attempts to shift the blame for administrative failures onto employees.”Employees working sincerely despite limited facilities should not be made scapegoats for the Board’s failure to make adequate preparations,” it said.
Besides the employees’ union, several other organisations, including the Akhil Bharata Ayyappa Seva Sanghom, have also expressed dissatisfaction over the pace of preparatory works at Sabarimala.

The board, meanwhile, acknowledged that some works had fallen behind schedule but maintained that they could be completed before the season begins. Its officials also alleged that the Congress-backed union was attempting to pre-empt criticism of its own leadership in the event of any lapses during the pilgrimage season.

The delay in upgrading the aravana plant was one of the major setbacks, a Board official admitted. ”One of the major lapses was on the part of the Devaswom PWD, which delayed the upgradation of the aravana plant by around 15 days. However, the situation is under control, as production of three lakh tins of aravana began on Monday,” the official said.

Even as the board sought to allay concerns over production, the distribution of the offering remains another potential trouble spot. Officials fear that poor internet connectivity at Sannidhanam and possible software glitches could disrupt transactions at the counters. ”As many as 19 counters will operate at Sannidhanam to distribute the offerings, all equipped with an integrated payment system. However, there are serious doubts about whether this arrangement can be sustained smoothly in the long run,” the official added.

articles.title: Cabinet approves ₹2,390 crore metro rail link from Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The project, approved by the Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, represents a significant advancement in the city's infrastructure development, an official statement said

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) approved the extension of the Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4 at an estimated cost of ₹2,390 crore, with a length of 8.449 kilometres and five elevated stations.
The project, approved by the Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, represents a significant advancement in the city's infrastructure development, an official statement said.
The Prime Minister listed the advantages of the project, saying it would provide a major boost to connectivity and ease of living.

"As Noida and Greater Noida grow, why should daily commutes become longer? Here is some good news for the people of Noida and Greater Noida! The Cabinet has approved an extension of the Aqua Line Metro.”
"Key advantages — easier access to offices, schools, hospitals and commercial hubs. Less congestion.”
“Shorter commutes. A major boost to connectivity and ease of living indeed," Mr. Modi said in a post on X.
The project would be completed over a period of four years, Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters at a Cabinet briefing.
Upon operationalisation of this corridor, Noida and Greater Noida will have 71.878 kilometres of active metro rail network, he said.
Mr. Vaishnaw said this project acts as a major expansion of the metro rail network in the city.
The corridor will introduce approximately 8.449 kilometres of new metro lines, significantly improving public transportation in Noida and Greater Noida, which currently lack efficient connectivity.

articles.title: PM’s visit: Six key roads to face traffic diversions on November 12, 13
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Traffic movement on six key roads in Mysuru, including stretches leading to Chamundi Hill, will be regulated on November 12 and 13 in view of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the city on Friday.
Mr. Modi is scheduled to inaugurate an LED dome planetarium during his visit.

The roads where traffic diversions will be in force include Lalitadripura Road (from Lalitadripura Ring Road junction to Helipad junction); IVAC Road (from IVAC junction to Chamundi Hill Road junction); Lalith Mahal Road (from T. Narasipur Road T junction to M.R.C. Circle); Chamundi Hill Road (from Sangolli Rayanna Circle to Chamundi Hill); Lorry Terminal Road (from M.R.C. Circle to Rajahamsa junction); and Nanjangud Road (from Rajahamsa junction to Nanjangud Ring Road junction).

The police have suggested an alternative route for vehicles proceeding towards Chamundi Hill from Sangolli Rayanna Circle. Motorists can take the route via Gautama Buddha Circle, M.M. Road, R. Mahadevappa Circle, Sangeetha Corner, T. Junction, Savitri Bai Phule Circle, Ring Road and Uttanahalli Ring Road before joining Chamundi Hill Road, a press release from the Commissioner of Police said.
The police have advised motorists to avoid the above mentioned road stretches and take alternative routes during the two days.
The police have urged motorists to plan their journeys in advance, use alternative routes wherever possible and follow the instructions of traffic personnel.

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap after U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two sides have exchanged thousands of captured soldiers throughout the almost five-year war, started by Russia’s 2022 invasion
Russia and Ukraine have agreed their biggest ever release of prisoners after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner told reporters on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
“One of the positives is that we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, and we’re going to finalise the numbers tomorrow,” he said.

Mr. Kushner and fellow U.S. mediator Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday (November 12, 2026) to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The two sides have exchanged thousands of captured soldiers throughout the almost five-year war, started by Russia’s 2022 invasion.
But diplomatic talks have so far failed to move the two sides closer to an agreement to halt the fighting, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people.

The two days of conversations in Abu Dhabi appeared to fit that mould, with the prisoner exchange and agreement to carry on talking the only concrete outcomes mentioned by any side in post-talks press statements.
Russian envoy Vladimir Medinsky and Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov also said a large scale prisoner exchange had been agreed, adding the numbers would be announced later.

Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a second straight day of U.S.-brokered talks on ways of ending the war started by Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

The envoys met for four hours on Tuesday (November 10) in the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which was chosen as a neutral venue. The talks, mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, were due to conclude later Wednesday (November 11).

Russia and Ukraine have agreed their biggest ever release of prisoners after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner told reporters on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

“One of the positives is that we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, and we’re going to finalise the numbers tomorrow,” he said.

Mr. Kushner and fellow U.S. mediator Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday (November 12, 2026) to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The two sides have exchanged thousands of captured soldiers throughout the almost five-year war, started by Russia’s 2022 invasion.

But diplomatic talks have so far failed to move the two sides closer to an agreement to halt the fighting, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people.

The two days of conversations in Abu Dhabi appeared to fit that mould, with the prisoner exchange and agreement to carry on talking the only concrete outcomes mentioned by any side in post-talks press statements.

Russian envoy Vladimir Medinsky and Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov also said a large scale prisoner exchange had been agreed, adding the numbers would be announced later.

Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a second straight day of U.S.-brokered talks on ways of ending the war started by Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

The envoys met for four hours on Tuesday (November 10) in the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which was chosen as a neutral venue. The talks, mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, were due to conclude later Wednesday (November 11).

The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Wednesday said the State government was committed to securing official recognition for the Kannada language and the Kannada flag.

He said former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah had earlier brought the issue of official recognition for the Kannada flag to the attention of the Union government. He had also prepared another book on Mahatma Gandhi’s 100-year legacy and the Gandhi Bharata programme held in Belagavi, which would be released at an appropriate time.

He recalled being inspired by a nearly 55-minute literary speech delivered by former Chief Minister J.H. Patel at the Kannada Sahitya Sammelana in Kanakapura and said he had requested Mr. Patel’s son, Mahima Patel, to publish it as a book.

Praising Shivarathri Deshikendra Swami of Suttur seer for encouraging writers and inspiring the publication of several books, Mr. Shivakumar said literature, spiritual thought and cultural preservation were essential for building a humane society. “The pen is mightier than the sword. Literature has the power to change society,” he said.

articles.title: 51-year-old woman undergoes mechanical mitral valve replacement at Gandhi Hospital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Doctors at the Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad, successfully conducted a mitral valve replacement (MVR) surgery on a 51-year-old woman recently.

The patient, Rajamma, was admitted to the Department of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery (CTVS) with complaints of breathlessness, classified as New York Heart Association Class III, indicating marked limitation of physical activity due to cardiac symptoms.

Following routine investigations, doctors performed an MVR procedure using a 27-mm mechanical valve. Post-surgery, she was shifted to the ICU and placed on mechanical ventilation with minimal inotropic support. She was successfully taken off ventilator support on the first post-operative day.

Anticoagulation therapy was subsequently initiated to prevent blood clot formation around the artificial valve. A postoperative 2D echocardiography with colour Doppler showed normally functioning mechanical valve leaflets, minimal pressure gradient across the prosthetic valve, no paravalvular leak and good left ventricular function. The patient has been declared fit for discharge, doctors said.

articles.title: Gang rape survivor thrown off roof in Bihar’s Begusarai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police say the accused arrested in this case was not involved in the previous incident.
A 30-year-old gang rape survivor was thrown off the roof of a building (approximately 15 feet) allegedly by relatives of the accused in Bihar’s Begusarai district.
The incident took place in the Simaria Ghat Bind Toli locality under the Chakia police station jurisdiction on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). She is currently admitted to Sadar Hospital, Begusarai.

“Based on the victim’s statement, the named accused, Bhongal Kumar, has been arrested, and police are conducting raids to arrest another unidentified accused,” Begusarai Deputy Superintendent of Police (Headquarters) Nikhil Kumar told The Hindu .
Under the supervision of the Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO), Sadar-02, the Chakia police team has launched an investigation into the incident.
The police said the accused arrested in this case was not involved in the previous incident.

“The recent incident involves an act of physical assault. Regarding the prior case, four accused individuals have already been arrested and sent to jail; for one additional accused, proceedings for the attachment of property have been initiated, and a bounty has been announced. None of the accused from the previous case have been released from jail. The case is currently undergoing a speedy trial,” the Begusarai police said.

The rape took place on June 11, 2026. “Ever since the incident, people associated with the accused have been continuously pressuring me to withdraw the case and threatening dire consequences,” said the victim’s husband.

The woman was admitted to the hospital on the night of June 11 after the incident and was discharged on June 12. However, five days later, she complained of pain, and an ultrasound revealed wood and stones lodged in her private parts. The victim subsequently remained hospitalised for several days.
A Special Investigation Team (SIT) was formed to probe the case, resulting in the arrest of four accused. Chakia Police Station in-charge Ranjiv Ranjan was also suspended for negligence of duty.

articles.title: Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express users may pay nearly ₹200 more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Charging fares inflating the distance by 40% on Konkan Railway network between Thokur and Madgaon and 100% on 55 km Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat section the reason for extra fares

From November 15, patrons of the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26655/656) will pay nearly ₹200 extra fare in chair car (CC) and about ₹300 extra on executive chair car (EC) when compared to the same distance travelled on other Vande Bharat services.

The actual base fare, for example, between Yeshwantpur and Madgaon in CC would be around ₹1,186 and in EC around ₹2,444. However, the actual distance of 670 km gets inflated to around 844 km increasing the base fare to ₹1,369 in CC (₹183 extra) and ₹2,795 (₹351 extra) in EC classes. The base fare excludes reservation charges of ₹40 and ₹60, superfast charges of ₹45 and ₹75, respectively, for these classes and 5% GST on all these charges. If the passenger opts for onboard food, catering charges ranging from ₹300 to ₹600, would be extra.

For Karwar, the likely base fare could be ₹1,292 as against the actual ₹1,100 in CC (₹192 extra) and ₹2,642 as against ₹2,253 in EC class; for Udupi, it could be ₹931 as against ₹809 (₹122 extra) in CC and ₹1,890 as against ₹1,651 (₹239 extra) in EC and for Mangaluru Junction, the base fare could be ₹809 as against the actual ₹721 (₹88 extra) in CC and ₹1,561 as against the actual ₹1,468 (₹93 extra) in EC class.
Source: Railway Ministry’s fare chart for premium services

Normal fares are collected on other VB expresses operating in Karnataka for almost similar distances. For example, the base fares on Mangaluru-Thiruvananthapuram Central VB Express have been ₹1,131 and ₹2,295 for CC and EC respectively for 620 km distance; KSR Bengaluru-Ernakulam Junction VB Express at ₹1,159 and ₹2,352 for 625 km; KSR Bengaluru-Belagavi VB Express at ₹1,132 and ₹2,295 for 612 km and on Yeshwantpur-Kacheguda VB, the base fares have been ₹1,113 and ₹2,267 for CC and EC respectively.
A 16-car Brand new Vande Bharat rake is kept ready for the November 15 inaugural run of Madgaon-Yeshwantpur VB Express from Mangaluru Junction on November 11, 2026. | Photo Credit: H S MANJUNATH

The extra fare becomes applicable as the Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd., (KRCL) on whose network half of the route passes through, inflates the distance by 40% to calculate passenger fares and by 50% for freight charges. KRCL network begins from Thokur near Mangaluru and extends till Roha in Maharashtra surpassing Madgaon. Thus, about 300 km distance between Thokur and Madgaon gets inflated to 416 km.

At the same time, the South Western Railway (SWR) inflates the 55 km distance on the Ghat section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road by 100%, making the chargeable distance to 110 km. Thus, the end-to-end inflated chargeable distance becomes about 844 km against the actual 670 km distance.

The SWR justified the inflated distance saying the Indian Railways follows the practice on almost all Ghat routes because of the challenges in operating through difficult terrains. KRCL was initially allowed to inflate the distance to recover the construction cost of about ₹3,555 crore. 🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 11 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express users may pay nearly ₹200 more

Charging fares inflating the distance by 40% on Konkan Railway network between Thokur and Madgaon and 100% on 55 km Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat section the reason for extra fares

From November 15, patrons of the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26655/656) will pay nearly ₹200 extra fare in chair car (CC) and about ₹300 extra on executive chair car (EC) when compared to the same distance travelled on other Vande Bharat services.

The actual base fare, for example, between Yeshwantpur and Madgaon in CC would be around ₹1,186 and in EC around ₹2,444. However, the actual distance of 670 km gets inflated to around 844 km increasing the base fare to ₹1,369 in CC (₹183 extra) and ₹2,795 (₹351 extra) in EC classes. The base fare excludes reservation charges of ₹40 and ₹60, superfast charges of ₹45 and ₹75, respectively, for these classes and 5% GST on all these charges. If the passenger opts for onboard food, catering charges ranging from ₹300 to ₹600, would be extra.

For Karwar, the likely base fare could be ₹1,292 as against the actual ₹1,100 in CC (₹192 extra) and ₹2,642 as against ₹2,253 in EC class; for Udupi, it could be ₹931 as against ₹809 (₹122 extra) in CC and ₹1,890 as against ₹1,651 (₹239 extra) in EC and for Mangaluru Junction, the base fare could be ₹809 as against the actual ₹721 (₹88 extra) in CC and ₹1,561 as against the actual ₹1,468 (₹93 extra) in EC class.

Source: Railway Ministry’s fare chart for premium services

Normal fares are collected on other VB expresses operating in Karnataka for almost similar distances. For example, the base fares on Mangaluru-Thiruvananthapuram Central VB Express have been ₹1,131 and ₹2,295 for CC and EC respectively for 620 km distance; KSR Bengaluru-Ernakulam Junction VB Express at ₹1,159 and ₹2,352 for 625 km; KSR Bengaluru-Belagavi VB Express at ₹1,132 and ₹2,295 for 612 km and on Yeshwantpur-Kacheguda VB, the base fares have been ₹1,113 and ₹2,267 for CC and EC respectively.

A 16-car Brand new Vande Bharat rake is kept ready for the November 15 inaugural run of Madgaon-Yeshwantpur VB Express from Mangaluru Junction on November 11, 2026. | Photo Credit: H S MANJUNATH

The extra fare becomes applicable as the Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd., (KRCL) on whose network half of the route passes through, inflates the distance by 40% to calculate passenger fares and by 50% for freight charges. KRCL network begins from Thokur near Mangaluru and extends till Roha in Maharashtra surpassing Madgaon. Thus, about 300 km distance between Thokur and Madgaon gets inflated to 416 km.

At the same time, the South Western Railway (SWR) inflates the 55 km distance on the Ghat section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road by 100%, making the chargeable distance to 110 km. Thus, the end-to-end inflated chargeable distance becomes about 844 km against the actual 670 km distance.

The SWR justified the inflated distance saying the Indian Railways follows the practice on almost all Ghat routes because of the challenges in operating through difficult terrains. KRCL was initially allowed to inflate the distance to recover the construction cost of about ₹3,555 crore. The Corporation now justifies the additional collection due to “heavy maintenance cost (due to difficult geographical conditions).”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SWR justified the inflated distance saying the Indian Railways follows the practice on almost all Ghat routes because of the challenges in operating through difficult terrains. KRCL was initially allowed to inflate the distance to recover the construction cost of about ₹3,555 crore. articles.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, sees no deliberate election bias
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Meta told the Court last month it had adopted ​measures to ensure equal treatment of ‌the two campaigns

Brazil's electoral authority fined Meta's Facebook 7.5 million reais ($1.34 million) for failing to fully comply ​with judicial orders during last month's Presidential election runoff campaign, but said there ‌was no evidence so far that the company had ​deliberately acted to influence the outcome.

In a unanimous decision, ⁠the country's top electoral court (TSE) ruled on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that Facebook had failed to adequately meet court demands related to allegations that its ‌platform treated content from the rival campaigns of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator ‌Flavio Bolsonaro differently.

Mr. Lula's coalition filed a complaint ahead of the ‌vote alleging ⁠restrictions on the distribution of its posts, the activity ⁠of purportedly inauthentic accounts, failures in identifying AI-generated content, and asymmetries in the operation of Meta's tools.
Meta told the Court last month it had adopted ​measures to ensure equal treatment of ‌the two campaigns. It did not immediately reply to a fresh request for comment.

The Court said Meta had provided some information and documents on the measures, but found that ‌parts of its orders were either not complied with, were ​only partially fulfilled, or were carried out after deadlines had passed.

"The records contain technical failures acknowledged ⁠by Facebook itself, but there are no elements allowing us to conclude, on a preliminary basis, that there was deliberate action to unbalance ‌the election," Justice Marco Aurelio Bellizze wrote in his ruling.
"That conclusion would require robust evidence, to be produced through the appropriate legal proceedings," he added.

According to Mr. Bellizze, the fine reflected Meta's conduct in responding to the Court orders as a whole, including delays, incomplete information and difficulties in verifying some of ‌the data submitted.

The amount corresponds to three daily fines of 500,000 reais between October ​17 and 19, and six days of fines of 1 million reais per day between October 20 ⁠and 25, when Mr. Lula unexpectedly secured re-election over Mr. Bolsonaro after his ⁠team mobilised a huge social media campaign.

Mr. Lula has long vowed to tighten rules on social media in the country. ‌In his victory speech, he said, "We had to overcome foreign interference in the election, coming from outside through digital platforms ​that we will have to regulate."

articles.title: New registration framework proposed to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions invites public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.

The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.

The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.
Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.

“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.
This competency-based approach seeks to facilitate professional development and career progression, and improve the quality of allied and healthcare services.
“The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability,’’ a senior Health Ministry official said.

By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed requirements, the regulations seek to ensure allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.
An integrated online registration system for submitting applications, verifying credentials, assess eligibility, and issue provisional registration certificates is also proposed.

Eligible professionals granted provisional registration will receive a Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID). The digital platform will simply procedures, improve access, and promote uniform efficiency across States and Union Territories.

National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions invites public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.

The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.

The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.

Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.

“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.

This competency-based approach seeks to facilitate professional development and career progression, and improve the quality of allied and healthcare services.

“The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability,’’ a senior Health Ministry official said.

By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed requirements, the regulations seek to ensure allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.

An integrated online registration system for submitting applications, verifying credentials, assess eligibility, and issue provisional registration certificates is also proposed.

Eligible professionals granted provisional registration will receive a Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID). The digital platform will simply procedures, improve access, and promote uniform efficiency across States and Union Territories.

articles.title: JSP Salur chairperson accuses Minister of supporting independent candidate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A war of words erupted between Jana Sena Party’s newly elected Chairperson of Salur Gorle Vijaya Kumari and the supporters of Minister for Tribal Welfare Gummadi Sandhya Rani after former accused the Minister of supporting independent candidate Gulla Manjeera and violating the alliance guidelines during the recently concluded local body polls.

Despite JSP being part of the alliance parties, Ms. Kumari alleged that the Minister Rani had backed Ms. Manjeera, who got 6,143 votes, resulting in the loss of JSP Councillors in three wards of the seven wards they contested in. She also claimed that all the independent candidates were allotted same symbol – “cupboard”, causing a lot of confusion in voters.
In the Municipal elections in Salur conducted on November 1, Mr. Kumari polled 9,686 votes, while her nearest rival and YSRCP candidate Ribka Rani got 9,390 votes.
JSP Salur Coordinator Gorle Tirupati Naidu asserted that the violation of “alliance dharma” would be brought to the notice of JSP high command in a couple of days.
Questioning the logic behind allocation of ‘cupboard’ symbol to all independent candidates, Mr. Naidu alleged that “it [independent candidates] was an unofficial panel created to defeat JSP”.
Meanwhile, supporters of the Minister refuted the allegations and said that JSP candidates were defeated in the absence of a dedicated network at ground level.
Meanwhile, for the deputy chairperson’s post YSRCP won 13 wards, while TDP got 11 seats in Salur elections.

JSP won four and independents got elected in three places. A BJP candidate was elected in one ward. Former Deputy Chief Minister and YSRCP senior leader Peedika Rajanna Dora hoped that their party would win the deputy chairperson’s post as it is the single largest party in the council.

articles.title: Farmer climbs tree on Shivamogga DC office premises, alleges corruption against Revenue Dept. officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tension prevailed for some time on the premises of the Deputy Commissioner’s office here on Wednesday after a farmer climbed a tree and threatened to jump off, alleging corruption by Revenue Department officials.

N. Nagaraj, 55, from Ramenakoppa village in Shivamogga taluk, climbed a huge banyan tree on the premises and refused to come down even after his relatives and officials appealed to him. Personnel of the Fire and Emergency Services were summoned.

Mr. Nagaraj said the then Deputy Commissioner had passed an order in August, in a land ownership dispute, in favour of him and a few other litigants. The tahsildar, who was to act on the order after verifying the relevant records, delayed the process and took money from the litigants, he alleged. He said he and the other litigants were worried because the tahsildar had been transferred the previous day.

After repeated persuasion by officials and relatives, Mr. Nagaraj agreed to come down. Fire and Emergency Services personnel helped him down with a ladder. He then told the media that a few Revenue Department officials took money to implement the Deputy Commissioner’s order and even demanded more. Later, he met Deputy Commissioner Prakash G.T. Nittali and submitted a petition.

When The Hindu c ontacted the Deputy Commissioner, Mr. Nittali said he had gathered information from the farmer about the issue. “The previous Deputy Commissioner issued an order, and the tahsildar has to act as per the order. The new tahsildar took charge of the office this morning. He will take up the issue and act as per law. I have told him the same,” he said.
On the allegations of corruption, he said that if there were specific allegations against anyone, backed by concrete evidence, he could order an inquiry and take further action.

articles.title: Science takes centre stage as students bring ideas alive through theatre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kerala School Science Drama Competition blends performance and scientific thinking to spark curiosity among young minds

Science and theatre came together on stage at the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi Hall in Thrissur on Wednesday as students showcased the power of drama to communicate scientific ideas at the 2026-27 Kerala School Science Drama Competition.

Organised by the General Education department, the competition was inaugurated by Rajan J. Pallan, MLA. Thrissur district panchayat president Mary Thomas presided over the function, while Mayfi Delson, chairperson of the Corporation’s Education Standing Committee, was the chief guest.

In his inaugural address, Mr. Pallan said theatre could make complex scientific concepts accessible to the public while nurturing scientific curiosity among students and young people. He recalled the significant role played by theatre in Keralam’s renaissance movements and in creating social awareness.

The growth of science had helped society understand the truth behind several superstitions that had long prevailed, he said, stressing the importance of using creative platforms to promote scientific thinking. District panchayat vice-president T.K. Sudheesh, Education Standing Committee chairperson Sheela George, Corporation councillor Joy Bastin and Science Club district secretary K.C. Sreevalsan also spoke.

articles.title: TGPCB panel calls for action against construction companies over environmental violations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB)’s task force committee has recommended the closure of four construction projects in Hyderabad and Rangareddy districts for carrying out construction activities without obtaining consent for establishment.
It has also recommended the closure of a captive ready mix concrete (RMC) plant operating without consent and adequate pollution control measures.

The recommendations followed inspections by the board’s Rolling Task Force teams in response to complaints of air pollution caused by construction activity. The inspections revealed several violations, including inadequate dust-control measures, improper storage and disposal of construction waste, and excessive noise levels.

The committee reviewed the compliance status of 18 construction projects at a meeting held at the TGPCB head office on Wednesday. Regional Officers, Task Force teams and representatives of the construction projects concerned attended the meeting.

The inspections found that several projects had failed to provide wind-breaking walls of at least 10 metres in height. Dust accumulation on internal roads and surrounding streets, inadequate sprinkling of water, and open storage of sand and construction debris were also reported.

Other violations included improper disposal of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, failure to maintain records of waste disposal, use of MS (Mild Steel) drum chutes instead of HDPE chutes, and ambient noise levels exceeding the prescribed daytime commercial limit of 65 dB(A), a statement from TGPCB informed.

The committee recommended environmental compensation for projects with major violations and forfeiture of bank guarantees in cases involving minor violations. It also directed non-compliant projects to rectify the deficiencies within 10 days, the statement said, without naming the violators.
The committee recommended stoppage of construction activities at another project for non-compliance. The board will initiate further action based on the recommendations.

articles.title: Netanyahu dismisses claims that Israel blocking supplies to Gaza
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Benjamin Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Donald Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected accusations that Israel has been delaying the entry of winter supplies into the Gaza Strip as the enclave faces worsening conditions this week, with severe rains flooding makeshift tents.
He said Israel was not to blame for the worsening conditions for Palestinians in Gaza's tent camps that have been hit by severe winter floods.

His remarks came after the U.S.-created Board of Peace — established under U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Israel-Hamas war and oversee Gaza's recovery — said Monday (November 9, 2026) that Israel's delaying of the entry of winter supplies into Gaza had “exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge”.

Torrential rain has battered the war-torn enclave in recent days, damaging tens of thousands of makeshift tents. Four people, including three children, were killed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) when a large sandstone slab collapsed onto tents during the rains.

Mr. Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Mr. Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes.
“Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza, and it is now cynically exploiting that suffering to shift blame onto Israel once again,” he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the situation in Gaza was “intolerable” and demanded Israel end “arbitrary restrictions” on aid. And in Washington, Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii, the top Democrat on the Senate's foreign spending subcommittee, called for Israel to immediately allow winter gear into Gaza.

“There are a lot of challenges when it comes to Israel and Palestine that are complicated, and fraught, and contentious,” Mr. Schatz said on the Senate floor on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). “But we should all be able to agree that repairing torn tents and helping people to dry out, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation.”

articles.title: Central committee suggests three-year roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand mining from active river channels
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems

The Supreme Court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) has suggested preparing a time-bound roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years.

The committee, a statutory body since 2023 and originally formed in 2002 on the apex court's order, has also recommended developing sustainable alternative sources of sand and aggregates to progressively reduce dependence on extraction from active river channels.
For this, it has suggested scientific desiltation of dams and reservoirs and recycling of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, among other measures.
These recommendations are part of the CEC's report submitted to the Supreme Court on November 2 as part of a sou motu case related to illegal sand mining in the National Chambal Sanctuary.

In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems.

"The impacts inter alia include riverbed degradation and infrastructure vulnerability, depletion of groundwater and loss of aquifers, destruction of aquatic and riparian habitats, and alteration of river morphology and hydrology, etc," said the committee.
It also highlights that there is no consolidated, reliable national database that quantifies the volume or value of illegally extracted river sand.
As a result, the CEC has recommended strengthening the existing regulatory and monitoring framework governing extraction from permissible areas.

This can be done through scientific identification of mineable stretches, regular replenishment studies, determination of sustainable extraction limits, environmental safeguards, digital tracking of mineral transportation and end-use and effective enforcement, it said.

"A time-bound roadmap shall be prepared to progressively phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years, alongside development of adequate alternative sources, including reservoir sediment, M-sand and recycled C&D waste, while ensuring that legitimate construction requirements are met,” the CEC said in its report.

articles.title: Prix Pascal: If AI writes your book, are you still a writer?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: France’s new Prix Pascal for AI-assisted books prompts a writer to reflect on the slow pleasures of making art, loss of individuality, and need to reclaim human imagination

There is now a new French literary prize for AI-assisted writing — the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA. The Pascal prize requires entrants to turn in an unpublished manuscript, fiction or non-fiction, in French, of approximately 3,00,000 characters, written with the help of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Writers must declare which AI model and prompts they have employed. The applications, to be submitted by November 30, consist of “a seed, a manuscript and a technical file, submitted simultaneously”. Ten finalists will be announced on December 4 and the winner will be revealed on December 15.

“This [submitted] work must be useful, or raise awareness, or help to solve in an original way one of the ecological, social and ethical challenges that threaten humanity. It cannot easily be controlled or colonised. It does not seek permission. And that, to many, is frightening. What better way to colonise the imagination than to introduce AI into the writer’s world? Also, that way everybody — even the ones with little understanding of what a writer does — can acquire the overnight label of one. Where does this leave writers who have spent years honing their craft, writers who have survived by the skin of their teeth? The world needs writers more urgently than ever before, and more of us should let some form of creative practice into our lives.

Two semesters ago, a few students from my Creative Writing course, at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, confessed to what their worst fears were: that, having come of age in the post-AI era, they would find it a challenge to access and exercise their imagination — which, in their understanding, was foundational to the course. articles.title: Ensure HYDRAA chief’s presence before Bench in contempt case: HC to DGP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana High Court, on Wednesday, directed Director General of Police C.V. Anand to ensure the presence of HYDRAA Commissioner and IPS officer A.V. Ranganath before a Bench on November 17 in a contempt of court case.

Earlier, Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy directed the HYDRAA Commissioner and Shamshabad Tahsildar to be present before the Bench on Wednesday, having issued Form-I notices to them. The Commissioner and the Tahsildar filed an interlocutory application seeking exemption from appearance. Not convinced by the reasons cited by the two officials, the judge directed the DGP to ensure their presence on November 17.

The Telangana High Court on Wednesday directed the Principal Secretary of Finance Sandeep Kumar Sultania to clear bills to the tune of ₹51.35 crore to be paid to persons whose lands were acquired by the government for various projects in Narayanpet district, within eight weeks.

Passing the direction, Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar instructed the officer to file a comprehensive additional affidavit explaining the payment mode and time required for clearing the remaining bills. The Principal Secretary, appearing before the Bench in virtual mode for hearing a batch of six contempt of court cases, informed that the State was in a precarious financial position and was not able to pay compensation at once to all the petitioners.
The judge observed that courts cannot be casual in contempt cases especially in matters connected to payment of compensation to citizens who gave away their lands for government projects.

The Telangana High Court on Wednesday issued notices to SPECTRA group entities in real estate business to respond to the contentions raised by Right Society in a PIL petition alleging that the group owners indulged in real estate scam.

Senior counsel B. Rachna Reddy appearing for the petitioner contended that the group owners took nearly 10,000 home buyers for a ride in Bhongir, Hyderabad, Shadnagar, Yadadri, Narkatpally, Balanagar and other areas.
The matter was adjourned to December 23 for next hearing.

More than 800 teams, each comprising four students from multidisciplinary backgrounds, from 190 colleges, including IITs and leading NIRF-ranked engineering institutions, competed in Lam’s advanced systems engineering challenge. The participation underscored the growing importance of systems engineering skills needed to design, build and optimise increasingly complex semiconductor manufacturing technologies.

Following a multi-stage, three-month competition that included qualification and hardware-build rounds, selected teams advanced to the finale. The winners were announced at the grand finale held at PES University in Bengaluru.

According to Lam Research, entries were evaluated on innovation, technical excellence, collaboration, problem-solving and performance under pressure, with IIT Guwahati emerging as the overall winner. IIT Ropar finished runner-up and NIT Calicut second runner-up. The winners shared prize money worth ₹10 lakh, while select students were offered internship opportunities with Lam Research.

He said advanced semiconductor manufacturing requires expertise spanning hardware, software, automation, data science, process engineering and advanced controls, making systems engineering a critical capability for the industry’s future growth. Unlike traditional engineering competitions focused on individual disciplines, the Lam Research Challenge encourages participants to apply systems-level thinking and understand how multiple technologies and functions interact within large-scale manufacturing operations, the company said.

Mr. Raghavan said the industry’s talent requirements are evolving beyond traditional engineering disciplines. Modern semiconductor manufacturing environments require engineers who can understand and optimise entire systems rather than individual components in isolation, creating growing demand for talent capable of integrating technologies across increasingly complex engineering environments.

Building the pipeline of future talent continues to be important as India expands its role across semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, equipment engineering and the broader electronics ecosystem, he added.

articles.title: Assam CM Himanta Sarma backs woman’s paternity case against ex-Uttarakhand Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ms. Indira Dewri has renewed her demand for a fresh CBI probe and DNA test to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has backed a woman’s demand for justice in a 23-year-old paternity row involving former Uttarakhand Minister and Congress leader Harak Singh Rawat.
In a social media post on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), the Chief Minister said he had met Ms. Indira Dewri, also known as Jenny, who claims that Mr. Rawat raped and impregnated her in 2003.

Condemning the treatment Ms. Dewri — who hails from Sadiya in Assam’s Tinsukia district — had received, Mr. Sarma wrote: “Yesterday (November 10, 2026), I met Jenny, a resident of Assam. What a man named Harak Singh Rawat from Uttarakhand did to her is extremely wrong and reprehensible. No one should have to suffer the kind of cruelty she endured. I stand firmly with her in this fight for justice.”
In the meeting, Ms. Dewri renewed her demand for a DNA test and a fresh Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son.
She told journalists in Dehradun on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that she has appealed to Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami for justice.
She would stay in Dehradun until her demands were addressed, she said.
Ms. Dewri criticised the earlier CBI investigation, alleging the agency had not recorded her statement properly. She also said the CBI did not collect samples from her son for a DNA test.
“I have received threats. I need protection,” she said, while also insisting on a narco-analysis.
Mr. Rawat denied the allegations, including the charge of rape, and challenged those involved to undergo DNA tests under court supervision.
He accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of reviving the controversy to target him and the Congress party ahead of State Assembly elections slated for 2027.

Condemning the treatment Ms. Dewri — who hails from Sadiya in Assam’s Tinsukia district — had received, Mr. Sarma wrote: “Yesterday (November 10, 2026), I met Jenny, a resident of Assam. In the meeting, Ms. Dewri renewed her demand for a DNA test and a fresh Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son.

She told journalists in Dehradun on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that she has appealed to Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami for justice.

She would stay in Dehradun until her demands were addressed, she said.

Ms. Dewri criticised the earlier CBI investigation, alleging the agency had not recorded her statement properly. She also said the CBI did not collect samples from her son for a DNA test.

Mr. Rawat denied the allegations, including the charge of rape, and challenged those involved to undergo DNA tests under court supervision.

articles.title: God belongs to everyone, says Akhilesh on his Ayodhya visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Claiming the BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud, the SP chief said that voters have made up their mind to bring his party to power in U.P.; he called for a voter list to be linked to Aadhaar

Dismissing the BJP’s criticism of his plans to visit Ayodhya next month, Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) emphasised that “God belongs to everyone” and slammed his critics for their alleged loot and destruction in Ayodhya.
Mr. Yadav is scheduled to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, with his family. BJP leaders triggered a political war of words by terming his visit politically motivated.

Samajwadi Party National president Akhilesh Yadav celebrates the birthday of Khajanchi, the child who was born in a bank queue during demonetisation, by presenting him with gifts and cash during a press conference at the party office in Lucknow. | Photo Credit: ANI

“God belongs to everyone. So why should we not visit these places? We will visit Kedareshwar, Mathura and Vrindavan as well. We have been visiting these places before, and we will continue to do so. Those who looted and destroyed the livelihood of common people should answer,” Mr. Yadav told journalists in Lucknow.
The SP president claimed that Uttar Pradesh voters have determined to bring his party back into power in the State.

“The farmers, youth, labourers, and traders of Uttar Pradesh want change. The public has made up its mind to form the government of the Samajwadi Party in 2027. The people of the State are ready; the end of the BJP is near. Under the BJP government, injustice, oppression, inflation, and unemployment are at their peak. The Chief Minister is unaware of the employment rate and unemployment rate,” Mr. Yadav said, urging party workers to win booths and be vigilant.

“The BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud. The BJP wanted to commit dishonesty through the [special intensive revision] SIR process, but the workers of the Samajwadi Party and the PDA guards saved their votes. It is the responsibility of all leaders and workers to keep their votes safe and strengthen the booths,” he added.

The SP chief demanded that the voter list be linked with Aadhaar cards and said that these cards should be made of metal so that fakes cannot be created. “If everyone’s Aadhaar card is biometric, then why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card? When discussions are being held about Digital India and becoming equal to the world, why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card?” he asked.

Mr. Yadav claimed that the BJP was scared of the PDA, his acronym for an alliance of minorities, Dalits, and backward class voters. “Now the fight is not 80 versus 20, but 95 versus 5. This time in the Assembly elections, the BJP will not be visible on the ground. Seeing the BJP’s defeat, the Chief Minister’s language and behaviour have changed,” he said.
Celebrating the birthday of Khajanchi, a 10-year-old boy born during demonetisation in 2016, Mr. Yadav described ‘note bandi ’ as the most corrupt decision in the world’s history.

articles.title: First phase of Musi rejuvenation to begin shortly, says Telangana CM Revath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Wednesday said the first phase of the Musi rejuvenation project would begin shortly, asserting that the river had to be cleaned up and restored rather than merely beautified. He said the government would ensure that no one suffers losses in the process and called for the cooperation of all political parties.

Speaking at the inauguration of the revived Thammidikunta Lake, he said Musi river pollution was causing hardships to people in Nalgonda district, who were paying the price for the neglect of successive governments. The lives of Hyderabad residents were closely linked to the river, he said.

Recalling the construction of Osmansagar and Himayatsagar reservoirs by the Nizam to protect Hyderabad from floods, he said the Musi riverfront had been developed nearly a century ago, but the water body had now become polluted.

Describing Hyderabad as a city of rocks and lakes, Mr. Revanth Reddy said it had 1,372 lakes, but nearly 50% had disappeared due to various reasons. Encroachments had resulted in waterlogging on roads and flooding of residential colonies during rains. He stressed the need to free lakes from encroachments as part of efforts to protect nature and establish Hyderabad as a global city.

He said Thammidikunta Lake had been expanded from 14 to 30 acres, keeping the future of coming generations in mind, even if some people suffered losses in the process. Actor Akkineni Nagarjuna had voluntarily handed over two acres of land to the government, he said, describing him as a hero in real life as well as in films.

The Chief Minister said the lake would become a new destination alongside Shilparamam and called for developing a lake economy around it. He directed police officials to ensure adequate security and suggested planting a Jammi tree on the lake premises so that lakes could become venues for Dasara celebrations and help preserve cultural traditions.

articles.title: German military to stop using Chinese-made drones, citing security concerns
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes; they will now be replaced with European products

Germany's military will no longer use Chinese-made drones, ​a defence ministry spokesperson said on Wednesday, amid mounting concern ‌among Western militaries that they could pose a ​security risk and be used to transmit ⁠sensitive information to Beijing.

Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes, ‌the spokesperson said. They will now be replaced with European products.
"To strengthen the Bundeswehr's ‌self-sufficiency and technological sovereignty, Chinese-made models will no ‌longer ⁠be used," the spokesperson said in an emailed ⁠statement.

There is no blanket ban on the use of systems from specific countries, the spokesperson said, adding the decision is based on ​individual risk assessments ‌aimed at safeguarding military security, IT and data security.
China's foreign ministry told Reuters that it opposed Germany's "discriminatory practice" targeting Chinese products.
Germany's Der Spiegel news outlet first ‌reported the change.

Local commanders had been allowed ​to purchase the drones under a 2024 strategy that included a "white list" of approved systems, ⁠including several made by China-based DJI, the world's largest drone maker, Spiegel reported.

DJI has repeatedly said its ‌drones do not pose a security risk and in May the company told US lawmakers that an independent review had found "no evidence of data transmission outside the United States".

The US last month prohibited vehicles made by China's BYD on its air base on Japan's ‌Okinawa island, and Poland in February banned Chinese-made vehicles from ​military facilities over concerns their sensors could be used to collect sensitive data.

The spokesperson said the ⁠German defence ministry had no general ban on vehicles from ⁠specific countries or manufacturers, but said sensors installed in modern vehicles are seen as potential security ‌risks, and therefore access to sensitive military sites can be restricted where necessary.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier

The Democratic Republic of Congo's worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as armed conflict hampers the response.
The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier.
It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health.
Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever.
Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years.
The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020.
The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu.
Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.
No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak.

Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

The Democratic Republic of Congo's worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as armed conflict hampers the response.

The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier.

It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health.

Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever.

Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years.

The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020.

The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu.

Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.

No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak.

Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

The email purported to come from the leader of an otherwise unknown group with an anti-woman name and contained particularly violent threats. It was signed with the same Russian name used in last week's threats against European broadcasters.
Authorities have not attributed the threats to any group or state, and no evidence has emerged linking the hoaxes to a government.

Police in Ireland also said they were aware of a “generic communication” sent to several educational institutions.

articles.title: COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels

Wars and trade disputes should not be allowed to distract the world from ​its struggle to combat global warming, the leaders of Brazil and Turkey told the COP31 climate conference ⁠on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

"A year ago, the planet left COP30 invigorated... (but) this momentum has dropped off at the start of this year. Climate change disappeared from the speeches and documents from global leadership," Brazil's President Luiz ‌Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year's conference, told the summit.
"We started talking more about weapons ‌and ⁠tariffs than the survival of future generations," he said. "The planet cannot be in the mercy of ⁠hegemonic struggles."
"Wars, crises, migration, famine and poverty increase the need for international solidarity each day," he said.
The U.S. and Israeli war on Iran this year has disrupted West Asia crude oil shipments and sent fuel prices soaring around the ​globe, triggering a scramble for reliable supplies.

Those dynamics ‌have pushed global warming down the list of urgent priorities for some governments, even as climate advocates argue they make the perfect case for a more rapid adoption of clean energy alternatives to oil.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told ​world leaders earlier in the day that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction, and that fast action was needed to ⁠avert it.

"The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction," Mr. Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters.

A UN report last month found ‌the world on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

articles.title: Navi Mumbai recognised as India’s cleanest city in latest Swachh Survekshan
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Indore, ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the winners this year
Navi Mumbai has been adjudged the cleanest city in India at a central government awards programme, while Gujarat’s Surat was second and Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh finished third.
Among cities with a population between three lakh and 10 lakh, Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain emerged as the cleanest urban centre, followed by the UT of Chandigarh and Guntur in Andhra Pradesh.
Indore, which had been ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the toppers this year.
The awards were presented by President Droupadi Murmu at an event held here.
Rewa, another city in Madhya Pradesh, emerged as the cleanest riverfront town, followed by Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) and Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) in second and third place, respectively.
In the 10 lakh-plus population category, Greater Visakhapatnam emerged as the cleanest city, followed by Jabalpur and Lucknow.
According to the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, in the Swachh Coastal Town category, Puri in Odisha was ranked first, followed by Kerala’s Alappuzha and Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri.
Rudrapur, in Uttarakhand, emerged as the cleanest Himalayan city, while Jammu secured the second position.
Last year, Indore had topped the league, followed by Surat and Navi Mumbai. Jaipur was recognised as the cleanest city in Rajasthan, while Gwalior received the distinction in Madhya Pradesh.

Swachh Survekshan is Swacch Bharat Mission-Urban’s flagship cleanliness assessment, with the goal of improving urban sanitation, hygiene, and waste management. Over 4,751 cities participated in the latest edition.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamil Nadu / government / politics / language / Delimitation / education / Governor / taxes and duties / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Bharatiya Janata Party
